Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the maple cream and let cool. Refrigerate for about 3 hours or until completely chilled.

Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a 17 x 12-inch (43 x 30 cm) baking sheet with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides. Generously butter and flour the paper and the unlined sides. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.

In another bowl, beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until the mixture triples in volume and forms a ribbon as it falls from the beaters, about 10 minutes. At low speed, drizzle in the oil.
Sift the flour mixture over the egg mixture, stirring gently with a whisk (see note). Spread the batter evenly on the prepared sheet.
Bake for about 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack.

Filling: Line a 17 x 12-inch (43 x 30 cm) baking sheet with parchment paper. Spread the tempered white chocolate in a thin layer about the same size as the sheet. Sprinkle with the maple-sugar flakes and pecans. Refrigerate for about 15 minutes or until the chocolate has set. Gently lift the sheet, breaking the chocolate into long strips.

In a bowl, whip the remaining heavy cream (1 cup/250 ml) until firm peaks form. With a whisk or a spatula, fold into the chilled maple cream. Set aside 1 ½ cups (375 ml) to frost the yule log, and keep the remaining cream to fill the inside of the cake.
Assembly: Flip the cake onto a sheet of parchment paper so it can be rolled easily.

Carefully remove the parchment paper from the cake. Trim the cake ends to straighten the edges. Spread the maple cream over the entire surface of the cake and add the raspberries. Roll the cake from the short side. Cover completely with the reserved maple cream.
Place on a serving tray. Cover with the strips of white chocolate. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400ºF (200ºC). Line an 18 x 13-inch (46 x 33 cm) baking sheet with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides. Generously butter the paper and sides of the baking sheet.
In a bowl, sift the flour and cocoa powder. Mix well and set aside.
In two bowls, separate the whites and yolks of 3 eggs. Set the egg whites aside.

In a large bowl, whisk the remaining 3 eggs, the egg yolks and 1/2 cup (105 g) of the sugar with an electric mixer until the mixture is pale, tripled in volume and falls from the beaters in a ribbon, about 5 to 7 minutes (using a stand mixer is preferable). Wash the whisk attachment.
In another bowl, whisk the reserved egg whites and salt with the electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually whisk in the remaining sugar until stiff, shiny peaks form.

Using a spatula, delicately fold the meringue into the egg yolk mixture. Fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture in three additions. Spread the mixture into an even layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the surface of the cake springs back when pressed with your fingers. Let cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes.

Run a thin blade between the side of the baking sheet and the cake. Sift the icing sugar over the entire surface of the cake and flip over onto another sheet of parchment paper. Delicately remove the top sheet of parchment paper. Cut the long sides of the cake slightly to straighten them out. Set the cake aside.
Syrup: Meanwhile, in a small pot, bring the water and sugar to a boil just until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and let cool for 10 minutes. Add the kirsch. Set aside.
Assembly: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, mix the ice cream until smooth but not melting.
Using a pastry brush, cover the cake with the syrup. Quickly spread the ice cream over the surface of the cake. Top the ice cream layer with the crushed raspberries.

Using the parchment paper, roll up the cake, starting from one of the short sides. Place the yule log on a baking sheet, seam side down. Cover and freeze for 2 hours or until the ice cream has hardened.

Swiss Meringue: In a bowl placed over a pot of simmering water, heat all of the ingredients while stirring just until the sugar and salt have dissolved and a thermometer reads 140°F (60°C). Remove the bowl from the pot. Whisk the mixture with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form (using a stand mixer is preferable).

Immediately cover the cake with the warm meringue. Using an offset spatula, create small decorative peaks in the meringue. Using a small kitchen torch, caramelize the surface of the meringue (see note).
Decorate the yule log with fresh raspberries, chocolate shavings (see note), mint leaves or marzipan figurines. Sprinkle lightly with icing sugar. Serve immediately.

Almond Crème Anglaise: In a pot over low heat, toast the almonds, stirring constantly, until they are fragrant and starting to brown. Pour in the milk and cream. Bring to a boil. Remove from the heat. Cover and infuse for 10 minutes.
Strain the milk mixture through a sieve placed over a bowl. Compost the almonds.
In the same pot off the heat, whisk together the egg yolks and sugar for 1 minute or until pale and smooth. Pour in the milk mixture while whisking constantly.

Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon and scraping the bottom and sides of the pot, until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon, about 10 minutes. Transfer into a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate for 3 hours or until completely chilled.

Cherry Filling: Meanwhile, in a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar, lemon juice, water and cornstarch. Add the cherries. Bring to a boil while stirring with a wooden spoon. Simmer for 1 minute. Transfer into a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 2 hours.
Meringue: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper, letting it hang over two sides.
In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch, vinegar and vanilla until smooth.

In another bowl, whisk the egg whites with an electric mixer until frothy. With the machine running, gradually add the sugar until stiff peaks form. Gently whisk in the cornstarch mixture. Spread the meringue out on the baking sheet in an even layer. Using an offset spatula, smooth out the surface of the meringue. Sprinkle with the almonds.
Bake for 25 minutes or until the meringue is slightly golden. Let cool completely on the baking sheet, about 1 hour (see note).
Assembly: Run a thin blade between the meringue and the baking sheet. Gently turn the meringue out onto a clean dishcloth. Remove the parchment paper.
In a bowl, whisk the 35% cream, icing sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Set aside ½ cup (125 ml) of the whipped cream in a small bowl.
Using an offset spatula, spread the remaining whipped cream over the meringue.
Set aside 10 cherries from the cherry filling in another small bowl. Using a spoon, spread the remaining cherry mixture over the whipped cream.
Using the dishcloth, roll up the meringue, starting from one of the long sides. Do not worry if the meringue cracks. Place the rolled meringue on a serving dish.

When ready to serve, sprinkle the yule log with icing sugar. Spread the reserved whipped cream along the top of the log. Garnish with the reserved cherries. Serve immediately with the almond crème anglaise (see note).
White Chocolate and Vanilla Whipped Cream: Place the white chocolate in a bowl.
In a small pot, bring the cream and vanilla to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Let sit for 2 minutes without stirring. Whisk until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for 8 hours.
Cranberry Filling: Meanwhile, in a bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.

In a food processor, finely chop the cranberries. Place in a pot with the sugar and lemon juice. Bring to a boil. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the liquid has evaporated. Remove from the heat.
Add the gelatin and mix until dissolved. Transfer into a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled.
Dark Chocolate Bark (optional): Meanwhile, line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Using a small offset spatula, spread the melted dark chocolate over the baking sheet into a thin layer about 1/8 inch (2 to 3 mm) thick. Refrigerate until the chocolate has set.
Detach the chocolate from the parchment paper and break into pieces. Sprinkle with the cocoa powder. Refrigerate.

Chocolate Genoise: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line an 18 x 13-inch (46 x 33 cm) baking sheet with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over the two short sides. Butter the paper and sides of the baking sheet.
In a bowl, combine the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt.

In another bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar with an electric mixer until the mixture has tripled in volume and falls from the beaters in a ribbon, about 10 minutes. Sift the dry ingredients over the egg mixture, alternating with the oil, and fold in using a whisk. Spread the batter out evenly on the baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack, about 1 hour.

Assembly: Use the parchment paper to lift the cake from the baking sheet. Cut all four sides of the cake slightly to straighten them out. Cut the cake lengthwise into 3 strips each about 16 x 4 inches (40 x 10 cm). Peel the parchment paper off each strip.

Working with one of the strips (this will be the last strip to add when assembling the cake), insert a bread knife at a 45-degree angle into one of the short ends and remove a 1-inch (2.5 cm) band of cake, making this end of the strip thinner. Set aside.
Whisk the white chocolate cream until semi-stiff peaks form using an electric mixer (do not over whisk or the cream will turn into butter).
Spread ¾ cup (180 ml) of the white chocolate cream over each strip of cake.
Spread the cranberry filling down the centre of each strip, leaving a ½-inch (1 cm) border all the way around.

Roll up one strip of cake. Gently roll a second strip around the first. Place the yule log vertically on a serving plate. Roll the last strip around the others, finishing with the thinned-out edge. Don’t worry if the cake cracks slightly or doesn’t fully close. Using an offset spatula, completely cover the cake with ¾ cup (180 ml) of the white chocolate cream. This will help cover any cake crumbs. Refrigerate for 1 hour.

Using an offset spatula, completely cover the cake with the remaining white chocolate cream. Decorate with the chocolate bark, cranberries and rosemary sprigs. The cake will keep for about 3 days, covered, in the refrigerator. Let sit out at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving. Slice and serve with the remaining chocolate bark, if desired.
Mascarpone Crème Légère: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.

In a small pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar, flour and cornstarch. Add the eggs and mix well. Add the milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pot. Simmer for 30 seconds. Remove from the heat.

Add the gelatin mixture and stir until dissolved. Strain the pastry cream through a sieve to remove any lumps, as needed. Pour into a bowl and cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool. Refrigerate for 2 hours or until completely chilled.
Mix the pastry cream with a spatula until creamy and smooth.

In a bowl, whisk the whipping cream and mascarpone with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Whisk one-third of the whipped cream mixture into the chilled pastry cream until smooth. Using the whisk or a spatula, gently fold in the remaining whipped cream. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Genoise: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line an 18 x 13-inch (46 x 33 cm) baking sheet with a strip of parchment paper, letting it hang over the two sides. Generously butter the paper and the sides of the baking sheet that are not lined with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the flour and cornstarch.

In another bowl, whisk the eggs, sugar, vanilla and salt with an electric mixer until the mixture has tripled in volume and falls from the beaters in a ribbon, about 10 minutes. With the machine running on low speed, gradually add the oil. Sift the flour and cornstarch mixture over the egg mixture and gently fold in using a whisk. Spread the batter out evenly on the baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Let cool completely on a wire rack, about 15 minutes.
Assembly: Use the parchment paper to lift the cake from the baking sheet. Cut all four sides of the cake slightly to straighten them out. Using a pastry brush, soak the cake with the coffee.
Set aside ½ cup (125 ml) of the mascarpone cream to cover the yule log. Spread the remaining cream over the entire surface of the cake. Sprinkle with the cocoa powder.

Starting at one of the short ends, use the parchment paper to help roll up the cake. Discard the parchment paper. Don’t worry if the cake cracks slightly. Place the yule log, seam-side down, on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Cover the outside of the log with the reserved mascarpone cream. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface and smooth out the log with your hand (see note). Freeze for 8 hours or overnight.
Dark Chocolate Bark: Meanwhile, line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Using a small offset spatula, spread the melted dark chocolate over the baking sheet into a thin layer about 1/8 inch (2 to 3 mm) thick. Refrigerate until the chocolate has set.
Detach the chocolate from the parchment paper and break into pieces. Sprinkle with the cocoa powder. Refrigerate until ready to decorate the yule log.
Cocoa Mirror Glaze: In a small bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the water. Let bloom for 5 minutes.
In a small pot, bring the remaining water to a boil with the sugar and cream. Whisk until the sugar has completely dissolved. Remove from the heat.

Add the cocoa powder to the pot. Add the gelatin mixture and stir until dissolved. Place a sieve over a measuring cup with a spout (this will make it easier to pour the mirror glaze over the cake). Strain the mirror glaze through the sieve. Let cool until a thermometer reads 95°F (35°C), about 50 minutes (see note). Once the mirror glazed has reached the desired temperature, mix with a spoon until as smooth and runny as possible.
Remove the plastic wrap from the yule log. Using a knife, cut away the ends of the yule log to straighten them out, as needed.

Place a wire rack over a baking sheet. Place the frozen yule log on the rack. Evenly drizzle the mirror glaze over the yule log, making sure to cover it completely. Let set for a few minutes. Using two large spatulas, carefully transfer the yule log to a serving plate.

Decorate the sides of the yule log with the chocolate bark. Let the cake defrost completely in the refrigerator before serving, about 8 hours or overnight. The yule log will keep for 3 days in the refrigerator.
White Chocolate Whipped Cream: Place the white chocolate in a bowl.
In a small pot, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and let sit for 2 minutes without stirring. Whisk until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for 8 hours.
Milk Chocolate Whipped Cream: Place the milk chocolate in a bowl.
In a small pot, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and let sit for 2 minutes without stirring. Whisk until smooth. Cover and refrigerate for 8 hours.
Dark Chocolate Ganache: Place the dark chocolate in a bowl.

In a small pot, bring the cream and corn syrup to a boil. Pour over the chocolate and let sit for 2 minutes without stirring. Stir with a spatula until smooth. Add the butter and stir until it has melted. Let cool at room temperature until thickened but still spreadable, about 2 hours.

Chocolate Cake: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a 17 x 12-inch (43 x 30 cm) baking sheet with parchment paper letting it hang over two sides. Generously butter and flour the parchment paper and the uncovered sides of the baking sheet.
In a bowl, combine the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
In another bowl, whisk the egg whites with an electric mixture until soft peaks form. Gradually add ½ cup (105 g) of the sugar and whisk until firm peaks form. Set aside.

In a third bowl, cream the butter and ½ cup (105 g) of the sugar with an electric mixer. Add the egg yolks and the vanilla. With the machine running on low speed, add the dry ingredients alternating with the milk. Gently fold in the meringue using a spatula. Spread the batter out evenly in the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out clean. Let cool completely in the baking sheet, about 1 hour.
Cocoa Crumble: Line another baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients until just moistened. Press together with your hands and let fall onto the prepared baking sheet in varying sized clumps.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring halfway through, or until cooked. Let cool completely.

Assembly: Remove the cake with the parchment paper from the baking sheet. Cut the long edges of the cake slightly to straighten them out. Spread the dark chocolate ganache over the entire surface of the cake.

Using an electric mixer, whip the white chocolate whipped cream until firm peaks form but is still spreadable (do not over whisk or the cream will turn into butter). Transfer ¼ cup (60 ml) of the cream into a pastry bag fitted with a plain tip. Spread the remaining white chocolate whipped cream over the dark chocolate ganache.
Starting at one of the short sides, roll up the cake. Don’t worry if the cake starts to crack. Place on a serving plate.
Using an electric mixer, whip the milk chocolate whipped cream until firm peaks form but is still spreadable. Transfer ¼ cup (60 ml) of the cream into a pastry bag fitted with a plain tip.

Cover the entire surface of the Yule log with the milk chocolate whipped cream (you can choose to either cover the ends of the cake or not). Garnish the top of the cake with dots of white chocolate and milk chocolate whipped cream. Sprinkle with 1/3 cup (75 ml) of the cocoa crumble and top with dark chocolate tuile cookies, if desired. Refrigerate until ready to serve. Let sit out at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving. Cut into slices and serve with the remaining crumble, if desired.

Candied Clementines: Place the clementines in a saucepan just large enough to hold them. Cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Drain and repeat 3 more times. This blanching will make them less bitter.

In the same saucepan, bring the water and sugar to a boil. Add the clementines and simmer gently for about 90 minutes (see note). Let cool. Refrigerate overnight in the syrup. The next day, drain and cut a thin slice off each end. Set aside.
Ganache: Lightly oil a small loaf pan (about 9 x 19 cm or 3 1/2 x 7 1/2 inches) and line it with plastic wrap.
Place the chocolate in a bowl. Set aside.
In the microwave oven or in a saucepan on the stove, bring the cream and honey to a boil. Pour over the chocolate. Let the chocolate melt for 5 minutes without stirring.
Whisk the mixture until smooth. Add the butter and vanilla and whisk until the butter has melted.

Pour a quarter of the ganache into the loaf pan. Freeze until firm, about 15 minutes. Arrange the clementines end to end in the middle of the loaf pan; the cut ends should be touching. Fill the pan with the remaining ganache, completely covering the clementines.
Refrigerate for 24 hours.
To serve, umould the ingot and cut it into slices with a sharp knife. To make cutting easier, dip the knife in boiling water, then dry it with a paper towel.
Sauce: In a small saucepan, dissolve the cornstarch in the broth. Add the remaining ingredients and bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Set aside.
Stir-Fry: In a bowl of boiling water, soak the vermicelli until tender. Drain and rinse under cold running water. Drain well and set aside.
In a wok or large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the tofu and carrots in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the peppers and cook for another 2 minutes.
Add the sauce and the remaining ingredients except for the green onions. Continue cooking, stirring frequently, until the vegetables are tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large serving bowl, place the noodles in one half of the dish and pour the stir-fry onto the other half. Sprinkle with the green onions. Serve immediately.
In a large pot, place shank and bones. Cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Simmer for about 10 minutes to remove impurities. Drain and discard broth. Clean the pot.

Rinse shank and marrowbones under cold water, rubbing to clean them thoroughly. Return to pot. Add onion, garlic, fish sauce, and peppercorns. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Simmer gently, covered, for about 4 hours or until meat falls off the bone. Skim, if needed.

Reserve meat and marrowbones in a bowl. Trim fat from the meat and remove the bone from the shank. Strain broth through a sieve and return to pot. Season with salt. Add meat, marrowbones, corn, chayote, and Chinese cabbage. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 15 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Add bok choy 1 minute before the end of cooking.
Place bulalu in the centre of the table. Ladle into bowls. Serve with jasmine rice, vinegar, and sambal oelek. Better eaten with a spoon and a fork.

In a glass dish or large sealable plastic bag, combine the chili paste, sesame oil, soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame seeds, ginger and garlic. Add the onion and meat and stir gently. Cover the dish or seal the bag and let marinate for 2 hours in the refrigerator.

Preheat a cast iron grill pan until very hot. Oil the pan. Grill a third of the meat and onion at a time until marked on both sides. Add oil, if needed. Garnish with the green onions and serve wrapped in lettuce leaves.
Delicious with our Gochujang Sauce.

In a large bowl, using a wooden spoon, or in a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook, combine the dry ingredients. Add the water and oil. Mix until the dough comes together into a soft ball. Knead the dough for 5 minutes on a work surface with your hands, or in the stand mixer, until smooth.

Form the dough into a ball and place in a clean, lightly oiled bowl, turning to coat it in the oil. Cover with a damp dishcloth and let rise in a warm, humid spot for 2 hours or until doubled in volume.

On a lightly floured work surface, divide the dough into 12 equal pieces. Form each piece into a ball using the palm of your hand. Using a rolling pin, roll each ball into an oval disc about 6 inches (15 cm) long. Using a pastry brush, cover the surface of the dough with a little bit of oil.

Fold each oval in half to form half-moons. Place each half-moon on a small piece of parchment paper and spread out on a baking sheet. Cover with plastic wrap. Let rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

Place a flat metal or bamboo steaming basket in the bottom of a large pot. Add enough water to just reach the bottom of the steamer and bring to a boil. Place a few buns at a time (still on the parchment paper) in the steamer. Make sure the buns are evenly spaced out so that they do not touch and stick together. Cover and steam for 12 minutes, making sure there is always water in the pot.

Pork Belly: In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, sugar and five-spice powder. Transfer to an airtight container. Add the pork belly to the container and mix to coat well in the marinade. Cover and marinate for 8 hours or overnight in the refrigerator, turning the meat over a few times, if possible. Drain the meat and discard the marinade.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a dry, non-stick ovenproof pot, cook the green onions until charred, about 3 to 5 minutes. Add the broth and pork. Bring to a boil. Cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours or until the pork is starting to fall apart, turning the pork over halfway through cooking. Remove the pork from the cooking liquid and let cool on a plate. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Strain the cooking liquid through a sieve. Compost the green onions. Set the cooking liquid aside.
On a work surface, cut the chilled pork into 12 slices.

In a large non-stick skillet, lay out the pork slices. Cover with the reserved cooking liquid. Bring to a boil and let reduce, spooning the sauce over the meat, until the pork is nicely glazed and there is no cooking liquid left in the skillet, about 10 minutes.
Assembly: Cover the inside of the steamed buns with hoisin sauce. Fill with a slice of pork, cucumbers, green onions, cilantro and sliced chili pepper, if desired.

Sautéed Mushrooms: In a large skillet, brown the onion and mushrooms in the butter. Deglaze with the Worcestershire and soy sauces and continue cooking for 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside and keep warm.
Cheese Sauce: In a bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in the milk. Set aside.

In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter with the flour, whisking continuously. Cook for 1 minute. Add the milk mixture and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Add the cheeses and stir until melted. Cover, set aside and keep warm.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the meats. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into 8 large, thin patties (see note).
Grill the patties for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, or until they are cooked through. Toast the buns.
For each burger, spread cheese sauce on the bottom half of the bun, then layer with a patty, some mushrooms, a second patty, lettuce, bacon and pickles. Close with the top half of the bun.

In a large bowl, combine the oatmeal, breadcrumbs, grated cheese, eggs, sesame and sunflower seeds, parsley, pepper, paprika, and vegetable flakes. Add the water and mix well until smooth. Leave to rest for 15 minutes.
Shape into 8 patties. Careful, it is a bit sticky!
Heat a little vegetable oil in a large heavy skillet and fry the patties until golden brown.
Pour enough water to cover halfway up the patties, add the tamari and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning them a few times in the cooking juices.
When the liquid is completely reduced, serve immediately.
Brush the meatloaf slice with olive oil.

In a large ridged skillet or on the grill, grill the meatloaf slice on one side for about 2 minutes. Flip the slice, sprinkle with the cheese, and cook for about 2 minutes or until the cheese has melted. Toast the bun.
Spread the mayonnaise in the bun. Place the meat on the bottom bread. Top with the tomato, bacon, and lettuce. Close and garnish with the pickle on a toothpick.
Toppings: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

Grill the onions for 8 minutes, the eggplant slices for 6 minutes and the bacon for 4 minutes, turning halfway through cooking, or until the vegetables are tender-crisp and the bacon is cooked through. Grill the buns, if desired. Set aside and keep warm.
Burgers: Using lightly oiled hands or a hamburger press, shape the meat into 6 large patties. Place on an oiled plate and season with salt and pepper.
Grill the patties for 3 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through.
Spread the inside of the buns with the chipotle cheese sauce. Layer with the patties, grilled vegetables, bacon and lettuce.

Chili: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the onion, bell pepper and garlic in the oil. Add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine. Cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes or until the mixture is almost dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Burgers: Generously heap the chili on the bottom half of each bun. Top with cheese, jalapeno and sour cream. Delicious with a green salad.
Chicken Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a food processor, finely chop the green onion. Add the chicken and finely chop. Season with salt and pepper.
With your hands, shape the chicken mixture into 6 large patties. Place on an oiled plate.
Grill the patties for 4 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Toast the hamburger buns, if desired.
Assembly: Spread the inside of the hamburger buns with caper-mayonnaise sauce. Place the lettuce and patties on the bottom of each bun. Top with the bacon and tomato slices. Close with the bun tops.
Salmon Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a food processor, coarsely chop the salmon. Place in a bowl. Add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine. Salt and pepper.
With your hands, shape the fish mixture into 6 large patties. Place them on a large, oiled plated.
Grill the patties for 2 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Toast the hamburger buns, if desired.
Assembly: Spread the insides of the buns with chermoula. Place the patties on them and top with mayonnaise and the radish and cucumber pickles. Close the burgers.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the hoisin and sriracha. Set aside.
In another bowl, mix the meat and the dipping sauce. Working with your hands, form the meat into 4 patties. Place on an oiled plate. Lightly oil the buns and zucchinis.
Grill the patties for 3 minutes per side or until fully cooked. Grill the zucchinis for 2 minutes per side, then grill the buns until toasted.

Spread the mayonnaise on the buns, as desired. Place lettuce on each of the bottom buns, then add the patties. Glaze with the sauce. Cover with a layer of zucchini and more sauce. Sprinkle with the grated carrot and close with the top buns.
Coleslaw: On a work surface, trim off both ends of the orange. Cut off the peel down to the flesh, then slide the knife between each membrane to remove the segments.
In a bowl, combine the orange segments and the remaining ingredients. Set aside
Trout: In a large bowl or sealable plastic bag, combine the cornmeal, flour, salt and cayenne pepper. Add the trout pieces and coat well. Shake to remove any excess.

In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown half of the fish at a time in the oil until cooked through, about 2 to 3 minutes on each side, depending on the thickness. Add more oil, if needed. Keep warm.
Assembly: In the same skillet, grill the buns. Spread with mayonnaise, then layer with the coleslaw, trout, cucumber and cilantro. Serve the burgers with lime wedges.

Mushrooms: In a large skillet, brown the mushrooms in the butter. Add the shallots and sauté until golden brown. Season with salt and pepper. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Deglaze with the broth, sauce, and vinegar. Bring to a boil and reduce until almost dry, about 2 minutes. Remove the thyme and adjust the seasoning. Keep warm.

Cheese Sauce: In a saucepan, off the heat, toss the cheese with the cornstarch. Add the milk and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring with a whisk until the cheese has melted, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Cover and set aside.
Hamburgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high. Oil the grate.
With your hands or a hamburger press, form eight large and thin patties with about 75 ml (1/3 cup) of meat each.
Grill the patties for 2 to 3 minutes per side or until cooked through. Season with salt and pepper.

Toast the buns. Generously spread the warm cheese sauce on the bottom buns. Add the patties. Top with mushrooms. Cover with a second patty and mushrooms. Top with cheese sauce, to taste, and arugula. Cover to close the burgers.
Buffalo Sauce: In a small pot, combine all of the ingredients. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the sauce has reduced by half. Set aside.
Blue Cheese Sauce: In a small bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. The sauce will keep for 3 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator (see note).

Marinated Onion (optional): In a small glass bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Cover with plastic wrap. Cook in the microwave oven for 1 minute. Let marinate at room temperature while you prepare the remaining ingredients.
Fried Chicken: In a shallow dish, place the flour. In a second shallow dish, lightly beat the eggs. In a third dish, combine the crushed cereal with the spices and salt.

Working one piece at a time, dredge the chicken in the flour, shaking off any excess. Dip into the beaten eggs, letting some of the excess drip off. Press lightly into the cereal mixture to coat well. Place on a plate. Using a pastry brush, cover the chicken with the oil on both sides.

Place the chicken in the basket of an air fryer, evenly spaced out. Cook for 15 minutes at 375°F (190°C). Flip the chicken over and continue to cook for 10 minutes or until cooked through and nicely browned.

Burgers: Spread the blue cheese sauce over the inside of the warmed hamburger buns. Top the bun bottoms with the chicken. Using a pastry brush, coat the chicken with the Buffalo sauce. Garnish with lettuce and marinated onions. Sprinkle with blue cheese. Close with the bun tops.
In a bowl, beat all the cheddar and lime butter ingredients until the lime juice is well incorporated. Place on a square of aluminum foil and shape a log the size of a toonie. Refrigerate.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
When the butter is hard, cut it into four slices.
Form four patties and make a well in the centre with your thumb. Place a slice of butter.
Carefully close the patties over the butter so that when it melts, it won’t run out of the patties. Season with salt and pepper.
Grill the patties for 5 to 6 minutes per side until the meat is cooked. Do not press the patties during cooking. Let the patties rest for 1 to 2 minutes before serving.
Toast the buns. Assemble the burgers with the toppings of your choice.
Harissa Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season lightly with salt. Refrigerate.
Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In another bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season generously with pepper. With your hands, shape the meat mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties. Set aside.
Burgers: Place the zucchini and onion slices on a large plate. Drizzle with the oil. Season with salt and pepper.

Grill the patties and onions for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until the meat is cooked through and the onion is tender. Keep warm. Separate the onion slices into rings. Grill the zucchini slices for 2 minutes on each side. Grill the hamburger buns.
Spread the harissa mayonnaise over the inside of the buns. Top the bun bottoms with the grilled zucchini and patties. Garnish with the mint leaves and onion rings. Close with the bun tops.
Greek Yogurt Sauce: In a small bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.

Patties: In a small pot off the heat, combine the lime juice with the brown sugar, ketchup, oil and spices. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 2 minutes while stirring until the sauce thickens slightly. Let cool.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

In a bowl, combine the ground pork and bacon. Season with salt and pepper. With your hands, shape the meat mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Using a pastry brush, cover the patties with the cooled sauce on both sides.
Burgers: Place the onion slices on a plate. Drizzle with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add the pineapple slices to the plate.

Grill the patties and onion slices for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until the meat is cooked through and the onion is tender. Keep warm. Separate the onion into rings. Grill the pineapple slices for 1 minute on each side. Grill the buns.
Spread the yogurt sauce over the inside of the buns. Place the lettuce over the bun bottoms. Top with the patties, onion and pineapple. Close with the bun tops.
Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a small food processor, finely chop the cheese curds. Transfer to a large bowl. Finely chop the bacon in the food processor and add to the bowl of cheese.
Add the ground beef to the bowl. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Mix well. With your hands, shape the meat mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties.

Burgers: Grill the patties for 4 minutes. Flip the patties over. Using a pastry brush, cover the patties with the ketchup. Continue to cook for 4 to 5 minutes or until the meat is cooked through. Grill the hamburger buns.
Spread the bun bottoms with mayonnaise and top with the patties. Garnish with the chips and lettuce. Close with the bun tops.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.
Lightly oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the meat, paprika, mustard and egg. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into 4 patties.
Lightly oil the vegetables. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook the patties on the grill for 4 to 5 minutes per side or until the meat is thoroughly cooked. Cook the vegetables on the grill for 2 to 3 minutes per side or until just tender. Toast the bread.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the sour cream and cilantro. Season with salt and pepper.
Generously spread sour cream and Baba Ghanoush on the bread. Add a meat patty.
Garnish with slices of grilled eggplant and zucchini.

Barbecue Sauce: In a saucepan over medium-high heat, bring the maple syrup, shallot and garlic to a boil. Simmer for about 3 minutes. Add the remaining ingredients and return to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for about 5 minutes or until the sauce thickens. Set aside.

Grilled Chicken: In a bowl, combine the chicken with the oil and 1/2 cup of the barbecue sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Keep aside the remaining barbeque sauce.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the chicken for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, or until the meat is cooked through. Slice the chicken thinly or chop coarsely. Keep warm. Toast the buns.

Spread mayonnaise on the inside of the buns. Divide the chicken evenly and place on the bottom halves of the buns. Drizzle with the reserved barbecue sauce. Garnish with the avocado and lettuce. Cover with the top halves of the buns. Serve with Coleslaw.
Raita: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate.
Chicken Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine all theingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into 4 rectangular patties the same size as the buns and oil lightly.
Grill the chicken patties for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, or until the meat is cooked through. Toast the buns.
Burgers: Spread the raita inside the buns. Place the patties on the bottom halves of the buns and garnish with the cheese and cucumber slices. Cover with the tops of the buns.
Sauce: In a bowl, combine the sour cream and curry powder. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Burgers: In a large nonstick skillet, brown the zucchini slices on each side in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.
In the same skillet, brown the buns on each side. Spread the sauce inside the buns. Garnish with the salmon patties, zucchini, tomatoes and spinach. Serve immediately.
Caramelized onions: In a skillet over medium heat, brown the onions in the oil for about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Deglaze with the vinegar. Set aside.

Avocado Relish: In a bowl, mash the avocado with a fork. Stir in the lemon juice, oil, mustard and green onion. Season with salt and pepper. Place a sheet of plastic wrap directly on the avocado relish and refrigerate while cooking the tuna patties.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

In a bowl, combine the tuna, 1/4 cup of the avocado relish and hot sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into 4 patties and carefully place them on the grill. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes on each side. Toast the buns.

Generously spread the remaining avocado relish on the inside of the buns. Place the tuna patties on the bottom halves of the buns and garnish with the caramelized onions and lettuce leaves. Cover with the tops of the buns.
Breaded Tofu: In a bowl, combine 125 ml (½ cup) of the flour with the water and spices. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Sprinkle the remaining flour (60 ml / ¼ cup) on the tofu slices and shake to remove any excess. Coat the tofu in the spicy batter. Set aside.
In a large non-stick skillet, heat the oil. Brown the tofu slices for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or until crisp. Add oil, if needed. Drain on paper towel.
Hamburgers: In the same skillet or in a hot oven, brown the cut side of the buns.
Spread the inside of the buns with mayonnaise and mustard. Layer with a slice of cheese and tofu. Garnish with the tomato, lettuce, and avocado slices. Cover with the top buns.

Pickled Cabbage: In a large bowl, massage the cabbage and salt with your hands to extract some water from the cabbage, for about 2 minutes. Add the dill and vinegar. Mix well. Let marinate while you prepare the burgers.
Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In another bowl, combine the meat and steak spice. With your hands, shape the meat mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties.
Burgers: Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until the meat is cooked through. Grill the hamburger buns.
Spread the mustard over the inside of the buns. Top the bun bottoms with the sliced pickles and patties. Divide the pickled cabbage among the burgers. Close with the bun tops.
Tomato and Basil Topping: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season generously with salt and pepper. Let marinate while you prepare the burgers.
Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In another bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season generously with pepper. With your hands, shape the meat mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties.
Burgers: Grill the patties for 4 minutes. Flip the patties over and top with the Parmesan. Continue to cook for 4 to 5 minutes or until the meat is cooked through. Grill the hamburger buns.
Divide the watercress among the bun bottoms. Top with the patties. Garnish with the tomato and basil topping. Close with the bun tops.
Roasted Vegetables: With one rack in the middle position and a second rack in the lowest position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line two baking sheets with silicone mats or parchment paper
Remove the stems from the mushrooms. With a spoon, remove the black part underneath the cap of the mushroom (the lamellae or gills) and reserve them for a vegetable broth or compost them.

Spread the vegetables out on the baking sheets. Toss with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 30 minutes or until tender and golden. Remove the baking sheets from the oven and drizzle the lemon juice over the vegetables.

Patties: Meanwhile, in a food processor, finely chop the beets and onion with the hoisin, steak spice and harissa. Add the chickpeas, oats and chickpea flour. Pulse for a few seconds at a time until the mixture forms a rough paste. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. With your hands, form the mixture into 6 patties.
In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, brown half of the patties at a time in the oil until browned on both sides and firm.
Assembly: In the same skillet, toast the inside of the burger buns. Spread generously with mayonnaise. Layer with the patties, roasted vegetables, beets and lettuce.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium.
In a bowl with your hands, combine the sausage meat, ground veal and garlic. Lightly season with salt. Shape into thin patties. Sprinkle with sesame seeds on both sides.
Meanwhile, grill the onions. Set aside.
Set the burners to high. Grill the patties for about 3 minutes per side or until they are thoroughly cooked. Toast the buns.
Generously spread hummus onto the bottom portion of the each bun.
Layer with a patty, grilled onions, Dijon mustard, a tomato slice, and lettuce.
Shape four 4-cm (1 ½-inch) thick patties with the ground meat. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a skillet, brown the buns on both sides in the butter. Keep warm.
In the same skillet, brown the mushrooms in half the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside in a warm bowl.

In the same skillet, grill the patties in the remaining olive oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side or until cooked through. Add oil, if needed. Season with salt and pepper. Before the end of cooking, top with the cheese and let melt.

Assembly: Spread the aioli on the buns. Top the bottom bun halves with the lettuce and add the patties. Add the mushrooms and basil. Sprinkle with a few drops of truffle oil. Cover with the top bun halves.
Quick Pickled Vegetables: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt. Let marinate while you prepare the burgers, stirring a few times. Drain before serving.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In another bowl, combine the ground beef with the brown sugar and soy sauce. Season with salt and pepper. With your hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties.
Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Grill the buns. Keep warm.

In a large skillet over medium-high, heat the oil. Carefully crack the eggs into the skillet and cook, on one side only, for 2 to 3 minutes or until the whites are set and the edges are golden. Season with salt. Sprinkle with gochugaru.
Spread the mayonnaise over the inside of the buns. Top the bottom buns with the patties, kimchi, pickled vegetables, cilantro leaves and eggs. Close with the bun tops.

Burgers: Place the bulgur in a bowl and cover with the boiling water. Let soak for 30 minutes. Strain through a sieve and return to the bowl. Add the lamb, egg and spices. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper. Shape 2 large patties the same size as the pita bread. Transfer to a plate. Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Tomato, Cucumber and Yogurt Salad: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Assembly: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the patties for 8 minutes on each side, turning carefully. Toast the pitas.
Spread the hummus on the pitas. Place each patty on a pita. Top with the tomato salad. Top with a second pita. Cut each sandwich into quarters.
Roasted Onion: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
On the baking sheet, toss the onion wedges with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 30 minutes or until the onion is tender and golden.
Arugula Pesto: Meanwhile, in a small food processor, purée all of the ingredients until fairly smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Patties: In a bowl, combine the ground lamb, breadcrumbs, sumac and egg. Season with salt and pepper. Using your hands, form the mixture into 4 patties.
In a large skillet over medium heat, cook the patties in the oil for 4 to 5 minutes on each side.
Burgers: Cover the bun bottoms with the sour cream. Top with the patties, roast onions, arugula and pesto. Close with the bun tops.

Coleslaw: In a large bowl, combine the vinegar, mustard, maple syrup, and oil. Add the apple and toss to coat thoroughly (to prevent browning). Add the cabbage and toss well. Season with salt and pepper. Let rest for 15 minutes.
Burgers: Spread the barbecued pulled pork on the bottom half of a hamburger bun and garnish with the coleslaw. Top with the other half of the bun and serve immediately.
Mango Sauce: In a personal blender or small food processor, purée all of the ingredients until smooth. Set aside (see note).
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the onion, vinegar and sugar. Let marinate while you prepare the burgers, stirring a few times. Drain.
In a second bowl, using your hands, combine the beef and garam masala. Season generously with salt and pepper. Shape into 4 patties. Place on a plate and coat with oil.
Grill the patties for 4 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Set aside on another plate. Grill the hamburger buns.
Cover the bun bottoms with the yogurt. Top with the lettuce, mint and burger patties. Garnish with the mango sauce and marinated onions. Close with the bun tops.
Patties: In a bowl, combine the meat, egg, onion jam and coriander. Season with salt and pepper. With your hands, form the mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate and brush with oil. Refrigerate.
Toppings: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine the red cabbage and vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Let sit for 10 minutes. Drain.
Meanwhile, grill the patties for 4 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Place the cheese on the patties and cook until it’s starting to melt. Grill the inside of the hamburger buns.
Spread mustard and mayonnaise over the inside of the buns. Divide the arugula and patties among the bun bottoms. Top with the onion jam and cabbage. Close with a bun top.
Beef Patties: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into 4 patties. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate. Preheat the deep fryer to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with paper towels.
Grill the patties for about 4 minutes on each side, or until the meat is well done. Toast the buns.
Fries: Meanwhile, fry the potatoes for 3 to 4 minutes or until golden brown. Drain on the paper towels. Season with salt.
Burgers: Spread ketchup on the inside of the toasted buns. Place the patties on the bottom halves of the buns and garnish with banana pepper slices and fries. Cover with the top halves of the buns.
Marinade: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Set aside.

Burgers: In another bowl, combine the meat and black bean paste. Shape into 10 patties the same diameter as the buns. Place the patties in a glass baking dish. Brush with marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.
Grill the patties until well done, about 3 minutes per side. Toast the buns.
Place the patties on the buns and top with kimchee.

Pepper Confit: In a large saucepan over high heat, sauté the peppers, onion and garlic in the oil until the peppers are tender and golden. Add the ketchup and harissa. Salt and pepper. Continue cooking for about 2 minutes. Set aside.
Jalapeño Cream Cheese: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Set aside.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
With your hands or a burger press, shape the meat into 4 large patties.
Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Salt and pepper. Quickly toast the buns on the grill.
Spread the inside of the buns with the cream cheese mixture. Place a patty on the bottom half of each bun. Top with the pepper confit and lettuce. Close up the sandwiches.
Portobello Patties: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

Remove and compost the mushroom stems. Place the mushroom caps on the baking sheet. Using a pastry brush, cover the mushrooms with the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 25 minutes or just until tender. Let cool.

In a bowl, combine both cheeses with the egg yolk and flour. Divide the cheese mixture among 4 of the mushrooms, pressing well to adhere. Sandwich together with another portobello to form into 4 patties.
Coating: Preheat the oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (180°C). Line half of a baking sheet with paper towels.
In a shallow bowl, place the flour. Season with salt and pepper. In a second shallow bowl, lightly beat the eggs and milk. In a third shallow bowl, place the breadcrumbs.

Coat each portobello patty in the flour, shaking off any excess. Dip into the egg mixture, letting some of the excess drip off. Press into the breadcrumbs. Dip a second time in the egg mixture and coat again in the breadcrumbs. Place on the empty side of the baking sheet.
Fry half of the coated mushroom patties at a time for 3 to 4 minutes or until golden. Drain on the paper towels.
Sauce: Meanwhile, in a bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients.
Assembly: Spread the sauce over the insides of the toasted buns. Place one portobello patty over each bun bottom. Top with the tomato slices and lettuce. Close with the bun tops. Serve immediately.
Patties: In a food processor, chop the shrimp. Pulse a few seconds at a time so they aren't chopped too finely. Transfer to a large bowl.

Add the egg, breadcrumbs, lemon juice and hot sauce. Season with salt and mix well. With lightly oiled hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Remoulade: Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.

Burgers: Using a brush, brush the patties with the oil. Place the patties in the air fryer basket lined with parchment paper. Cook at 200 °C (400 °F) for 8 minutes (see note). Turn the patties over and continue cooking for 6 minutes, until cooked through and golden brown.
Spread the inside of the buns with mayonnaise. Top the bottom halves of the buns with a shrimp patty and rémoulade. Add the lettuce leaves and close the burgers.
Cocktail Sauce: In a small bowl, combine the mayonnaise and ketchup. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Burgers: In a bowl, combine the zucchini ribbons, lime juice and salt. Let marinate until ready to serve, about 20 minutes. Drain.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

In a food processor, coarsely chop the shrimp. Add the cornmeal, green onions, egg and harissa. Season with salt and pepper. Pulse for a few seconds until combined but still slightly chunky. With lightly oiled hands, form the mixture into 6 patties. Place on a plate. Oil the patties.
Grill the patties for 3 minutes on each side or until cooked through but still juicy. Toast the buns.
Spread the cocktail sauce over the inside of the buns. Top the bun bottoms with the patties, the zucchini mixture and the nasturtium leaves. Close with the bun tops.
Turkey Patties: In a bowl, thoroughly combine all the ingredients.
With slightly damp hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties. Brush with oil and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the patties for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or until they are cooked through. Toast the buns, if desired.
Spread the sriracha mayonnaise onto each bun. Layer with the lettuce, turkey patty, cucumbers and bean sprouts. Close the burgers.

Pickled Cranberries: In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Season with salt. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until the cranberries start to burst slightly and the liquid is thick and syrupy, about 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. With your hands, shape the meat mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate. Lightly oil the patties.
Burgers: Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until the meat is cooked through. Grill the hamburger buns.
Cover the bun bottoms with mayonnaise and mustard. Top with lettuce, the red onion and patties. Garnish with the pickled cranberries. Close with the bun tops.
Glaze: In a bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Set aside 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the mixture in a small bowl for serving.
Dressing: In a large bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Season with salt. Set aside 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the dressing in another small bowl for serving.
Coleslaw: Add all the ingredients to the large bowl with the dressing. Toss to coat the vegetables with the dressing. Adjust the seasoning.

Burgers: In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the pork belly slices for 5 minutes per side, until crisp. Pour in the glaze and coat the meat well. Continue cooking for 2 minutes, until the meat is nicely caramelized.
Spread the bottom halves of the buns with the reserved glaze. Top with the pork belly slices and the slaw. Spread the inside of the top halves with the reserved dressing. Close with the bun tops.
Wasabi Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Cover and refrigerate.
Fried Cod and Pickles: Preheat the oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (180°C). Set a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Place ½ cup (75 g) of the flour in a shallow dish and set aside.

Place the remaining flour in a separate bowl. Add the pale ale and dill. Stir gently with a fork just until the batter comes together (there will still be a few lumps of flour visible). Season with salt and pepper.

Dredge two pieces of fish at a time in the flour, shaking off any excess. Coat in the batter and carefully drop into the hot oil. Watch out for splattering. Cook for 3 minutes or until the batter is golden. Let drain on the wire rack. Repeat with the remaining fish. Repeat the same set of steps with the pickle slices. Cook for 2 minutes and keep warm.

Burgers: Toast the inside of the burger buns. Spread the inside of the buns with the wasabi mayonnaise and top with a few lettuce leaves. Divide the fried cod and pickles between the burgers and finish with the tops of the buns.

Barbecue Sauce: In a small saucepan, brown the onion in the oil. Add the remaining ingredients and bring to boil. Simmer for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens. Set aside.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high.
Bean Sprout Salad: In a wok over high heat, sauté the beans in the oil for 1 minute. Add the sauces and cook for 1 minute. Keep warm.
Shape the meat into 4 patties. Season with salt and pepper. Brush the meat with half the barbecue sauce.
Grill the patties for about 5 minutes per side or until the meat is thoroughly cooked. Toast the buns.
Spread barbecue sauce in the buns. Add the meat and garnish with the bean sprout salad and lettuce leaves.
Brush the chops with barbecue sauce. Marinate for 15 minutes at room temperature. Keep the remaining sauce aside.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium.
In a cast iron skillet, brown the onions in the oil on the grill for about 15 minutes (you can also do this on the stove in a non-stick skillet). Set aside.

Grill the chops over medium-high heat, for about 4 minutes per side depending on their thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Place on a work surface and slice thinly. Combine the pork with the onions and the remaining barbecue sauce.
Toast the buns. To serve, top with the pork mixture and shredded lettuce.
Coleslaw: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. If possible, let the salad rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow the cabbage to soften.
Barbecue Sauce: In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil and simmer for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Set aside.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high. Oil the grate.

In another bowl, combine the meat, barbecue sauce, and green onions. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into four patties. Grill the patties for about 3 minutes per side or until the meat is thoroughly cooked. Brush with barbecue sauce. Toast the buns.

Spread the inside of the buns with mayonnaise. Place the meat inside the buns. Top with the cheese and coleslaw. Serve with the remaining coleslaw and barbecue sauce. Delicious with slices of grilled potatoes or potato chips.
Beet Chiffonade: In a bowl, combine the cider vinegar, water, sugar and salt. Add the beet slices. Let marinate for 10 minutes.
Toppings: In another bowl, combine the mustard and honey. Set aside.
In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook the onions in the butter until nicely golden, about 10 minutes. Set aside.
Burgers: In a bowl, combine the pork, bacon and green onion. Season with salt and pepper. With your hands or a burger press, form the mixture into four patties.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the patties for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Top the patties with the cheese slices and let melt for 1 minute. Toast the hamburger buns.
Spread the inside of the buns with the honey-mustard mixture. Top the bun bottoms with the burger patties, beet slices, caramelized onions, spinach and pear. Finish with the bun tops.

Vegetable Salad: In a bowl, whisk together the brown sugar, fish sauce, lime juice and sambal oelek just until the brown sugar has dissolved. Add the bell pepper and cucumber. Toss to coat the vegetables with the dressing. Let marinate while you prepare the patties. Drain before serving.
Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.

In a food processor, chop the onion, garlic and cilantro. Add the shrimp, fish sauce, brown sugar and sambal oelek. Pulse a few times so as not to chop the shrimp too finely. Transfer to a large bowl.
Add the pork and breadcrumbs to the bowl. Mix well. With your hands, shape the mixture into 8 patties. Place on a plate. Oil the patties.
Burgers: Grill the patties for 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Grill the hamburger buns.
Cover the inside of the buns with mayonnaise. Top the bun bottoms with the lettuce, patties and salad. Close with the bun tops.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Spread the bell pepper, cucumber and mango out on a plate. Drizzle with the lime juice. Set aside.

With your hands, form the ground pork into 8 large, thin patties. To make this easier, place the patties between two pieces of plastic wrap and flatten with your hands or use a hamburger press. Place the patties on an oiled plate. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly brush with oil.
Grill the patties for 2 to 3 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Grill the buns.

Spread the inside of the buns with tzatziki. Place 2 patties on each bun bottom. Top with the bell pepper, cucumber, mango, lettuce and cilantro. Add Sriracha, to taste. Close with the bun tops and serve.
Coleslaw: Place the cabbage in a bowl. Set aside.

In a small saucepan or in the microwave oven, bring the vinegar and sugar to a boil. Pour over the cabbage, add the sour cream and mix well to combine. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate while preparing the burgers.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, place ½ cup of the bread crumbs. Set aside.

In another bowl, soak the bread slices in the milk. Let rest for 5 minutes. Squeeze the bread with your hands, discard the remaining milk and place the bread back in the bowl. Add the chicken, butter, nutmeg and remaining bread crumbs. Mix thoroughly. Season with salt and pepper.
Shape 4 patties and coat with the reserved bread crumbs.
Grill the patties for about 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Toast the buns.
Place the grilled patties on the toasted buns and top generously with coleslaw.
Sauce: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Burgers: Toast the hamburger buns. Cover the inside of the buns with the sauce. Top the bun bottoms with the chicken, pickles and lettuce. Close with the bun tops.
Chicken: Preheat the electric or charcoal smoker to 150 °C (300 °F). Add the chips and let smoke for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, season the chicken with salt and pepper. Place the chicken thighs in the smoker. Close the lid and cook for 45 minutes or until cooked through, turning every 15 minutes.
Coleslaw: In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Burgers: Spread the inside of the rolls with the mayonnaise. Top with the coleslaw and pieces of chicken, whole or thinly sliced. Close the burgers.
Mayonnaise: In a small bowl, whisk together all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Set aside.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium-high. Oil the grate.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the spinach in the oil until just wilted. Salt and pepper. Place a sieve over a bowl. Place the spinach in it and let cool slightly.
Grill the sausage patties until cooked through, about 5 minutes per side. Place a slice of cheese on each patty and let melt for 1 minute. Toast the buns.

Spread the bottom halves of the buns with the tomato sauce. Top with the sausage patties and the spinach. Spread the inside of the top halves with the mayonnaise. Close the burgers and serve right away.
Caper Mayonnaise: In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Keep in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
Salmon Patties: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In another bowl, combine all the ingredients until smooth. Add bread crumbs if the mixture is too soft. Season with salt and pepper. Shape into 6 patties.
Adjust the burners to medium heat. Grill the patties for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or until the salmon is cooked through. Toast the buns.

Burgers: Spread the caper mayonnaise on the inside of the toasted buns. Place the lettuce and then the patties on the bottom halves of the buns. Garnish with cucumber slices and cover with the top halves of the buns.
Coleslaw: In a bowl, combine the cabbage, vinegar, sugar and green parts of the green onions. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside while you make the burgers.

Burgers: In a large bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, vinegar, sriracha and egg. Season with salt and pepper. Add ½ cup (40 g) of the panko and mix well. Let sit for 5 minutes. Add the salmon and white parts of the green onions. Mix well.
In a shallow dish, combine the remaining panko with the sesame seeds.
Using a 1/4-cup (60 ml) ice cream scoop, shape the salmon mixture into 8 balls. Flatten them to form patties and press into the panko mixture on both sides.
In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the salmon patties in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes on each side or until nicely browned.
Cover the insides of the hamburger buns with mayonnaise and sriracha. Top the bottom buns with the salmon patties. Garnish with the coleslaw. Close with the bun tops.
Galettes: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a food processor or with a knife, coarsely chop the salmon. Transfer to a bowl. Add the remaining ingredients to the bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
With your hands, shape the salmon mixture into 4 patties. Place on a large plate. Lightly oil the patties.
Burgers: Grill the patties for 3 minutes on each side or until the fish is cooked through. Grill the hamburger buns.

Spread barbecue sauce over the inside of the bun bottoms. Top with the patties. Garnish with roasted bell peppers and arugula. Spread mayonnaise over the inside of the bun tops, then close the burgers.
Quick remoulade sauce: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate.
Burgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.
Shape the tuna into 4 patties. Grill until pink inside, 2 or 3 minutes per side. Season with salt and pepper. Toast the buns.
Meanwhile, in a non-stick skillet, fry the eggs in the oil until the whites are set. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the remoulade sauce on the buns. Garnish each bun with lettuce, tomatoes, a patty and an egg.
Patties: In a bowl, combine 1 egg with the tuna, panko and mayonnaise. With your hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties. Place on a plate.
In a shallow dish, place the flour. In a second shallow dish, lightly beat the remaining egg. In a third shallow dish, place the tempura.
Working one at a time, dredge the patties in the flour, gently shaking off any excess. Dip into the beaten egg, letting some of the excess drip off. Press into the tempura to coat well.
Place the patties in the basket of an air fryer. Cook for 10 minutes at 400°F (200°C) or until browned. Remove the patties from the air fryer.

Marinated Cucumbers: Meanwhile, in a bowl, whisk together the vinegar and sugar. Season with salt. Whisk until the sugar and salt have dissolved. Add the cucumbers and dill. Mix well and let marinate for 5 minutes. Drain.
Burgers: Cover the inside of the buns with the cream cheese. Top the bun bottoms with the avocado slices, tuna patties, marinated cucumbers and lettuce. Close with the bun tops.
Grilled Vegetables: Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high. Oil the grate.

Oil the bell peppers and zucchini. Season with salt and pepper. Place the peppers on the grill, skin side down. Brush with oil and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until the skin is well charred. Place the peppers in an airtight container. Let cool. Remove the skin. Set aside.
Grill the zucchini on each side. Set aside.
Patties: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. With your hands or with a hamburger press, shape the meat mixture into four patties.
Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Season with salt and pepper.

Hamburgers: Toast the buns. Spread the inside with mayonnaise and mustard. Place the patties on the bun bottoms. Layer with the cheese, zucchini, tomato, bell pepper and basil. Cover with the bun tops.

In a small bowl, combine the ricotta, sundried tomato pesto and pepper. Cover and set aside. In another bowl, combine the milk-fed ground veal, chopped onion, fresh basil, pepper, breadcrumbs and egg.

Shape eight 1-cm (1/2-inch) thick patties. Place about 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of the cheese mixture on 4 patties and top with remaining 4 patties. Seal the edges by crimping them lightly with a fork. Brush the patties with Worcestershire sauce.

Grill on the barbecue on high heat for 1 minute on each side. Continue cooking over medium-low heat for about 4 to 5 minutes per side or until the meat is brown on the outside and is no longer pink inside.
Serve the veal patties on sesame Kaiser rolls. Top with the remaining sundried tomatoes pesto, basil leaves and slices of Portobello mushrooms.
Serve with grilled peppers.
Sauce: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Tofu Patties: With the rack in the top third of the oven, preheat the oven to broil. Line a baking sheet with foil.
In a food processor, purée all of the ingredients, except for the cheese, until smooth. Use a spatula to scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed. Season with salt and pepper.
With lightly oiled hands, form the tofu mixture into 8 thin patties. Place on the baking sheet.
Broil the patties for 5 minutes, turning them over halfway through, or until browned. As soon as they are out of the oven, top half of the patties with a slice of cheese.
Burgers: Meanwhile, place the buns on a second baking sheet, cut-side up. Toast the buns in the oven for 1 to 2 minutes.

Cover the inside of the bun bottoms with some of the sauce. Top with a plain tofu patty, pickle slices and half of the lettuce. Cover with the middle bun layer. Cover with sauce. Top with a cheese-covered patty, onion and remaining lettuce. Finish off with the bun tops.

Patties: Stuff four hamburger patties with 15 ml (1 tablespoon) jalapeño pesto each. Season with salt and pepper. Preheat the grill, setting the burners on medium-high. Oil the grate. Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through.

Hamburgers: Toast the hamburger buns. Spread the inside with Dijon mustard and mayonnaise. Layer with lettuce leaves and the patties. Add, to taste, slices of cheese, tomato, sandwich pickles, and onion.
In a bowl, combine the mushrooms, onion, oil and Worcestershire. Season with salt and pepper. Place the vegetable mixture in the basket of an air fryer. Cook for 8 minutes at 400°F (200°C).
Meanwhile, shape the meat into 2 patties. Place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper.
Push the vegetables to the sides of the air fryer basket. Place the beef patties at the centre of the basket. Cook for 10 minutes, flipping the patties over halfway through cooking (see note).

Cover the inside of the hamburger buns with mustard and mayonnaise. Place the patties on the bun bottoms and top with the cheese. Cover with the vegetable mixture and arugula. Close with the bun tops. Serve with green salad, if desired.
Chipotle Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate.
Hamburgers: Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high. Oil the grate.
With your hands or a hamburger press, shape the meat into four patties.
Grill the patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until cooked through. Season with salt and pepper.
Toast the buns. Place the patties on the bottom buns and spread with chipotle mayonnaise. Garnish with fried onion rings. Cover with the top buns.
Sauce: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Burgers: With your hands or a hamburger press, shape the meat into four patties. Season with salt and pepper.

In a non-stick skillet, cook the patties in the oil for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, or until they are cooked through (see note). Place a slice of cheese on each patty and continue cooking until the cheese starts to melt. Set the patties aside on a plate and keep warm. In the cleaned skillet, toast the buns.
Spread the mayonnaise on the inside of the buns. Top with the patties, tomato slices and lettuce. Close the buns.
Tomato Confit: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C).
In a bowl, combine the tomatoes, lemon juice, sugar and salt. Let marinate for 5 minutes. Drain.
In a baking dish, combine the tomatoes and oil. Bake for about 25 minutes or until the tomatoes begin to caramelize and wilt.
Transfer to a serving dish. Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until completely chilled.
Burrata: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the garlic in the oil. Remove the garlic. Add the bread and toast on both sides. Add oil, if needed.
Place the burrata over the tomatoes and cut in half. Season with pepper and top with the basil. Serve with the toasted bread.
Confit Figs: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high (see note). Oil the grate.

In a cast iron skillet, off the heat, place the figs and lemon slices. Cover with the oil and honey. Season with salt and pepper. Place the skillet on the barbecue and cook for 5 to 6 minutes or until the figs are glazed and tender, stirring occasionally.
Burrata: Meanwhile, on a plate, oil the onion slices. Season with salt and pepper.
Grill the onion slices for 3 minutes on each side or until tender.
Arrange the figs and the lemon slices in a serving dish. Top with the Burrata and onions. Garnish with the herbs and chive blossoms. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with toasted baguette.
Confit Tomatoes: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Let marinate for 15 minutes. In a strainer, drain the tomatoes well. Discard the marinade.

Place a piece of parchment paper over a sheet of foil. Place the tomatoes at the centre of the parchment. Tightly seal into a packet. Place the packet directly on the grill and cook for 10 minutes or until the tomatoes start to shrivel. Place the packet on a plate and open the paper to let the tomatoes cool.
Burrata: Meanwhile, brush the peach wedges with 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the oil. Grill the peaches on both flesh-sides until heated through, about 5 minutes.

Place the burrata on a serving dish and cut in half. Add the tomatoes and peaches. Drizzle with the remaining oil and the honey. Garnish with basil leaves. Add a pinch of fleur de sel and pepper. Serve with toasted bread.
Roasted Tomatoes: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high.
In a small casserole dish or cast iron or enamelled skillet, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.

Place the casserole dish on the barbecue. Close the lid and cook for 5 minutes or until the tomatoes are tender. Remove from the heat and let cool. Drain the tomatoes and set the cooking liquid aside.

Burrata: Place the burrata at the centre of a serving dish. Shape the prosciutto and cantaloupe slices into small rose shapes (roll up one slice at a time to form a flower), or fold slices into a series of pleats, and arrange around the burrata alternating with the drained grilled tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Using a knife, cut open the burrata. Drizzle with the reserved tomato cooking liquid. Garnish with basil leaves. Serve with grilled bread or crackers of your choice.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).

In a baking dish, toss the grapes with the lemon juice and honey. Add the rosemary sprigs. Season with salt. Bake for 12 minutes or until the grapes have burst slightly, stirring halfway through cooking. Remove from the oven. Remove and compost the rosemary sprigs.

Place the burrata on a serving dish. Using a small knife, cut a cross in the top of the burrata to open it. Top with the grapes and their cooking juices. Garnish with onion petals and sprinkle with the hazelnuts. Drizzle with olive oil and honey. Sprinkle with fleur de sel. Serve with grilled bread.

Dressing: In a small pot, bring the rhubarb, vinegar, water and sugar to a boil. Simmer for 8 minutes or until the rhubarb is tender. Remove from the heat. Add the camomile and let infuse for 10 minutes.

Remove and compost the camomile. Transfer the rhubarb mixture to a tall, narrow container (such as a measuring cup). Using a hand blender, purée the mixture until smooth. With the machine running, slowly drizzle in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. The dressing will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

Compote: In another small pot off the heat, combine all of the ingredients. Bring to a boil while stirring often. Simmer for 8 to 12 minutes, until the compote thickens slightly. Do not overcook. Transfer to a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate for 45 minutes or until completely chilled.
Puffed Buckwheat (optional): Meanwhile, line a baking sheet with paper towels. Place a sieve over a heatproof bowl.

In a deep pot over medium-high heat, warm the oil to 400°F (200°C). Add the buckwheat and stir until puffed up. Watch out for splattering. Immediately drain the puffed buckwheat in the sieve. Spread the buckwheat out on the baking sheet. Season with salt. Let cool. The puffed buckwheat will keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container at room temperature. An excellent addition to salads and soups.
Assembly: In a bowl, combine 3 tbsp (45 ml) of the dressing with the cherry tomatoes and strawberries. Season with salt and pepper.

Place the compote in a shallow dish and top with the burratina. Place the tomato-strawberry mixture around the cheese. Garnish with basil leaves. Sprinkle fleur de sel and chili powder over the cheese. Top with the puffed buckwheat and serve with toasted bread.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
