Salt and pepper. Press lightly and spread the leek and cheese mixture over them. Add the remaining potatoes, then the squash. Finish with the firm cheese and top with a cabbage leaf. Fold the leaves toward the centre and finish with a cabbage leaf.

Brush with butter. Wrap the pan in two sheets of aluminum foil. Place the pan on a baking sheet. Bake for about 1 hour and 30 minutes. Remove from the oven. Place a plate on top. Let stand for 15 minutes.
Unmould and serve with a green salad.
In a saucepan, soften the shallots and garlic in the butter for about 2 minutes. Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Add the milk and bring to a boil, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Add the cheese, nutmeg and parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Stir until the cheese has melted.
Place the cooked cauliflower or broccoflower in a serving dish. Spoon the sauce over and serve.
Cauliflower: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
On a work surface, quarter the cauliflower, keeping the leaves intact. Place the cauliflower pieces in a baking dish.
In a bowl, combine the oil and garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Coat the cauliflower with the oil mixture.
Bake for 40 minutes or until the cauliflower is al dente when pierced with the tip of a knife and nicely browned.

Sauce: Meanwhile, in a small pot over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the cracked pepper and cook for 1 minute while whisking. Add the flour and cook for 1 minute while stirring. Whisk in the milk. Bring to a boil. Simmer gently for 2 minutes or until the sauce thickens. Remove from the heat.

Add both types of cheese to the pot. Mix until the cheese is melted and the sauce is smooth. Adjust the seasoning. Cover and set aside. Reheat over low heat, as needed, without letting the sauce boil.

Spread the sauce out in a shallow serving dish. Top with the cauliflower and generously sprinkle with more Parmesan. Season with pepper. Serve as an appetizer or alongside our herb-crusted rack of pork, if desired.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to medium.

Place the cauliflower, onion, and garlic in the centre of the doubled up aluminum foil square. Drizzle with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Close to seal the foil. Cook on the grill for about 10 minutes or until the cauliflower is tender.
Serve with Grilled Pork Chops with Molasses and Lime.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (210°C).
On a work surface, remove the leaves and cut down the stem of the cauliflower so that it stands flat. Place the cauliflower, stem side down, in a baking dish.
In a bowl, combine the remaining ingredients. Coat the cauliflower thoroughly with the mixture. Season with salt and pepper.

Bake for about 45 minutes, or until the cauliflower is tender with the tip of a knife. If needed, cover the cauliflower with aluminum foil to prevent further browning while it cooks for a few minutes longer.

In a large saucepan, bring the water, vinegar, sugar, garlic, salt, and spices to a boil. Add the vegetables and bring to a boil. Simmer for about 5 minutes or until the vegetables are al dente. Remove the garlic cloves.

Spoon the vegetables in four clean 250 ml (1 cup) jars and fill with the boiling liquid up to ½-cm (¼-inch) off the rim. Close and let cool. Refrigerate. Wait at least 24 hours before serving to allow the flavours to develop. Keeps for about 6 months in the refrigerator.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the butter, honey, spices, salt and pepper. Add the cauliflower and toss to coat well. Lay out on the baking sheet in an even layer.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, turning over halfway through, or until golden.

1. With the rack in the upper third of the oven, preheat the broiler. Let preheat for about 5 minutes. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil. Wash a cauliflower, drain well, and break into small florets directly on the baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, and toss well with your hands. Bake for 8 minutes. With oven mitts, remove the baking sheet from the oven. Toss the cauliflower with a spatula and continue baking for about 4 minutes or until the cauliflower is cooked through and lightly browned.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the sugar, salt, spices, and oil. Coat the cauliflower florets. Bake for about 25 minutes or until the cauliflower is cooked and golden brown.
In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Let pickle for at least 15 minutes. Drain when ready to use.
Pickled kohlrabi will keep for at least 1 week in the refrigerator. Delicious in spring rolls or Vietnamese banh mi sandwiches.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Strain the sauerkraut in a colander and rinse under cold water. Drain well, pressing between your hands to extract as much liquid as possible. Set aside.

In a 12-inch (30 cm) round, 2 1/2-inch (6 cm) deep Dutch oven or a large, deep non-stick skillet over medium heat, cook half of the bacon at a time until nicely browned. Set aside on a plate. Pour the cooking fat into a glass bowl.
In the same pot, soften the onion in 3 tbsp (45 ml) of the cooking fat. Set the remaining cooking fat aside. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute while stirring.
Add the sauerkraut, wine, water, spices, bay leaves, potatoes and bacon to the pot. Season with pepper and mix well. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake in the oven for 1 hour.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown the sausages in 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the reserved cooking fat.

Remove the sauerkraut from the oven. Place the sausages over the sauerkraut. Continue baking in the oven, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes or until the sausages are cooked through and the liquid from the sauerkraut has almost completely reduced.

On a work surface, slice the sausages, if desired. Remove the bay leaves and juniper berries from the sauerkraut and compost them. Arrange the sliced sausages over the sauerkraut. Sprinkle with the parsley. Place the choucroute at the centre of the table. Serve with your choice of mustard (such as Dijon, whole-grain) and slices of country bread, if desired.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, beat the egg with the water using a fork. Set the egg wash aside.
Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip. On the baking sheets, pipe balls of dough 2.5 cm (1 inch) in diameter, spacing them apart.
Using a brush, brush the balls of dough with the egg wash. Sprinkle generously with pearl sugar.
Bake one sheet at a time for 25 minutes or until the puffs are golden brown. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Serve, or keep in an airtight container for 2 days at room temperature. Chouquettes are best the day they are made.

Maple Cream: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the cornstarch and flour. Whisk in the maple syrup, 1 cup (250 ml) of the cream and the eggs until smooth. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring continuously while scraping the sides and bottom of the pan. Let simmer for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.

Transfer the cream into a bowl and stir in the butter until smooth. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool and refrigerate for about 3 hours or until completely chilled.
Chou Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.

In a saucepan, bring the water, butter, sugar and salt to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon. Return the saucepan to the heat for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly until the mixture forms a ball that comes off the sides of the pan. Remove from the heat and let cool for 1 minute.
In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, or with a wooden spoon, add the eggs, one at a time, stirring thoroughly after each addition until smooth.
Transfer the dough into a pastry bag fitted with a 3/4-inch (2 cm) plain tip and shape approximately 20 choux (balls) onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them evenly.
In a bowl, combine the maple sugar and almond powder. Brush the choux with the milk and sprinkle generously with the maple sugar mixture.

Bake for 30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. Reduce the oven temperature to 225°F (110°C) and continue baking for about 20 minutes. Let cool completely. Cut the pastries in half horizontally. Remove some of the inside if the pastry is not completely dry.
Assembly: In a bowl, beat the remaining cream (1 cup/250 ml) until stiff peaks form. With a whisk or spatula, fold the whipped cream into the cooled maple cream.
With a pastry bag or spoon, fill the choux pastries with the maple cream. Close the cream puff. Refrigerate until ready to serve. Cream puffs are always best the same day.

Pastry Cream: In a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar, cornstarch and flour. Add the eggs and whisk until smooth. Add the milk and vanilla. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the sides and bottom of the pot, until thickened. Strain the pastry cream, if needed. Transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Refrigerate for 3 hours or until completely chilled.
Choux Pastry: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a pot, bring 2/3 cup (150 ml) of the water to a boil with the butter, sugar and salt. Remove the pot from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms into a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides of the pot.

Return the pot to medium heat and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes to dry out the dough. This step is crucial for a successful choux pastry. A thin film will form on the bottom of the pot once the dough has sufficiently dried out. Remove from the heat and let cool for 1 minute. Transfer to a bowl or into the bowl of a stand mixer.
Using a wooden spoon or the paddle attachment, beat in 3 eggs, one at a time, mixing between each addition until the mixture is smooth.
Transfer into a pastry bag fitted with a ¾-inch (2 cm) plain tip. On the baking sheet, form cream puffs using about 3 tbsp (45 ml) of the mixture for each one, evenly spacing them out.
In a bowl, whisks the remaining egg with the remaining water. Brush the cream puffs with the egg wash.

Bake for 25 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (165°C). Bake for another 20 minutes or until the cream puffs look dry and golden. Turn off the oven and let the cream puffs dry out for 30 minutes, keeping the oven door slightly ajar with a wooden spoon. Remove from the oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet.
Whipped Cream: In a bowl, whisk the cream, sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until firm peaks form. Transfer to a pastry bag fitted with a large star tip.

Assembly: Cut off the top of each cream puff and fill with the pastry cream (see note). Garnish with banana slices and a few dollops of whipped cream. Close the cream puffs with their tops. Drizzle with the caramel.
Choux Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

In a saucepan, bring the water, butter, honey and salt to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the flour at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough forms into a smooth ball that comes off the sides of the pan.
Place the saucepan over low heat and cook, stirring constantly, for about 2 minutes or until the mixture forms into a soft and sticky ball. Remove from the heat and let cool for 1 minute.
In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, in a food processor or with a wooden spoon, add the eggs, one at a time, stirring well between each addition until the dough is smooth.

With a 30 ml (2 tbsp) ice cream scoop or with a pastry bag fitted with a 2 cm (3/4-inch) plain tip, shape 24 balls of dough on the baking sheet, spacing them evenly. Run the scoop under cold water between each ball to prevent the dough from sticking.

Bake for 30 minutes or until the choux are golden brown. Reduce the oven temperature to 165 °C (325 °F) and continue baking for 20 minutes. Let cool completely. With a bread knife, cut the top of the choux and set aside for assembly. Remove any moist dough inside the choux.
Raspberry Cream: In a saucepan off the heat, combine the sugar, flour and cornstarch. Whisk in the eggs and milk.

Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and taking care to scrape the bottom and sides of the pan. Pour into a bowl. Cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the warm pastry cream. Refrigerate for 3 hours or until the pastry cream has completely chilled.
In a bowl, whip the cream until stiff peaks form. With a whisk, fold the whipped cream in the cooled pastry cream. Stir in the raspberries.
Assembly: With a spoon, fill the bottom of the choux with the raspberry cream. Top with two or three fresh raspberries. Close the choux.
In a bowl, combine the icing sugar, water and food colouring until smooth.
Drizzle the choux with the pink icing and/or simply dust with icing sugar. Store in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

Pastry Cream: In a small pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar and flour. Add the eggs and vanilla. Mix well. Add the hot milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the sides and bottom of the pot, until thickened. Let simmer for 1 to 2 minutes over low heat. Remove from the heat. Add the butter.

Strain the cream through a sieve, if needed. Transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool. Refrigerate for 2 hours or until completely chilled. When ready to use, mix with a spatula until creamy and smooth.
Choux Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a pot, bring the water, butter and salt to a boil. Remove the pot from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon. Return the pot to medium heat and cook, stirring, until the mixture forms into a ball and detaches from the sides of the pot, about 2 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and add the eggs, one at a time, mixing between each addition until the mixture is smooth.
Transfer into a pastry bag fitted with a ¾-inch (2 cm) plain tip. Pipe 12 cream puffs onto the baking sheet, spacing them out. You can freeze the cream puffs at this point, if desired (see note).
Bake for 25 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 275°F (135°C) and bake for another 20 minutes. Let cool completely on a wire rack.

Cut off the top of each cream puff and remove any dough from the middle that has not completely dried out. Fill with the chilled pastry cream. Close the cream puffs with their tops. Using a spoon, drizzle the melted chocolate over the cream puffs.

Gluten-free Pastry Cream: In a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar, cornstarch and salt. Add the egg and egg yolk. Mix well. Add the hot milk and vanilla. Bring to a boil over medium heat while whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pot, just until the mixture thickens. Simmer over low heat for 2 minutes.

Strain the pastry cream through a sieve, as needed. Transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap directly on the surface of the cream. Let cool. Refrigerate until completely chilled, about 3 hours. When ready to use, mix with a spatula until creamy and smooth.
Gluten-free Choux Pastry: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the rice flour, quinoa flour and cornstarch.

In a pot, bring the water, milk, butter, sugar and salt to a boil. Remove the pot from the heat. Add the flour mixture all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms into a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Return the pot to medium heat and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes to dry out the dough. Transfer to a bowl or into the bowl of a stand mixer.

Using a wooden spoon or the paddle attachment, mix the dough for 3 minutes to cool and to draw out the humidity. Add the eggs and egg white one at a time, mixing well between each addition, until the mixture is shiny and smooth.

Using a 3-tbsp (45 ml) ice cream scoop or a pastry bag fitted with a ¾-inch (2 cm) plain tip, shape 12 balls of choux pastry, evenly spacing them out on the baking sheet. Rinse the ice cream scoop under cold water between each use to prevent the choux pastry from sticking. Freeze at this point, if desired (see note).
Bake for 30 minutes or until golden. Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (165°C). Bake for another 25 minutes. Let cool completely.
Using a bread knife, cut off the rounded tops of each cream puff and set aside. Remove any dough that has not completely dried out from inside the cream puffs.
Assembly: In a bowl, whisk the cream and icing sugar with an electric mixer until semi-stiff peaks form. Transfer into a pastry bag fitted with a star tip.

Fill the bottom of the cream puffs with the pastry cream and top with the whipped cream. Garnish with berries, if desired. Close with the tops of the cream puffs. Sprinkle with icing sugar. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Craquelin: Using an electric mixer, cream the butter with the brown sugar. With a spatula, add the flour and salt. With your hands, finish mixing the dough until smooth.
Using a rolling pin, roll out the dough between 2 sheets of parchment paper to a thickness of about 2 mm (1/8 inch). Refrigerate for 1 hour.

Using a round cookie cutter about 6 cm (2 1/2 inches) in diameter, or the same size as the cream puffs, cut out the craquelin rounds and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Keep the craquelin rounds in the freezer.
Choux Pastry: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.
In a saucepan, bring the milk, water, sugar, salt and butter to a boil.
When the butter has melted, remove the saucepan from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough is smooth and pulls away easily from the sides.
Return the saucepan to low heat and cook, stirring the dough, for about 2 minutes to dry it out well.
Remove from the heat and let cool for a few minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing vigorously with a wooden spoon, an electric mixer or a food processor until the dough is smooth.
Using a pastry bag fitted with a fairly large plain tip, pipe 6 cm (2 1/2 inch) puffs onto the baking sheet, spacing them apart (see note).

Place a craquelin round on top of each puff. Place in the oven. Immediately lower the oven temperature to 190 °C (375 °F). Cook for 15 minutes. Then lower the oven temperature to 180 °C (350 °F) and continue baking for 15 minutes. If needed, lower the temperature to 165 °C (325 °F) and finish baking for a few more minutes. Let cool.
Chocolate Coffee Chantilly: In a bowl, place the chocolate.
In a saucepan, bring 250 ml (1 cup) of the cream and the corn syrup to a boil. Remove from the heat, add the coffee beans, cover and let infuse for 5 minutes.

Strain through a sieve directly over the chocolate. Let stand for 1 minute. Using an electric mixer, beat the mixture. Gradually pour in the remaining cold cream (500 ml/2 cups). Pour into a container. Cover and let set for 12 hours in the refrigerator.
Whip the chocolate cream until soft peaks form. It's important not to overwhip the cream, as it could become grainy.
Cut the pastries in half horizontally. Place the cream in a pastry bag fitted with a star tip and pipe it onto the bottom halves of the puffs. Close the choux.
Craquelin Topping: In a bowl, cream the butter, brown sugar and food colouring with an electric mixer. With the machine running on low speed, add the flour and salt.
Using a rolling pin, roll the mixture out between two sheets of parchment paper until 1/8 inch (3 mm) thick. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Using a 1 ½-inch (4 cm) round cookie cutter, cut out 24 circles of craquelin. Repeat with the scraps as needed. Spread the craquelin out on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Refrigerate.
Choux Pastry: Meanwhile, with both racks in the middle positions, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line two baking sheets with silicone mats or parchment paper (see note).

In a pot, bring the milk, water, butter, sugar and salt to boil. Remove the pot from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms into a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Return the pot to medium heat and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes to dry out the dough. Transfer to a bowl or into the bowl of a stand mixer.

Using a wooden spoon or the paddle attachment, mix the dough for 5 minutes to cool and to draw out the humidity. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well between each addition, until the mixture is shiny and smooth.
Transfer into a pastry bag fitted with a large plain tip. On each baking sheet, pipe twelve 1 ½-inch (4 cm) round cream puffs, evenly spacing them out.
Place a circle of craquelin over each puff. Freeze at this point, if desired.

Bake for 20 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (165°C) and bake for another 15 minutes. Turn off the oven and leave the cream puffs there for to dry for 15 minutes, keeping the oven door slightly ajar with a wooden spoon. Let cool completely on a wire rack, about 1 hour.
Assembly: In a bowl, whisk the whipping cream, dulce de leche and salt with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Transfer to a pastry bag fitted with a plain tip.
Transfer the apple jelly into a second pastry bag fitted with another plain tip or in a cone of parchment paper.

Pierce the bottoms of each cooled cream puff with the piping bag tip and fill with the apply jelly, then the caramel whipped cream (see note). Refrigerate on a baking sheet lined with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a small pot, bring the sugar, corn syrup and water to a boil. Cook, without stirring, until an amber caramel forms. Remove from the heat.

Working one at a time, dip the bottom of each filled cream puff into the hot caramel, being careful not to burn yourself. Use kitchen tongs, as needed. Place the cream puffs back on the baking sheet to let the caramel cool and set at room temperature, about 30 minutes.

Insert a wooden stick into the top of each cream puff, if desired. Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve. The cream puffs, once fully assembled, are best enjoyed the day they are made.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).
Cut Brussels sprouts in half if they are small (or quarter if they are large). Place on a baking sheet. Add bacon. Drizzle with a little olive oil. Season with salt and pepper and toss well.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes or until vegetables are tender and beginning to brown. Add pecans a few minutes before the end of cooking, to toast lightly.
Serve with meat or fish.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
On a non-stick baking sheet, toss the Brussels sprouts with the onion and oil. Season with salt and pepper. Turn the Brussels sprouts so they are cut side down on the baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes. Add the apples and bake for 30 minutes or until Brussels sprouts are tender and well roasted.
In a large non-stick skillet, brown the pancetta in the oil. Add the hazelnuts and brown. With a slotted spoon, reserve the pancetta and hazelnuts on a paper towel.

In the same skillet, brown the Brussels sprouts in the hot fat. Season with salt and pepper. Add the broth and bring to a boil. Simmer, stirring frequently, for about 10 minutes or until the sprouts are tender and glazed with the sauce. Adjust the seasoning. Spoon in a serving dish and sprinkle with the pancetta and hazelnuts.
In a large non-stick skillet, brown the bacon in the oil. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and transfer to a plate. Keep the rendered fat in the skillet.

In the same skillet, brown the Brussels sprouts in the rendered fat. Season with salt and pepper. Deglaze with the broth and mustard. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium heat, stirring frequently, for about 10 minutes or until the sprouts are tender and the broth has evaporated. Adjust the seasoning.
Spoon onto a serving platter and sprinkle with the bacon.
Roasted Brussels Sprouts: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Salt and pepper. Spread the mixture out in the baking sheet. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and the breadcrumbs are crisp and golden, stirring two or three times during cooking.
Salad: In a large bowl, whisk together the oil, lime juice, maple syrup and garlic. Salt and pepper. Add the remaining ingredients and the roasted Brussels sprout mixture. Adjust the seasoning.
Transfer the salad to a large serving bowl. Sprinkle with Parmesan shavings and herb leaves. Top with the spicy chili-citrus condiment.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a bowl, combine the Brussels sprouts, Parmesan, 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the oil and the garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Spread the mixture out in the baking sheet. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until the sprouts are tender and the cheese is crispy and golden, stirring two or three times during cooking.
Meanwhile, in a small skillet over high heat, brown the pancetta in the remaining oil. Using a slotted spoon, remove the pancetta from the skillet and set aside on a plate lined with paper towels.
In the same skillet over medium heat, toast the bread in the pancetta cooking fat until golden. Add more oil as needed. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the Caesar dressing out in a serving dish. Add the Brussels sprouts. Top with the pancetta, croutons and capers.
Brussels Sprouts: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Place the stalk of Brussels sprouts on the baking sheet. Using a pastry brush, coat the sprouts with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Place the bacon slices around the stalk on the baking sheet. Bake for 8 minutes.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven. Turn over the stalk of Brussels sprouts and the bacon slices. Using a pastry brush, coat the sprouts with the bacon fat. Bake for another 8 minutes or until the bacon is crispy. Drain the bacon on a plate lined with paper towels. Continue to bake the sprouts for 20 minutes or until tender and golden.
Toppings: Meanwhile, in a skillet over medium-high heat, cook the bread in the oil until golden. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from the heat and let cool.
In a small food processor, finely chop the bread with the bacon. Transfer into a bowl. Wash out the bowl of the food processor.
In the clean food processor, purée the mayonnaise, sour cream and green onion until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Place the stalk of Brussels sprouts on a serving dish. Drizzle with the green onion cream. Sprinkle with some of the bacon breadcrumbs, Parmesan and lemon zest. Season with pepper. Serve with the remaining toppings. Serve immediately as an appetizer.
Brussels Sprouts: Preheat half of the grill, setting the burners to high (see note).
Place the Brussels sprout stalk on a baking sheet. Using a pastry brush, coat the sprouts with the oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the stalk on the side of the barbecue that is off. Close the lid and grill for 40 minutes or until the sprouts are tender and golden, turning the stalk over halfway through cooking.
Blue Cheese Crumble (optional): Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients until just moistened. Press the mixture together with your hands, letting it fall in pieces of varying sizes onto the baking sheet.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes or until the crumble is cooked, stirring halfway through. Let cool completely, about 30 minutes.
Ranch Sauce: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all of the ingredients.

Place the grilled Brussels sprout stalk on a large serving dish. Serve with the ranch sauce, blue cheese crumble and fried onions. Delicious served with Buffalo Pork Skewers or grilled meat, if desired, or on its own during cocktail hour.
Craquelin: In a bowl, mix all the ingredients until the dough is smooth. Between two sheets of parchment paper, roll out the dough to a thickness of 3 mm (1/8 inch) and freeze for 30 minutes.

Remove the paper from the top. Using a 4 cm (1 1/2 inch) round cookie cutter, cut 10 circles from the craquelin dough. Using a 1.5 cm (3/4 inch) round cookie cutter, cut 20 circles from the craquelin dough. Keep in the freezer while you prepare the cream and the puffs.

Almond Praline Cream: In a pot off the heat, whisk together the sugar and cornstarch. Add the egg yolks and stir to combine. Stir in the milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly and scraping the bottom and sides of the pan until the mixture thickens. Remove from the heat.
Pour the pastry cream into a bowl. Cover the surface directly with plastic wrap. Let cool, then refrigerate until completely chilled, about 2 hours.
Choux Puffs: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

Transfer the choux pastry to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) plain tip. On the baking sheet, pipe 10 balls of dough 4 cm (1 1/2 inches) in diameter, spacing them apart. Then pipe 20 small balls 1 cm (1/2 inch) in diameter, attaching them on either side of the large balls.
Place the craquelin disks (small and large) on the balls of dough (small and large).
Bake for 25 minutes or until the puffs are cooked and golden brown. Turn the oven off, prop the door ajar with a wooden spoon and let sit for 30 minutes. Let cool completely on the baking sheet.

Assembly: Beat the pastry cream with an electric mixer to make it smooth again. Stir in the almond butter. In another bowl, whip the cream until stiff peaks form. Using a spatula, fold the whipped cream into the praline cream. Transfer to a pastry bag fitted with a 1 cm (1/2 inch) star tip.
Using a bread knife, cut the puffs in half horizontally. Sprinkle the bottoms with half the almonds, fill with the almond praline cream, then finish with the remaining almonds. Close the choux.
Serve, or refrigerate until ready to serve. Cream puffs are always best the same day.
In a saucepan, brown 2 slices of chopped bacon in 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of olive oil. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside on paper towels.

In the same saucepan, brown 1 chopped onion. Sprinkle with 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of flour and cook for 1 minute. Add 1 jar 240 ml of clam juice and bring to a boil, stirring continuously. Add 1 litre (4 cups) of chicken broth, 500 ml (2 cups) of peeled and cubed potatoes and 500 ml (2 cups) fresh or frozen corn kernels. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Add 500 ml (2 cups) Cajun Shrimp and 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of 35% cream. Warm through. Season with salt and pepper. Top with bacon and serve with lemon wedges.
Cinnamon sugar: In a bowl, combine the sugar and cinnamon. Set aside.
Choux pastry: Preheat the oil in the deep fryer to 190 °C (375 °F). Line a baking sheet with paper towels.

In a saucepan, bring the water, brown sugar, oil and salt to a boil. Off the heat, add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough forms a ball and pulls away from the sides.
Return the saucepan to low heat and cook, stirring the dough, for 1 minute.
Remove from the heat and let cool for a few minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, beating vigorously with a wooden spoon or an electric mixer, until the dough is smooth.

Place the dough in a pastry bag fitted with a star tip. Pipe a 10 to 15 cm (4 to 6 inch) strip of dough. Cut it with scissors and let it drop gently into the hot oil. Watch out for splatters. Fry 3 or 4 churros at a time for 3 to 4 minutes or until golden brown. Drain on the paper towels. Repeat with the remaining dough.
Roll the churros in the cinnamon sugar. Serve warm with the spicy chocolate sauce, if desired.
Topping: In a small bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Set aside (see note).
Churros: Preheat the oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with paper towels or a wire rack.

In a pot, bring the milk, water, butter, sugar and salt to a boil. Remove from the heat. Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms into a smooth ball that pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Return the pot to medium heat and cook, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes to dry out the dough. Transfer to a bowl.

Using a wooden spoon or an electric mixer, stir the dough for 3 minutes to cool and to draw out the humidity. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well between each addition, until the mixture is shiny and smooth. Stir in the cheese. Transfer the mixture into a pastry bag fitted with a large star tip.

Over the deep fryer, pipe out a log of dough about 4 to 6 inches (10 to 15 cm) long. Cut the log with kitchen scissors and let fall gently into the hot oil. Watch out for splattering. Fry 3 to 4 churros at a time for 3 to 4 minutes or until nicely browned, turning them over often during cooking. Drain on the baking sheet. Keep the churros warm (in an oven preheated to 200°F/95°C) while you fry the remaining churros.
Place the churros on a large serving dish. Sprinkle with the Parmesan topping. Serve immediately.
In a pot over medium heat, soften the pumpkin and onion in the oil. Add the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining ingredients and bring to a boil. Simmer, uncovered, over medium heat for 35 minutes or until the pumpkin is tender.
Remove the cloves, cardamom and cinnamon. Let cool, cover and refrigerate until the chutney is completely chilled.
In a blender or food processor, coarsely purée all the ingredients.
Transfer to a bowl. Serve, or cover and refrigerate. The chutney will keep for 1 week in the refrigerator.
In a saucepan, bring the vinegar and sugar to a boil. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the onions and cook for 2 minutes.
Place the allspice in cheesecloth or a tea ball. Add to the saucepan with the remaining ingredients. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove the allspice.
Pour the chutney into hot sterilized jars. Sterilize the filled jars in boiling water for 15 minutes to ensure a long shelf life. You can also freeze the chutney.

Chutney: In a small pot, bring the vinegar, honey and water to a boil. Add the remaining ingredients. Season with pepper and mix well. Simmer over medium-low heat for 30 minutes or until the liquid is thick and syrupy, stirring a few times. Transfer to a jar and let cool. Cover and refrigerate. The chutney will keep for 3 days in the refrigerator. Let sit out at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving.
For Serving: When ready to serve, transfer the chutney to a shallow bowl. Garnish with the diced apple. Serve with the cheese and baguette.
In a small pot, bring all the ingredients, except for the persimmons, to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes or until the liquid starts to become syrupy.

Add the persimmons and continue cooking for 5 minutes. Transfer to airtight containers. Let cool and refrigerate for 2 hours before serving. The chutney will keep for 1 month in the refrigerator, and in sterilized Mason-style jars, for 1 year at room temperature.
Delicious served cold with charcuterie and cheese, or warm with meat pie or turkey.

In a saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion and garlic in the oil until the onion is translucent. Season with salt and pepper. Add the broth, sugar, and 500 ml (2 cups) of cranberries. Bring to a boil and simmer gently for about 15 minutes.
Add the remaining cranberries and cook for 10 minutes. Let cool. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled. Adjust the seasoning.

In a small pot over medium heat, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes or until the fruits are translucent and the cooking liquid is thick and syrupy. Transfer to an airtight container and let cool. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, cook the bacon until crispy. Drain the bacon on paper towels. Set aside. Pour the bacon fat into a glass bowl. Once cool, compost the bacon fat.

In the same skillet over medium heat, soften the onion and thyme in the oil. Season generously with pepper. Cook for 10 minutes or until the onion is nicely caramelized, stirring often. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute longer.

Deglaze the skillet with the water and vinegar while stirring. Add the dates, honey and vanilla. Bring to a boil. Simmer over low heat for 10 minutes or until the dates have broken down and the liquid has been almost completely absorbed. Add the bacon and cook for another 5 minutes. Adjust the seasoning. Transfer into a bowl and let cool. Refrigerate for 1 hour or until the chutney is completely chilled.
Serve the chutney with a selection of cheese and cold cuts. Serve with the crackers. The chutney will keep for 1 week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

In a saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add the vinegar, water, sugar and fruit. Bring to a boil and simmer gently until the liquid is syrupy, about 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and add the vanilla. Let cool, then refrigerate.
Delicious with fine cheese and bread.

In a saucepan, brown the onions in the butter. Season with salt and pepper. Add the remaining ingredients, except for the sea buckthorn berries. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes. Add the berries and cook for 5 minutes or until the fruit is cooked and the liquid is syrupy. Adjust the seasoning.

Pour the chutney in an airtight container or into hot sterilized jars. The chutney will keep for about three weeks in the refrigerator. Freeze or sterilize the jars filled in boiling water for 15 minutes to ensure long storage at room temperature.
In a pot off the heat, combine all of the ingredients except for the brown sugar. Bring to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes or until the apples and onions are tender.
Add the brown sugar and mix well (see note). Continue to cook over medium-low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often. The chutney will start to thicken and the syrup will have reduced until almost dry.

Transfer to an airtight container and let cool. Cover and refrigerate. The apple chutney will keep for 1 month in the refrigerator or 3 months in the freezer. The chutney is great on a cheese or charcuterie board, in sandwiches or served as a topping for curry.
In a saucepan, combine the grapes, currants, ginger, vinegar, shallot and spices. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring until the grapes wilt and release their juice.

In a small bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in the water. Add to the grapes and continue cooking over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, or until the mixture thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool completely. The chutney will keep for 1 week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Delicious served with cheese and charcuteries on Mixed-Seed Crackers.
Place all ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer until syrupy, about 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Let cool completely. Serve with Meatless Tourtière with Chickpeas and Mushrooms.
In a skillet over medium heat, cook the shallots in the oil until lightly golden. Deglaze with the vinegar and brandy. Let the liquid reduce by half. Remove from the heat.

Add the remaining ingredients except the crackers. Season generously with salt and pepper and mix. Simmer over low heat, stirring often, until the liquid has almost completely evaporated and the shallots are meltingly soft, about 15 minutes. Transfer to an airtight glass container and let cool slightly. Cover and refrigerate for 3 hours before enjoying. The chutney keeps for 1 month in the refrigerator. Serve the chutney with crackers and as an accompaniment to a cheese platter.
Place all the ingredients in a blender and purée until smooth.
Delicious with curries (lamb, beef or lentil) or Tandoori Salmon. This chutney can also be used to flavour rice or yogurt.

In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Simmer over medium heat for 25 minutes or until the mixture is jammy and the cooking juices have reduced almost completely and are syrupy. Adjust the seasoning. Transfer to an airtight container and let cool. Cover and refrigerate. The chutney keeps for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
In a pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil while stirring. Simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Transfer to airtight containers. Let cool, then refrigerate. The rhubarb chutney will keep for 1 month in the refrigerator. You can also store the chutney in sterilized jars for 1 year at room temperature (see note).
Delicious served with beef, pork or grilled chicken.
Place a grill wok on the grill. Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the open area of the grate.

Place the onion, garlic, ginger and chili pepper in a bowl. Add 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the oil and season with salt and pepper. Transfer to the wok and cook for 6 minutes or until well grilled, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, place the tomatoes directly on the oiled grill and cook until well marked and starting to split, about 6 to 8 minutes, turning halfway through. Let cool, then peel.

In a pot over medium heat, toast the spices in the remaining oil. Add the tomatoes and break them up with a potato masher. Add the grilled onion mixture, fish sauce, sugar and lime juice. Let simmer for 30 minutes or until the chutney thickens.
Serve the grilled yellow tomato chutney warm or cold. It will keep for 1 week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
In a bowl, whisk together the orange zest, juice, mayonnaise, and Tabasco sauce.
Keep 60 ml (1/4 cup) of that mixture to spread on the rolls. Coat the salmon with the remaining sauce and let rest in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners on medium-high.
Grill the salmon for about 3 minutes per side. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the skin after cooking. Grill the outer surface of the rolls, then spread the inside with the orange mayonnaise.
Add the salmon. Top with the lettuce and onion.
Gremolata: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate.
Sandwich: Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high. Oil the grate.
Oil and roast the bell peppers, skin side down, until well blackened. Place the peppers in an airtight container. Let cool. Remove the skin. Set aside.
Brush the tuna, zucchini, and fennel with oil. Season with salt and pepper. Grill the vegetables on each side until tender. Keep warm, if necessary.
Grill the tuna on each side until the desired doneness. Drizzle the tuna and vegetables with the lemon juice.
Toast the roll insides. Rub the garlic clove on the toasted side.
Spread the mayonnaise inside the rolls. Place the tuna on the bottom rolls. Top with gremolata and the roasted vegetables.
Poolish: In a large bowl, combine the water, flour and yeast until smooth. Cover and let rise for 3 hours at room temperature or until doubled in volume (see note).

Dough: Pour the water into the bowl of poolish. Using your hand, break the poolish up in the water, pressing it between your fingers. Pieces of the poolish will float in the water. Add the flour and salt. Mix with your hand, pressing the dough between your fingers until the flour is completely moistened. The dough will be very soft and sticky. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes.

Keeping the dough in the bowl, with a moistened hand, stretch and fold the dough over itself. Repeat this step three times, turning the bowl a quarter turn between each fold. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
Filling: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season generously with pepper.

Spread the olive mixture over the dough. Still keeping the dough in the bowl, with a moistened hand, stretch and fold the dough over itself. Repeat this step three times, turning the bowl a quarter turn between each fold. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
With a moistened hand, repeat the previous step. Cover and let rise for 2 hours at room temperature or until the dough has more than doubled.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle the surface of the dough with flour. Turn the bowl out onto the baking sheet, flour-side down. Sprinkle the top of the dough with flour.

With lightly floured hands, gently stretch the dough into a large 15 x 7-inch (38 x 18 cm) rectangle. Let rise for 30 minutes or until the dough has puffed up slightly and bubbles are starting to form.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
Bake for 40 minutes or until the bread is nicely browned. Let cool completely on a wire rack before cutting into the bread (see note).
In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Let steep for 5 minutes.
Spoon into glasses.And put cinnamon sticks in them.
On a work surface, stick a clove into the peel of each orange cube. Place in the slow cooker. Add the remaining ingredients.
Cover and steep on low for 4 hours. It can be maintained on Warm for up to 12 hours.
Place the pink peppercorns in a tea filter bag or tie them up in a square of cheesecloth.
In a saucepan over low heat, combine the apple juice or cider with the cinnamon sticks, cloves and peppercorns. Heat for 10 minutes. Remove from heat and let steep for 5 minutes.
Remove the spices and peppercorns. Pour the cider into glasses and garnish with a slice of apple studded with a clove, if desired.
In a wine glass three-quarter filled with ice cubes, pour the ice cider.
Add the sparkling drink. Serve with the Apple and Cheese Bites.
Place a champagne flute in the freezer for 1 hour.
In the flute, combine the pear liqueur and the lemon juice. Top off the glass with the cold sparkling cider
Thread a cube of pear-flavoured pâte de fruit on a cocktail pick and set on the rim of the glass, if desired.
In a blender, purée the mango and orange juice until smooth. Strain through a sieve.
Place about 30 ml (2 tbsp) of mango purée in each of 8 champagne flutes. Slowly pour in the cider. Stir to combine. Serve immediately.
In a saucepan, bring the broth and barley to a boil. Cover and simmer gently for about 1 hour or until the barley is tender. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
With a knife, thin out the central stem at the base of each cabbage leaf.
In a large pot of salted boiling water, blanch the cabbage leaves until tender, about 5 minutes. Cool into ice water and drain. Set aside.

In a large skillet, brown the mushrooms, onion, and bell pepper in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add the zucchini and garlic and sauté for about 2 minutes. Deglaze with the wine and reduce until almost dry. Add the cooked barley. Adjust the seasoning. Cool and stir in the egg.
Spread 250 ml (1 cup) of tomato sauce at the bottom of a 33 x 23-cm (13 x 9-inch) baking dish. Set aside.

For each cabbage leaf, place about 125 ml (1/2 cup) of the barley mixture in the centre and close to thoroughly trap the mixture in the rolls. Place them side-by-side in the baking dish. Cover with the remaining sauce and sprinkle with the cheese. Cover with a sheet of aluminum foil and bake about 1 hour.
With a knife, pare down the central stem at the base of each cabbage leaf.
In a large pot of boiling salted water, blanch the cabbage leaves until they are tender, about 5 minutes. Plunge into ice water and drain. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).

In a large skillet, brown the onion and bacon in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add the garlic and sauté for about 1 minute. Allow to cool in a large bowl. Add the meat, rice, salt, mustard, thyme and 500 ml (2 cups) of tomato sauce. Season with pepper. Blend well with a wooden spoon or your hands. Set aside.
Spread the remaining tomato sauce and broth in the bottom of a 33 x 23-cm (13 x 9-inch) baking dish. Set aside.

Take a bit of stuffing and shape into a cigar shape. Place in the centre of a cabbage leaf, fold the sides toward the centre and roll. Put the cigars side by side in the baking dish. Add a slice of bacon on each roll. Cover with foil and bake for 1h30 to 2 hours until the cabbage becomes fork tender.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
In a bowl, combine the meat, onion, garlic, and spices. Season with salt and pepper.

Crumble half the meat mixture into a 33 x 23-cm (13 x 9-inch) baking dish. Sprinkle with half the rice and cover with half the tomatoes. Layer with half the cabbage and press gently. Add the remaining meat and rice in the same way. Cover with the remaining tomatoes. Layer with the remaining cabbage. Season with salt and pepper. Add the broth. Cover with a sheet of aluminum foil. Bake for 2 hours. Remove the foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Cut the lemon into 1/8-inch (3 mm) thick slices. Remove the seeds. Place in a small saucepan.
Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and let simmer for 2 minutes. Drain the lemon slices and set aside. Discard the cooking water.

In the same saucepan, bring the sugar, water and limoncello to a boil until the sugar has dissolved. Add the lemon slices and let simmer over medium heat for about 10 minutes or until tender and translucent. Let cool completely in the syrup. When ready to serve, drain the lemon slices.
Beautiful as garnish for Ricotta Cake.
In a measuring cup or small pitcher, combine the wine and lemon juice.
Divide the ice alternating with the lemon slices among four wine glasses. Top off the glasses with the Muscat lemonade.
Place the rack at the centre of the oven. Preheat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C). Layer a baking sheet with parchment paper.
On the baking sheet, mix the pumpkin with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Bake in the oven for 40 minutes or until the pumpkin is tender and golden. Add the remaining ingredients and serve.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 220 ºC (425 ºF). Butter and flour a 30 x 23-cm (12 x 9-inch) baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine all the ingredients except for the mango and cinnamon. Pour into the prepared dish and evenly place the mango on top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until the clafoutis has puffed up. Sprinkle with the cinnamon. Serve warm or at room temperature.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter a 10-inch (25 cm) quiche plate and generously sprinkle with sugar.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, sugar, vanilla and salt. Add the flour. Whisk in the cream and milk until smooth (see note). Pour into the quiche plate and top with the cherries.
Bake for 35 minutes or until golden. Let cool on a wire rack. Serve warm or at room temperature with vanilla ice cream or crème fraiche, if desired.
In a large pot, cook the vegetables in salted water until tender, about 30 to 40 minutes. Drain.
With a masher, coarsely crush the vegetables with the butter. Then, using an electric mixer, purée with the cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel the clementines, making sure to leave them whole.
On a work surface, remove the stems of the jalapeños. Save the jalapeños for another use. Place the jalapeño stems on the clementines. Perfect for decorating an autumn cheese board.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Oil a 20-cm (8-inch) square Pyrex baking dish.
Pour the beaten eggs into the dish. Season with salt and pepper. Bake until firm, about 10 minutes. Cut the omelet into quarters. Using a spatula, lift the pieces from the dish. Keep warm.
Meanwhile, dredge the eggplant slices in the flour. In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown on both sides in the oil. Set aside.

Toast 3 slices of bread for each sandwich. Spread a generous amount of hummus on 1 slice. Top with 1 piece of omelet and 1 eggplant slice. Top with another slice of bread. Spread with mustard to taste. Top with 2 tomato slices and 1 piece of lettuce and finish with 1 slice of bread spread generously on the underside with hummus. Secure with 4 toothpicks and cut into quarters.
Serve immediately.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the pancetta slices on the baking sheet. Bake until crisp, about 15 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Set aside.
Make the mayonnaise: In a bowl, whisk together the mustard, honey, garlic and egg yolk. Whisking constantly, add the oil in a thin stream. Season with salt and pepper.

For each sandwich, spread 1 bread slice with mayonnaise. Top with 2 slices of pancetta and tomato. Season with pepper. Top with 1 bread slice spread with mayonnaise. Top with duck and arugula and finish with 1 bread slice. Secure with 4 toothpicks and cut into quarters.
If you have time to make them, serve with Root Vegetable Fries.
Pesto mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise and pesto. Set aside.
Club Sandwich: Preheat the oven’s broiler.
In a skillet, brown the mushrooms in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Toast the bread slices on a baking sheet in the oven or toaster.

For each club sandwich, generously spread pesto mayonnaise onto three slices of bread. Top a slice of bread with a slice of tomato, a lettuce leaf and two slices of bacon. Cover with a second slice of bread and top with a quarter of the chicken and mushrooms and a slice of cheese. Close the sandwich with a third slice of bread, mayonnaise side down.
Layer the sandwiches and secure with the wooden skewers. Prick an olive on the skewer and serve straight up.
Olive Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Sandwich: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread the pancetta slices on the baking sheet. Bake for about 15 minutes or until crisp. Drain on paper towel. Set aside.

Spread the inside of the bread slices with olive mayonnaise. Layer the turkey and tomato on four slices of bread. Cover with a second slice of bread. Layer with lettuce and pancetta. Cover with the remaining bread. Insert four toothpicks in each sandwich and cut into quarters.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise, capers, lime juice and zest with a whisk. Season with pepper.
Cut the lobster into small pieces. Toast the bread and spread with the mayonnaise mixture.
Cut the lobster into small pieces. Toast the bread and spread with the mayonnaise mixture.
Serve immediately.

With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Line a 38 x 25-cm (15 x 10-inch) baking dish with a sheet of parchment paper, letting it hang over each side. Lightly oil the baking sheet and the sides of the baking dish.
Lay the bacon slices on the baking sheet. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes or until golden brown and crisp. Drain on paper paper. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine the eggs and 60 ml (1/4 cup) of the mayonnaise. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture into the baking dish and bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until slightly moist. Cut the omelet into six pieces. Set aside. Turn off oven and add the bacon to keep warm.

Assembly: Toast three slices of bread and spread with mayonnaise. On a slice of bread, place the egg and three slices of bacon. Cover with a second slice of bread. Lay three slices of tomato and two lettuce leaves. Finish with a third slice of bread. Insert a toothpick in the centre of each corner of the sandwich and cut into triangles. Repeat to prepare the other club sandwiches.

Lavender Whipped Cream: In a saucepan over medium heat, bring the blueberries, sugar and half the cream to a boil. Remove from the heat and add the lavender. Cover and let steep for about 5 minutes. Strain through a fine mesh sieve. Add the remaining cream. Cover and refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, about 2 hours. Add the lemon juice and whip until soft peaks form. Keep chilled.
Cobbler: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
In a 20-cm (8-inch) square cake pan, combine 250 ml (1 cup) sugar and the cornstarch. Add the blueberries and stir to combine. Set aside.

In a food processor, combine the flour, baking soda, salt and remaining sugar. Add the butter and pulse a few seconds at a time until the butter is the size of peas. Add the cream and lemon juice and pulse again until the dough becomes crumbly. Remove the dough from the food processor.
Spread the dough evenly over the blueberries. Sprinkle with large-crystal sugar.
Place the pan on the baking sheet (the sheet will catch any blueberry juices that boil over). Bake for about 70 minutes.
Serve warm or cold with lavender whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.
Fruits: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a 13 x 9-inch (33 x 23 cm) baking dish, combine the fruit, sugar and cornstarch. Bake for 30 minutes or until the fruit mixture is boiling and the cooking juices are thick and syrupy.

Dough: Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Add the butter and mix with your fingertips until it forms pea-sized pieces. Add the yogurt and mix just until the dough is moistened. Shape into a square with your hands.

On a floured work surface, roll the dough out to form a 9 x 6-inch (23 x 15 cm) rectangle, about 3/4 inch (2 cm) thick. Using a 2-inch (5 cm) round cookie cutter, cut out circles of dough. Reuse any dough scraps. Using a pastry brush, cover the circles of dough with milk and sprinkle with sugar.
Remove the baking dish from the oven. Cover the fruit with the circles of dough, letting them overlap slightly, as needed.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the dough is nicely browned. Let cool. Serve with ice cream, if desired.

Filling: In a saucepan, off the heat, combine fruit, sugar and cornstarch. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 2 minutes or until sugar has melted. Pour into a 20-cm (8-inch) square pan or a 2-litre (8-cup) soufflé dish. Set aside.
Dough: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F).
In a bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Add shortening and combine with a pastry blender or your fingers until it is the size of peas.
Add soy (or rice) milk and vanilla. With a wooden spoon, stir until flour is moistened, but texture is still lumpy. Spread dough over fruit with your hands. Sprinkle sugar over cobbler.
Place the baking dish on a baking sheet. This will contain overflowing juices.
Bake for about 50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the dough comes out clean. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Peaches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Place six 1-cup (250 ml) oven-safe jars or ramekins on a baking sheet.
In a bowl, combine the sugar, cornstarch and cinnamon. Stir in the peaches and lemon juice. Divide evenly among the jars or ramekins. Set aside.
Dough: In a small bowl, combine the cream and lemon juice. Set aside.

In another bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. With a pastry dough cutter or your hands, add the butter and mix until crumbly. Add the cream mixture and stir until the liquid is absorbed but the dough is still crumbly.
Place the dough in clumps over the fruit. Sprinkle with sugar if desired. Bake for about 35 minutes or until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Serve hot or warm.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F).

Filling: Combine the sugar and cornstarch in a square 20-cm (8-inch) baking pan or 2 litre (8 cup) soufflé dish. Add the fruit and ginger and toss well using a spatula. Place the pan on a baking sheet. Set aside.

Dough: In a food processor, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Add the butter and pulse until it has the size of peas. Add the buttermilk and pulse until the dough is crumbly.

Scatter the dough over the fruit with your hands and bake for about 1 hour or until the pastry is golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean. Serve warm or cold. If desired, serve with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

In a cocktail shaker, vigorously combine the ice cubes with the brandy, vermouth, lemon juice, cane syrup, sweet clover and foamer. Filter the mixture into a lowball whisky glass filled with ice cubes. Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Insert the apple slice into the cocktail, if desired.

In a lowball whisky glass filled halfway with ice, combine the cranberry juice, the white rum, the Amaro Siciliano and the almond liqueur. Add the raisins, the cranberries and the orange zest. Stir and serve with a cinnamon stick.
Spiced Syrup: In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat. Strain and let cool.

Cocktail: Cut the top off the pineapple. With a knife, cut around the inside of the pineapple, leaving about 1 cm (1/2 inch) of flesh, without piercing the skin. With a spoon, gradually scoop out the flesh to hollow the pineapple. Cut the flesh into pieces and discard the core.
In a blender, purée the pineapple pieces and water until smooth. Strain through a sieve. You will get about 250 ml (1 cup) of pineapple juice.
In a shaker, vigorously shake the pineapple juice, tequila, lime juice, spiced syrup and ice cubes. Pour into the hollowed-out pineapple. Serve with two straws and ice cubes.
In a shaker, vigorously shake the pineapple juice, whisky, cane syrup, lime juice, egg white, ginger, Angostura and ice cubes for 1 minute.

Fill a whisky glass (lowball) with ice cubes. Place pineapple slices against the side of the glass. Strain the cocktail into the glass through a small sieve. Using a small grater, garnish the glass with nutmeg and lime zest.
Syrup: Using a mortar and pestle, coarsely crush the peppercorns. Set aside in a bowl with the lime zest and basil leaves.
In a small pot, bring the water and sugar to a boil. Pour into the bowl of aromatics. Let cool. Cover and refrigerate for 8 hours.
Strain the syrup and pour into a glass jar. Add the lime juice. The syrup will keep for 1 week in an airtight jar in the refrigerator.
Cocktail: Divide the cold syrup and beer among four lowball whisky glasses. Garnish with the lime slices and basil leaves.
Place the ice cubes in a very cold lowball whisky glass. Add the beer, spruce soda, grapefruit syrup and lemon juice. Mix gently to combine. Garnish with the rosemary sprig.
In a shaker, muddle the raspberries with the mint leaves. Add the lime juice, cane syrup, Aperol and vodka.
Fill with ice cubes and shake vigorously. Strain and pour into two martini glasses. Add ice cubes and top with the tonic water.
Place the raspberries in a cocktail shaker. Add the cane syrup. Using a cocktail muddler, crush the raspberries to extract the juice.

Add the vodka, lime juice and ice cubes to the shaker. Mix vigorously for 1 minute. Strain through a small sieve into a tall glass or a wine glass. Top up with the sparkling water. Garnish with the cotton candy and add a straw. Before drinking, use the straw to stir the cotton candy into the cocktail until melted.
In a shaker, vigorously combine the juices, rum, ice and cinnamon. Strain and pour into martini glasses. Top off the glasses with the soda and garnish with the orange zest, if desired.
Divide the tonic water between two wine glasses or wide cocktail glasses.
In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix the remaining ingredients, except for the dried roses. Filter into the glasses.
Decorate each glass with some dried roses and a piece of grapefruit zest, first pressing it around the rim of the glass.
Lavender Syrup: In a small pot, bring the water and sugar to a boil until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat. Add the lavender flowers. Cover and let infuse for 15 minutes.

Strain the syrup through a sieve placed over a bowl, pressing on the flowers with the back of a ladle to extract as much liquid as possible. Compost the flowers. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour (see note).
Cocktail: Rub the rim of an old fashioned glass with the lemon zest. Place the large ice cube in the glass.

In a shaker, combine the amaretto, lemon juice, lavender syrup and foamer. Add the ice cubes, then shake vigorously. Strain into the glass. Garnish the rim of the glass with the lemon zest and a lavender stem.
In a small bowl, combine the gin and saffron. Let infuse for 20 minutes. Strain into a cocktail shaker and set the saffron pistils aside.
In a small glass bowl, heat the honey and lemon juice in the microwave oven for 30 seconds. Stir until the honey dissolves. Add an ice cube to cool the mixture.

In the cocktail shaker, vigorously mix the saffron-infused gin with the honey mixture, vermouth and ¾ cup (180 ml) of the ice cubes. Place the remaining ice cubes in a Boston Shaker glass. Strain the gin mixture into the glass. Top up with the sparkling water. Garnish with three of the reserved saffron pistils.
Thread the olives onto a cocktail pick and place in the glass.
In a blender, combine the grapefruit juice, rum, sugar, egg white half, and orange blossom water until frothy.
Immediately pour into four tall glasses and fill with tonic water, to taste. Garnish with rosemary sprigs.
In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix the ice cubes, liqueur, rum, milk and cinnamon. Strain into a 2/3-cup (150 ml) stemmed glass. Add frothed milk foam, if desired. Sprinkle with more cinnamon.

With a vegetable peeler or zester, remove 8 long zests from the lemon. In 8 champagne flutes, pour the juice and sparkling wine in equal parts. Add a twist of lemon on the rim of each glass. Serve cold.
In a cocktail shaker, combine the gin, orange juice, cane syrup, lemon juice and ice. Shake vigorously. Pour the mixture and some ice into two wine glasses.
Stir 4 cubes of orange gelée into each glass. Top up with the Champagne. Garnish with the remaining orange gelée cubes threaded onto a toothpick, if desired.
SHRIMP: In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil. Add salt. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring occasionally. Remove from the heat and drain. Let cool, then refrigerate for about 1 hour.
MANGO SAUCE: In the food processor, purée the mango, vinegar, sugar and horseradish. Add the lime zest. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour the sauce into a bowl and place it in the middle of a serving plate. Surround with the shrimp.

Steamed Shrimp: In the top part of a steaming pot, cook the shrimp, covered, for about 3 minutes or until they change colour. Transfer to a large bowl and refrigerate for about 30 minutes or until the shrimp have completely chilled. Shell the shrimp, keeping the tail on.
Cocktail Sauce: Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate, if necessary. Pour the sauce in your choice of glasses or bowls and place the shrimp around the rim.
Chili Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Grilled Shrimp: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
In a bowl, toss the shrimp with the olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Grill the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes on each side, or until cooked through.
Place the shrimp on a serving plate and serve with the chili mayonnaise.

In a saucepan, bring 250 ml (1 cup) of water and the sugar to boil, stirring until the sugar has dissolved. Pour into a pitcher. Add the water, lemon juice, rum, lychee and syrup. Refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight.
Serve with ice.
In a small measuring cup with a spout, combine the citrus liqueur and crème de cassis.

When ready to serve, place the crushed ice in a 1 ½-cup (375 ml) transparent glass. Slide the lemon slice between the ice and the side of the glass. Add the tonic water and lemon juice. Pour in the citrus liqueur mixture to create the effect of a total eclipse. Stir before drinking.
Rosemary Sugar: On a small plate, combine the sugar and rosemary. Rub the rim of a lowball whisky glass with the lemon wedge. Coat the rim of the glass with the rosemary sugar. Set aside.

Cocktail: Place 1 sprig of rosemary in a cocktail shaker. Add the vermouth, gin, lemon juice and maple syrup. Using a cocktail muddler, crush the rosemary slightly to extract the flavour. Shake vigorously.

Fill the prepared glass with finely crushed ice cubes. Place the remaining rosemary sprig and a stick of maple taffy in the glass. At the last moment, strain the cocktail through a small sieve into the glass.
On a work surface, cut 1 round slice of grapefruit from one of the grapefruit halves. Juice the remaining grapefruit to obtain ¼ cup (60 ml) of juice.
Cut the grapefruit slice into 4 pieces and place on a baking sheet. Sprinkle with sugar. Quickly caramelize using a culinary torch or under the broiler. Let cool.
In a blender, finely crush the ice with the grapefruit juice and the remaining ingredients until frothy. Pour into two martini or margarita glasses. Garnish with the caramelized grapefruit pieces.

Cucumber Juice: In a blender, purée the cucumber until smooth. Place a fine sieve over a bowl and pour in the cucumber purée. Cover and let drain, without pressing on the pulp, for 1 hour in the refrigerator. Compost the pulp. Save the juice. You should obtain about ¾ cup (180 ml) cucumber juice (see note).
Cocktail: Place the ice in a tall, cold glass. Add the cucumber juice, gin, lime juice and cane syrup. Mix. Top off with the tonic water. Garnish with the mint and cucumber slices, if desired.
In a blender, purée the ice cubes with the diced apple, apple brandy, maple sugar and verjus until smooth.
Pour into a glass. Garnish with apple slices. Serve with Sweet and Salty Popcorn with Herbs.
Cassis Granita: In a flat airtight container of about 2 litres (8 cups), combine the water and crème de cassis. Cover and place in the freezer for 6 hours or until completely frozen.
Place 4 coupe glasses in the freezer 1 hour before serving.
Cocktail: In a small pitcher, combine all the ingredients except the flowers.
Using a fork, scrape the surface of the granita to break it into crystals.
Divide the cocktail among the chilled glasses, then the cassis granita. Decorate with edible flowers, if desired.

In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix both types of rum, all of the juices, both types of syrup and the ice cubes. Strain the mixture into a large glass filled with crushed ice. Garnish with the orange slice and cherry.

In a cocktail shaker, muddle 2 orange slices with the handle of a wooden spoon. Add the Lillet, St-Germain, lemon juice and a few ice cubes. Shake vigorously. Filter into a lowball glass half-filled with ice. Top up with sparkling water and garnish with an orange slice.
In a strainer set over a bowl, drain the lychees. Set aside 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the syrup and 6 lychees. Reserve the remaining syrup and lychees for another use.
In a small pitcher, combine the lychee syrup, clementine juice, vodka, lemon juice and ginger. Strain the mixture into martini glasses. Top off each glass with the cider.
Thread the lychees onto small skewers. Decorate each glass with a lychee skewer and a slice of clementine.
In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix all of the ingredients until very frothy. Strain into Champagne coupes. Spoon the foam on top of the cocktails. Serve immediately.
In a large pitcher, combine the passion fruit syrup, vodka and lime juice. Set aside in the refrigerator.
When ready to serve, pour 75 ml (2 ½ oz) of the mixture and 45 ml (1 ½ oz) of tonic water into each glass. Garnish with 2 lime wedges and fill the glass with ice cubes.
Camomile Syrup: In a small pot, bring the water and sugar to a boil until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat. Add the camomile. Cover and let infuse for 30 minutes.

Strain the mixture through a sieve set over a bowl, pressing on the camomile with the back of a ladle to extract as much syrup as possible. Compost the camomile. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour. The syrup will keep for 1 month in an airtight container in the refrigerator (see note).
Cocktail: In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix the calvados, apple cider, lemon juice, camomile syrup, egg white, bitters and ice for 1 minute.
Strain into a glass filled with ice cubes. Decorate with a fan of apple slices and edible flowers threaded onto a cocktail skewer.
In a champagne flute, combine the vermouth, brandy and cider. Add the ice. Top off with the apple must and garnish with apple slices.

Plum Syrup: In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes. Strain through a sieve, pressing on the plums with the back of a ladle to extract as much juice as possible. Compost the residue. Let cool. Cover and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour. The syrup will keep for 3 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator (see note).
Cocktail: In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix the syrup, aquavit, lemon juice and ice cubes. Strain into a tall glass filled with crushed ice. Garnish with the plum wedges and lemon slices.
In a blender, purée the carrot with the rum, ginger syrup, triple sec and lemon juice until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve.
Pour into a whisky glass (lowball) filled with ice cubes. Garnish with carrot ribbons.
In a bowl, whip the cream, lemon zest and honey with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form. Refrigerate.
In a blender, purée the strawberries, apple juice, rum, sugar and lemon juice.
Place the crumbs on a plate.
Remove the glasses from the freezer. Moisten the rim of each glass with the lemon wedge and dip the rims in the crumbs.
Divide the cocktail among the glasses. Top with whipped cream and decorate with strawberry slices.
In a large pitcher, combine the orange juice, gin, cane syrup and 6 rosemary sprigs, lightly crushed. Marinate for 12 to 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Strain the mixture and discard the steeped rosemary sprigs.
When ready to serve, pour 90 ml (3 oz) of the mixture and 45 ml (1 ½ oz) of tonic water into each glass. Garnish with a rosemary sprig and fill the glass with ice cubes.

In a shaker, vigorously mix the ice cubes with the gin, syrup, triple sec and lemon juice for 30 seconds. Strain the mixture into a chilled lowball whisky glass. Add a few ice cubes and top off with the beer. Garnish with a large piece of orange zest (removed with a vegetable peeler).

In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix half of the ice cubes with the whisky, vermouth and Triple Sec. Strain into a stemmed glass over the remaining ice cubes. Add the ginger beer. Garnish with the thyme.

Jasmine Syrup: In a small pot, bring the water and sugar to a boil until the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat. Add the tea and let infuse for 5 minutes. Strain through a sieve and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour. The syrup will keep for 3 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator (see note).

Cocktails: In a cocktail shaker, vigorously mix the jasmine syrup, gin, lemon juice, cherry liqueur, cherry syrup and ice cubes. Strain into two very cold Champagne coupes. Add the tonic water. Garnish each coupe with a cherry threaded onto a cocktail skewer and a few flowers.
In a cocktail shaker, combine the strawberries, lemon and honey. Using a muddler, crush the fruit. Add the gin, thyme and ice cubes. Shake vigorously.
Place the large ice cube in a lowball whisky glass. Strain the cocktail into the glass. Decorate with thyme sprigs and strawberry slices.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a large skillet over medium heat, soften the peppers and onions in 3 tbsp (45 ml) oil until they begin to brown. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute while stirring. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside in a bowl.
On a plate, dredge the lamb in flour, shaking off any excess.
In the same skillet, brown the lamb in the remaining oil. Set aside on a plate.

Place half the potatoes in a large earthenware casserole or a large, deep baking dish. Sprinkle with rosemary. Place the meat on the potatoes then add the onion and pepper mixture. Cover with the remaining potatoes. Add the broth and wine. Sprinkle with cheese and breadcrumbs.
Cover and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes. Uncover and cook for 30 more minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
In a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, brown the pork shoulder on all sides in 1 tbsp of the butter. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.

Add the carrots, onion and celery to the pot. Continue to cook until the onion and celery are translucent. Sprinkle with the flour and mix to coat the vegetables well. Deglaze with the wine, scraping the bottom of the pot. Return the meat to the pot along with the broth, bay leaves and tomato. Bring to a boil. Cover and bake in the oven for 3 hours, turning the meat over halfway through cooking.
Remove the pot from the oven. Add the Morteau sausage to the pot. Cover and continue to bake for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the Toulouse sausages in the remaining butter.
Remove the pot from the oven. Flip the Morteau sausage over and add the Toulouse sausages (see note). Continue to bake, uncovered, for 30 minutes. Adjust the seasoning.
Remove the pork shoulder from the pot and place on a plate. Using a fork, shred the meat, removing any excess fat. Compost the fat.

On a work surface, slice the Morteau sausage. Return the sausage and shredded pork to the pot. Mix well to coat with the sauce. Sprinkle with the parsley. Serve with mashed potatoes or cooked white beans drizzled with lemon juice, if desired.
Line a 1 litre (4 cups) coeur à la crème hearth-shaped pierced mold with a layer of moist cheesecloth, letting it hang over the sides.
With a sharp knife, split the vanilla bean in half to open it and remove the seeds.
In a blender, purée the cheese, sugar, honey and vanilla seeds or extract until smooth. Pour into a bowl.

In a bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form. Set aside. With a spatula, fold the whipped cream and egg whites into the cheese mixture. Pour into the prepared mold. Fold the cheesecloth over the mixture.
Place the mold on a rack over a baking sheet to drain. Refrigerate for 24 hours.
Unmould onto a serving platter and serve with strawberry coulis. Ideally serve the same day.
