Salmon: In a bowl, combine the baking powder and Cajun spice mix. Coat the salmon cubes with the spice mixture. Add the oil and toss to coat the fish cubes.
Place the salmon cubes in the air fryer basket lined with parchment paper. Cook at 200 °C (400 °F) for 7 minutes for pink fish, or longer depending on the desired doneness.
Cajun Mayonnaise: Meanwhile, in another small bowl, whisk together all the ingredients. Set aside.
Sandwiches: In a large bowl, toss the cabbage and onion with the oil, vinegar and mustard. Season with salt.

Spread one side of the bread slices with the Cajun mayonnaise. Place the salmon cubes on half the bread slices. Top with the coleslaw. Close the sandwiches. Serve with chips or a green salad, if desired.

In a 9 x 5-inch (23 x 14 cm) glass dish, coat the salmon in the oil. Cover with plastic wrap. Cook in the microwave oven 1 minute at a time, for a total of about 2 minutes, or until the salmon is cooked. Refrigerate for 1 hour until completely cooled. Drain.
In a bowl, shred the salmon with a fork. Add the basil, mayonnaise, mustard and shallot. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.
Drizzle the avocado slices with the lime juice.
Spread the salmon filling on 4 slices of bread and top with the avocado. Close the sandwiches. Press down lightly to flatten them, trim the crusts if desired, and cut into 3 rectangles each.
On a work surface, split open the pitas to obtain 12 discs. For each sandwich, slightly overlap 2 pita discs.

Spread 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the garlic sauce over the lower third of the pitas. Garnish with sliced shawarma chicken, pickles and turnips. Fold the sides of the pitas in towards the centre and tightly roll up to seal in the filling.
In a large, lightly oiled grill pan over medium-high heat, lightly brown 3 sandwiches at a time on all sides. Cut the sandwiches in half, if desired. Serve immediately.
Coleslaw: In a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside until ready to serve.

Sandwiches: In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the tempeh strips in the oil for 2 minutes on each side. Season with salt and pepper. Reduce the heat to medium and add the barbecue sauce. Toss to coat the tempeh in sauce. Cook for 2 minutes, adding water as needed to prevent the sauce from sticking to the pan. Remove from the heat and sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Let cool for 5 minutes.

On a work surface, lay out the bread slices. Spread the mashed avocado over 4 slices of bread and barbecue sauce over the other 4 slices. Arrange the tempeh over the mashed avocado. Top with some coleslaw and a piece of bread. Serve with the remaining coleslaw and sweet potato fries, if desired.
In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise, feta and spicy bomba. Season lightly with salt and generously with pepper.
In another bowl, combine the tuna, shallot, lemon zest, lemon juice and olives with ¼ cup (60 ml) of the mayonnaise mixture. Adjust the seasoning.

Lay the toasted bread out on a work surface. Spread the remaining mayonnaise mixture over the bread. Divide the herbs between two pieces of bread. Top with the tuna salad and cucumber ribbons, rolling them up slightly. Season the cucumbers with salt and pepper. Close with the remaining slices of bread. Cut the sandwiches in half and serve immediately.
On a work surface, cut the block of tofu into 4 large slices. Pat the tofu slices very dry. Season with salt.
In a shallow dish, place the cornstarch. In a second shallow dish, combine the breadcrumbs, Parmesan and oregano.
Gently coat the tofu slices with the cornstarch.
Pour the oil into the same dish. Press the tofu into the oil to soak in the cornstarch. Press the tofu into the breadcrumb mixture to coat well on both sides.
Place the tofu in the basket of an air fryer. Cook for 20 minutes at 400°F (200°C).

Remove the basket from the air fryer. Flip the tofu slices over. Top with the tomato sauce, about 3 tbsp (45 ml) per slice. Sprinkle with the cheese. Continue to cook for 5 minutes or until the cheese is melted and golden.

Cover the inside of the kaiser rolls with the antipasto. Top the bottoms of the rolls with the tofu. Garnish with the arugula. Close the sandwiches with the tops of the rolls. Cut in half, if desired.
Tofu: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush a non-stick or parchment paper-lined baking sheet with the oil.

Place two layers of paper towels on a work surface. Place the tofu on the paper towels and cover with another two layers of paper towels. Press with your hands to absorb all of the water. Change the paper towels as needed. Cut the tofu into 16 slices.
Place the cornstarch on a plate. Dredge the tofu slices in the cornstarch and place them on the baking sheet. Bake for 20 minutes, flipping the slices over halfway through cooking.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven. Using a pastry brush, coat the tofu slices with the barbecue sauce on both sides. Continue baking for 10 minutes or until the sauce begins to caramelize slightly.
Coleslaw: Meanwhile, in a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Sandwiches: Cover the inside of the toasted buns with the barbecue sauce. Place 4 slices of tofu on each bun bottom. Top with the coleslaw. Close with the bun tops and serve immediately.
Tartare Sauce: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate.
Tofu: In a shallow bowl, combine the pickle juice and lemon zest. Season with salt. Set the marinade aside.

Place two layers of paper towels on a work surface. Place the tofu on the paper towels and cover with another two layers of paper towels. Press with your hands to absorb all of the water. Change the paper towels as needed.
Soak the tofu pieces in the marinade for 5 minutes on each side, turning them over gently (see note).
Preheat the oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (180°C). Place a wire rack over a baking sheet.
In a bowl, combine ¾ cup (115 g) of the flour with the cornstarch, salt and baking powder. Add the beer and whisk until the batter is smooth. Place the remaining flour in a shallow bowl.

Drain the tofu pieces from the marinade and dredge in the flour, gently shaking off any excess. Dip one piece of tofu at a time in the beer batter and coat well. Fry two pieces of tofu at a time for 5 minutes or until the batter is golden, shaking the fryer basket to prevent them from sticking to the bottom. Watch out for splattering. Remove the tofu from the fryer and drain on the wire rack. Season with salt.
Sandwiches: Cover the inside of the toasted buns with the tartare sauce. Top the bun bottoms with the fried tofu. Garnish with lettuce. Close with the bun tops and serve immediately.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the mayonnaise, lemon juice and garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Add the lettuce, arugula and antipasto or marinated eggplant. Mix well.

On a work surface, cut the buns in half horizontally without going all the way through to the other side. Open them like a book and place on the baking sheet. Place 2 slices of cheese on each bun. Bake for 3 minutes or until the cheese has melted.
Fill the buns with the meatballs and salad. Serve with chips, if desired.
Zucchini: Off the heat, pour oil into a deep skillet or saucepan to a depth of 2.5 cm (1 inch). Over medium-high heat, heat the oil to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a baking sheet with paper towels.
Fry the garlic slices in the hot oil for a few seconds. Using a slotted spoon, remove the garlic and drain it on the baking sheet.
In the same skillet, fry a few zucchini slices at a time until golden, about 4 minutes (see note). Watch out for splattering. Drain on the baking sheet with the garlic. Let cool.

In a bowl, combine the fried zucchini and garlic with the remaining ingredients. Salt and pepper. The marinated zucchini keeps for 5 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator. It's even better the next day (see note).
Sandwiches: On a work surface, cut the buns in half horizontally without going all the way through to the other side.

Spread the inside of the buns with the ricotta. Top the bottom halves of the buns with the arugula and mortadella slices. Top with the marinated zucchini, about 125 ml (1/2 cup) per sandwich. Close the sandwiches. Cut in half, if desired.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Brush the vegetables and slices of bread with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Grill on each side.
Generously spread the red bell pepper pesto on each slice of bread. Top with the grilled vegetables and zucchini blossoms. Close the sandwich.
Spread: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Sandwiches: Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
On a large plate or baking sheet, coat the vegetables with the oil. Season with salt and pepper.

On a work surface, cut two pieces from the baguette, each about 6 inches (15 cm) long. Save the rest of the bread for another use. Cut the pieces of baguette in half horizontally. Using a pastry brush, cover the inside of the bread with oil.

Grill the bell pepper wedges for 10 minutes or until tender and nicely browned, flipping them over halfway through. At the same time, grill the eggplant and zucchini slices for 6 minutes or until nicely browned, flipping them over halfway through. Grill the inside of the baguette pieces.

On a work surface, thinly slice the bell pepper. Cover the inside of the bread with the Parmesan spread. Top the bottom baguette pieces with the eggplant and zucchini. Sprinkle with fleur de sel. Add the bell pepper and basil leaves. Close the sandwiches. Cut in half. Serve immediately.

Place the eggs in a small pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Once boiling, cover the pot and remove from the heat. Let sit, covered, for 10 minutes. Remove the eggs from the water and plunge into very cold water to immediately stop the cooking. Peel the eggs.

In a large bowl, mash the eggs with a fork. Add 3 tbsp (45 ml) of the mayonnaise and continue to mash until the mixture is creamy. Add the celery and celery leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
In a bowl, combine the shrimp, tarragon and remaining mayonnaise. Let marinate for 5 minutes.
Open the rolls. Divide the lettuce, egg mixture and shrimp mixture between the sandwiches.
In a large bowl, coarsely crush the eggs with a fork. Add the mayonnaise and combine while crushing until creamy. Stir in the Parmesan cheese and green onion. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the egg mixture on half the bread slices and cover with the remaining slices. Cut each sandwich into 4 wedges.

Decoration: On one or two long serving dishes, place the sandwiches, side by side in a row as shown. Cover the two cut surfaces with a little mayonnaise. Sprinkle with fresh herbs, pressing gently on the sandwich.
Place the eggs in a pot and cover with warm water. Bring to a boil. Cover and remove from the heat. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Drain the eggs and fill the pot with cold water. Return the eggs to the pot and let cool for 15 minutes. Peel the eggs under cold running water and pat dry. Compost the shells.
On a work surface, cut the eggs in half. Remove the yolks and place in a bowl. Dice the egg whites.
Using a fork, mash the egg yolks. Add the egg whites, celery, dill, yogurt, pepperoncini peppers and brine, green onions, jalapeño, lemon zest and juice. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.

Cut the buns in half horizontally without going all the way through to the other side. Open the buns like a book and line the insides with lettuce leaves. Top with the chopped egg salad. Close the sandwiches.
Place the eggs in a bowl of warm water for 5 minutes to bring them to room temperature. Drain.

In a pot of simmering water, cook the eggs for 8 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove 3 eggs from the pot and plunge into a bowl of ice water. Cook the remaining eggs for 2 more minutes and plunge into a second bowl of ice water. Let cool for 15 minutes. Peel the eggs, rinse and pat dry, making sure to keep the two batches of eggs separated.
In another bowl, mash the 5 eggs that cooked for 10 minutes with a fork. Add the mayonnaise and chives. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut the 3 eggs that cooked for 8 minutes in half lengthwise.
Meanwhile, on a work surface, using a bread knife, remove the crust from the bread (see note). Cover the bread with a clean dishcloth until the eggs are ready.

Spread out half of the bread slices and cover with the smoked salmon, cutting the slices to fit, as needed. At the centre of each sandwich, place 1 tsp of the fish roe. Place 1 egg half, cut side down, over the fish roe. Cover the remaining bread slices with the mashed egg mixture. Close the sandwiches. Cut the sandwiches into two rectangles, making sure to cut through the egg lengthwise. Wipe down the knife between each cut.
Place the eggs in a pot and cover with warm water. Bring to a boil. Cover and remove from the heat. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Drain the eggs and fill the pot with cold water. Return the eggs to the pot and let cool for 15 minutes.
Peel the eggs under cold running water and pat dry. Compost the shells.
In a bowl, mash the eggs with a fork. Stir in the mayonnaise and chives. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, on a work surface, using a breadknife, remove the crusts from the bread (set aside for another use). Cover the bread with a clean dishcloth until the egg mixture is ready.

On the work surface, lay out half of the bread slices and cover with the cucumber slices. Top with the egg mixture and chips. Cover one side of the remaining bread slices with mayonnaise and place, mayonnaise-side down, over the sandwiches. Cut each sandwich in half or into quarters.

Eggs: Place the eggs in a pot and cover with warm water. Bring to a boil. Cover and remove from heat. Let sit for 10 minutes. Drain the eggs and fill the pot with cold water. Return the eggs to the pot and let cool for 15 minutes. Peel the eggs under cold running water and pat dry. Compost the shells.
In a bowl, mash the eggs with a fork. Add the remaining ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.

Sandwiches: On a work surface, cut off the crusts from the bread slices. Spread mayonnaise over the inside of the bread slices. Top half of the bread slices with the egg mixture. Garnish with the sliced radishes and close the sandwiches. Cut each sandwich into three equal parts. Thread the gherkins onto mini skewers and use to garnish each sandwich.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
Using your fingers, crumble the sausage meat over the baking sheet. Spread the onion out over the meat. Bake for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the spinach, oil and garlic. Season with salt and pepper.
On a work surface, cut the buns in half horizontally without going all the way through to the other side.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven. Cover the inside of the buns with the sausage mixture. Place the buns on the baking sheet. Divide the spinach mixture among the breads, pressing down lightly. Place 2 slices of cheese on each sandwich. Bake in the oven for 3 minutes or until the cheese is melted.
Top with the antipasto and close the sandwiches. Serve with green salad, if desired. Serve immediately.
Confit Tomatoes: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325ºF (165ºC). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine the tomatoes, oil, sugar and red pepper flakes. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the tomatoes out on the prepared baking sheet, cut-side up. Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes.

Remove the baking sheet from the oven. Using a fork, lightly crush the tomatoes to extract the juice. Continue to bake for 5 minutes or until the tomatoes are cooked and lightly browned. Let cool completely on the baking sheet, about 15 minutes.

Tonnato Sauce: Meanwhile, in a tall, narrow container (such as a measuring cup), combine all of the ingredients except for the oil. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Using a hand blender, purée the mixture until smooth. With the machine running, slowly drizzle in the oil (the sauce will begin to form a mayonnaise in less than 1 minute). Adjust the seasoning. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour to allow the sauce to set slightly.

Sandwiches: Lay the bread slices out on a work surface. Generously cover with the tonnato sauce. Divide the arugula among 4 pieces of bread. Top with the confit tomatoes and basil. Close the sandwiches with the remaining bread slices. Cut in half. Serve immediately or wrap individually.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 120 °C (250 °F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Combine Parmesan cheese and breadcrumbs in a shallow bowl. Place flour in a second bowl and egg in a third.
Season cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour and dip in beaten egg. Drain, then coat in Parmesan mixture. Shake to remove any excess.

In a non-stick skillet, brown two cutlets on both sides in half the oil until cooked. Set aside on the baking sheet. Top with mozzarella cheese. Melt in oven for about 10 minutes while you make sauce.

In the same skillet, brown onion in remaining oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add tomatoes. Bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes or until sauce thickens. Add parsley. Adjust seasoning.
Spread the inside of rolls with mayonnaise. Place cutlets on the bottom half and top with sauce. Cover with top half.

Spread the cake slices with a thin layer of peanut butter. Top four slices of cake with banana slices and top with the hazelnut spread. Cover with the other cake slices. Spread butter on each side of the sandwiches.
In a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat, brown the sandwiches for 2 minutes on each side or until golden brown. Serve immediately.
In a bowl, combine the tuna, mayonnaise and green onion. Season with pepper.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of each slice of bread.

On a slice of whole-wheat bread, spread some of the tuna mixture and garnish with olives. Cover with a slice of white bread. Layer the lettuce, tomato and egg. Finish with a slice of whole-wheat bread.
Cut the sandwiches diagonally into triangles and secure with toothpicks.
Dijonnaise: In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise and mustard.
Sandwiches: Spread the inside of the breads with dijonnaise. Cover with the ham, cheese, gherkins and pork slices. Close the sandwiches.
In a large ridged skillet or panini grill, grill the sandwiches over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing down with a spatula. Serve immediately.
Lemon Mayonnaise: In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Poivrer. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Sandwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Spread the potato waffles on a non-stick or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 15 minutes. Turn them over and continue baking for 5 to 10 minutes or until golden brown.

Meanwhile, in a large non-stick skillet over medium-low heat, cook the eggs in the butter on one side only for sunny-side up, or carefully turn them over and cook lightly on the other side, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Salt and pepper. Set aside.

Spread one side of 12 waffles with the lemon mayonnaise. Divide the lettuce, bacon and tomato slices among 4 waffles. Salt and pepper. Cover each with a second waffle. Top with the avocado slices and an egg. Close the sandwiches with the remaining waffles.
In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla and cinnamon.
On a work surface, spread the jam over 4 slices of bread and the peanut butter over the remaining 4 slices. Close the sandwiches.
Dip one sandwich at a time in the egg mixture, letting it soak in. Place the sandwiches on a plate while you prepare to cook them.

Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-low heat. Melt half of the butter in the skillet. Place two sandwiches at a time in the skillet and brown for 2 minutes on each side, flipping them over with a spatula. Keep the sandwiches warm on a baking sheet in an oven preheated to 200°F (95°C) while you cook the remaining sandwiches in the remaining butter, or serve them as you go. Serve with maple syrup.
Break 8 slices of bread into pieces. In a food processor, crumble bread by pulsing a few seconds at a time. Set aside in a bowl.
On a work surface, slightly flatten each slice of pork tenderloin with a meat mallet to get 1-cm (1/2-inch) thick slices. Set aside on a plate. Season with salt and pepper.
Place flour in a shallow bowl and eggs in a second bowl.
Preheat oil in the deep fryer to 180 °C (350 °F). Line a baking sheet with paper towels.
Dredge each slice of meat in flour and shake to remove any excess. Dip in beaten eggs and drain. Roll in breadcrumbs and press to coat well. Set aside.
Fry 2 slices at a time in oil for about 4 minutes or until meat is cooked. Drain on the baking sheet.

Dip each fried pork slice in Tonkatsu sauce and place between two slices of white sandwich bread. Remove crusts with a knife. Cut sandwiches into 3 equal rectangles and place on a plate, side by side, cut side up.
Chicken: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with foil.

In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, garlic, lemon zest and juice. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside ½ cup (125 ml) of the yogurt mixture in a small bowl and refrigerate until ready to assemble the sandwiches.
Add the oil, tomato paste and spices to the large bowl of yogurt. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. Add the chicken and toss well to coat.

Place the onion wedges on one side of the baking sheet. Toss with oil. Season with salt and pepper. Spread the chicken mixture out on the other side of the baking sheet. Bake for 20 minutes. Remove the baking sheet from the oven. Set the onion aside on a plate. Using a fork, shred the chicken on another plate. Return the chicken to the baking sheet.
Preheat the oven to broil. Bake the chicken until some pieces are crispy, about 5 to 6 minutes.

Sandwiches: On a work surface, open the pitas and gently separate the two sides to get a total of 8 discs. For each sandwich, place two pita halves on the work surface, overlapping them slightly. Cover with the reserved garlic yogurt. Top with the lettuce, tomato, chicken and onion. Firmly roll up without closing the extremities. Serve immediately.
Tofu: In a glass dish, combine the peppers, oil, honey, lime zest and juice. Add the tofu and coat well in the marinade. Cover. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Drain the tofu and set the marinade aside.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners to high. Oil the grate.
Grill the tofu for 2 minutes on each side. Toast the buns, if desired. Keep warm.
Toppings: In a bowl, combine the lettuce, radishes, green onions, cilantro, mayonnaise, lime juice and the reserved marinade. Season with salt and pepper.
Fill the burger buns with the tofu, some of the salad and the tomato. Serve with the remaining of the salad.
Tartare Sauce: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate.
Fish: Preheat the oil in a deep fryer to 350°F (180°C). Place a wire rack over a baking sheet.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Fill a bowl two-thirds of the way up with ice. Place a second bowl over the ice. This will keep the fish batter cold to ensure a very crispy coating.
In the second bowl, combine 3/4 cup (115 g) of the flour with the cornstarch, baking powder and salt. Whisk in the beer until the batter is smooth. Place the remaining flour in a shallow dish.
On a plate, season the fish with salt and pepper. Coat the fish with the flour, shaking off any excess.

Dip two pieces of fish at a time in the beer batter to coat well. Fry two pieces of fish at a time in the hot oil for 5 minutes or until the coating is nicely browned. Watch out for splattering. Place on the wire rack.
Place the hamburger buns on the wire rack beside the fish. Transfer the baking sheet to the oven for 5 minutes to continue to crisp up the fish coating and to toast the buns.
Assembly: Spread the tartare sauce over the inside of the toasted buns. Top the bun bottoms with the fried fish. Garnish with iceberg lettuce and pickles. Close with the bun tops. Serve immediately.

In a food processor, chop the cilantro, green onion and garlic. Add the shrimp, egg, soy sauce and sambal. Blend until coarsely puréed. Season with salt and pepper. Using a spatula, scrape down the sides of the food processor as needed.
Place the sesame seeds in a shallow bowl.

On a work surface (see note), spread the shrimp purée over the bread, using about 1/4 cup (60 ml) per slice. Working with one slice of bread at a time, press shrimp-side down into the sesame seeds. On the work surface, cut each slice of bread into 4 triangles.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium heat, warm the oil for 5 minutes. Brown half of the bread triangles at a time in the oil, sesame-side down, for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip over and continue to cook until the bread is golden, about 1 minute. Drain on a plate lined with paper towels. Serve with store-bought sweet chili sauce, if desired.
Tzatziki: Over a bowl, grate the cucumber and radishes on the large holes of a box grater. Add the lemon juice and salt. Mix and let stand for 10 minutes.

Drain the vegetables, squeezing them in a sieve or with your hands, and place them in another bowl. Add the remaining ingredients. Season with pepper and mix. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Cutlets: On a work surface, season the chicken with salt and pepper.
In a shallow dish, place the flour. In a second shallow dish, lightly beat the eggs. In a third shallow dish, combine the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds.

Dredge the cutlets in the flour. Shake to remove any excess. Dip into the beaten eggs, letting the excess drip off. Coat with the breadcrumbs, pressing on both sides. Freeze at this point, if desired (see notes).

In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook half the cutlets at a time in half the oil (30 ml/2 tbsp) for 4 minutes per side or until golden brown. Drain on a baking sheet lined with paper towels. Keep warm (in an oven preheated to 95 °C/200 °F).

Pickled Onion: Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the onion and lime juice. Season with salt. Cover with plastic wrap. Microwave for 30 seconds. Stir the onion and heat for another 30 seconds. Let cool slightly and drain when ready to serve.

Sandwiches: On a work surface, cut the focaccia in half horizontally. Spread the inside of the focaccia with the tzatziki. Arrange the chicken cutlets on the bottom half of the focaccia. Top with the cucumber rounds, pickled onions and lettuce. Close the sandwiches. Cut into four pieces. Serve immediately.
Lemon Butter Cookies: In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer. Add the egg yolk and lemon zest, beating until smooth. At low speed, or with a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients until smooth. Shape the dough into a disc and cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone mats.

On a lightly floured surface, roll out the dough into a 1/8-inch (3 mm) thick sheet. With a 2 ½-inch (6 cm) round cookie cutter, cut out 24 cookies. Reuse the scraps. Place on the prepared baking sheets and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Bake, one sheet at a time, for 10 to 12 minutes or until the cookies are lightly golden brown. Let cool completely.

Strawberry Parfait: In a saucepan off the heat, combine ½ cup (105 g) of the sugar and the cornstarch. Add the eggs and whisk thoroughly. Add the strawberry purée and lemon juice. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, scraping the sides and bottom of the saucepan until the mixture thickens. Let simmer for 1 minute. Transfer to a bowl. Cover and refrigerate for about 3 hours or until completely chilled.
In another bowl, whip the cream with the remaining sugar (¼ cup/55 g) until stiff peaks form. With a whisk, gently fold the whipped cream into the strawberry mixture.
Spoon the strawberry cream into a pastry bag fitted with a large star tip, and generously pipe onto half of the cookies. Top with the remaining cookies and press lightly. Freeze for about 4 hours.
Serve or individually cover the parfait sandwiches in plastic wrap.
Frozen Lemon Parfait: Line a 28 x 20-cm (11 x 8-inch) glass dish (with straight sides) with parchment paper, letting it hang over each side.

In a saucepan off the heat, combine 60 ml (¼ cup) of sugar and cornstarch. Add eggs and stir with a whisk until smooth. Stir in lemon juice and bring to a boil. Remove from heat and add butter. Stir until melted. Strain through a sieve over a large bowl and set aside.
In another bowl, beat egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining sugar (125 ml / ½ cup) and beat until sugar has dissolved and meringue forms stiff peaks.
Spoon meringue onto lemon cream and gently fold in with a spatula or whisk. Pour into prepared dish and freeze for 6 hours or until firm.
Lemon Cookies: In a bowl, combine flour and baking powder. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer. Add egg yolk and lemon zest and combine thoroughly. At low speed or with a wooden spoon, add dry ingredients and stir until smooth. Shape dough into a disc and cover in plastic wrap. Refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
On a floured work surface, roll out dough into a 3-mm- (1/8-inch-) thick square. Cut pastry to form straight edges. Cut into twelve 10-cm (4-inch) square cookies.
With a thin spatula, place cookies on baking sheet. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes or until they begin to brown. Let cool completely before handling.
Unmould parfait and cut into six squares. Place parfait slices between two cookies and cover individually in plastic wrap. Store in an airtight container in the freezer.

On a large cutting board, finely chop together the lettuce, meats, mozzarella and grilled bell peppers. Add the antipasto, mayonnaise, oregano, honey and vinegar. Chop again to thoroughly combine the ingredients.

On a work surface, cut the buns in half horizontally without going all the way through to the other side. Open them like a book and cover the insides with the chopped mixture. Cut the sandwiches in half. Serve immediately.
On a work surface, cut the mango lengthwise along the pit at the centre to get 2 slices. Set the slices aside. Remove any remaining flesh from around the pit and dice.
In a bowl, whisk the 35% cream, sugar and vanilla seeds with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form.

Spread the whipped cream over the 4 slices of bread. Place the mango slices diagonally over 2 slices of bread. Cover any empty spaces at the corners of the bread with the diced mango. Close the sandwiches.

Tightly cover the sandwiches with plastic wrap, keeping them facing the same direction as they were when you built them. Using a marker, trace a diagonal line along the length of the mango slices (follow the angle of the slices, avoiding any pieces of diced mango). Refrigerate for 2 hours.
On a work surface, cut the wrapped sandwiches along the marked line using a bread knife in a sawing motion. Unwrap the sandwiches. Serve immediately.
Rice: Rinse the rice under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well.

In a pot, bring the rice and water to a boil. Cover and cook over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes or until the water has been completely absorbed by the rice. Remove from the heat and let rest for 5 minutes, covered. Remove the lid and fluff the grains of rice with a fork (see note).
In a small bowl, combine the rice vinegar, sugar and salt until the sugar and salt have dissolved. Pour the mixture over the cooked rice and stir gently to coat well. Let cool.

Tofu: Meanwhile, on a work surface, cut the tofu in half lengthwise. Cut each half block of tofu in three widthwise to get a total of six 3-inch (7.5 cm) square slices. Place two layers of paper towels on the work surface. Place the tofu on the paper towels and cover with another two layers of paper towels. Press with your hands to absorb all of the water. Change the paper towels as needed. Season the tofu with salt.
Beat the egg in a shallow bowl. In a second shallow bowl, combine the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds.
Dip the tofu slices into the beaten egg, letting some of the excess drip off. Press into the breadcrumb mixture to coat well.

In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook half of the tofu slices at a time in the oil for 3 minutes on each side or until nicely browned. Add more oil as needed. Drain on a plate lined with paper towels.
Sandwiches: On a work surface, place a nori sheet matt-side up with one corner pointing down.
With slightly wet hands (see note), place ⅓ cup (75 ml) of the rice at the centre of the nori sheet, shaping it into a 3-inch (7.5 cm) square.
Top the rice with one-sixth of the spinach, and one-sixth of the cucumber and avocado slices. Cover with one slice of tofu. Top with another ⅓ cup (75 ml) rice, shaping it into a square.
Wet the corners of the nori sheet. Fold the four corners of the nori sheet over the rice to close into a sandwich. Repeat these steps with the remaining nori sheets, rice, vegetables and tofu.
Cut the sandwiches in half (see note). Sprinkle the cut-side of the sandwiches with sesame seeds. Serve with soy sauce, tamari sauce, katsu sauce or spicy mayonnaise, if desired.
Sandwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the slices of pancetta side by side on the baking sheet. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, or until crisp. Set aside on paper towels. Adjust the oven to broil.

In a pot of simmering salted water, add the vinegar. Crack the eggs one at a time in a saucer and slide each into the water as you go.Let poach for about 3 minutes or until the desired doneness. The yolks should be runny. Set the poached eggs on a plate to drain.

On the same baking sheet, without parchment paper, place the slices of bread. Broil. Turn the slices over. Sprinkle four with the cheese. Continue baking for about 5 minutes or until the cheese is golden brown and the bread is toasted.
Salad: In a bowl, whisk together the oil, vinegar and mustard. Add the lettuce and toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper.
Assembly: Layer the pancetta over the slices of cheese toast. Add the eggs and salad. Spread the mayonnaise on the remaining toast and close the sandwiches.
In a bowl, combine the flour and baking powder. Set aside.

In another bowl, cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer. Add the egg yolk and vanilla and beat until smooth. Using a wooden spoon, stir in the dry ingredients. Shape the dough into a disk. Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

On a floured surface, roll the dough to a thickness of about 3 mm (1/8 inch). Using a 6-cm (2 1/2-inch) round cookie cutter, cut out 18 cookies. Using a thin spatula, lift each cookie onto the baking sheet.
Bake until the cookies begin to colour, about 12 minutes. Let cool completely on the cookie sheet before handling.

For each sandwich cookie, spread 15 ml (1 tablespoon) dulce de leche on the underside of a cookie. Top with a cookie. Spread with dulce de leche. Top with a third cookie, underside facing down. Spread dulce de leche around the sides of the sandwich and roll in the coconut. Repeat with the remaining ingredients. Store at room temperature.
Soft Ginger Cookies: In a bowl, combine the flour, baking soda and salt.

In another bowl, cream the butter, brown sugar, sugar, molasses, oil, fresh ginger, vanilla and spices with an electric mixer. Add the egg and mix until smooth. With the machine running on low speed, stir in the dry ingredients.

Using a 2-tbsp (30 ml) ice cream scoop, shape the dough into 24 balls and place on a baking sheet lined with a silicone mat or parchment paper. Refrigerate for 2 hours or freeze at this point, if desired (see notes).
Ginger Sugar: Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the sugar and ground ginger. Set aside.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line two baking sheets with silicone mats or parchment paper.
Roll the cookies in the ginger sugar. Place 8 cookies on each baking sheet, evenly spaced out. Press the cookies down slightly.

Bake one sheet at a time for 9 to 10 minutes or until the cookies are cooked on the outside but still soft at the centre, rotating the baking sheet halfway through cooking. Let cool completely on the baking sheet, about 1 hour.
Cream Cheese Filling: In a bowl, cream the cream cheese and butter with an electric mixer. With the machine running, gradually add the icing sugar and mix until smooth and creamy.

Using a 2-tbsp (30 ml) ice cream scoop, cover the bottom of half of the cookies with the cream cheese filling. Close the sandwiches with the remaining cookies, pressing down lightly. The sandwich cookies will keep for 3 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Let sit out at room temperature before serving.
Spread the inside of the baguette with mustard. Drizzle with olive oil.
Garnish the bottom half with the mortadella, pear and bocconcini.
Close the sandwich. Wrap twine around the baguette at approximately 1 ½-inch (4 cm) intervals to make 10 small sandwiches. Slice the bread between the pieces of twine.
Parmesan Oil: Preheat the pizza oven on high (3) with the door closed for 20 minutes.
In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Sandwiches: On a floured work surface, roll out one ball of pizza dough at a time into a 10-inch (25 cm) circle. Remove any excess flour. Place the dough on a lightly floured pizza peel.
Using a brush, spread some of the Parmesan oil over the dough. Fold the dough in half and place it on a lightly floured pizza peel.
Using the pizza peel, slide one pizza at a time onto the hot stone. Bake in the pizza oven for 2 to 3 minutes, rotating the pizza 4 or 5 times during cooking, or until the crust is nicely browned.

Once out of the oven, on a work surface, unfold the dough without breaking it. Spread more Parmesan oil. Fill each pizza sandwich with ricotta, pistachios, lemon zest, mortadella and arugula. Close the sandwich. Cut in two and serve.
Cashew Spread: In a small pot, cover the cashews with the water. Bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and let soak for 15 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water.

In a blender, purée the soaked cashews with the remaining ingredients, except for the chives, until smooth. Add a little water, as needed. Season with pepper. Transfer to a bowl and stir in the chives. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Sandwiches: Meanwhile, with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Lightly brush the bread slices with oil and place on a baking sheet. Bake for 6 minutes or until lightly browned.
In a bowl, delicately toss the tomato slices with the oil, vinegar and Tabasco. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the cashew mixture over the toasted bread. Top with the arugula, tomato slices and bell pepper strips.

In a saucepan of salted simmering water, add the vinegar. Break the eggs into four saucers. Slide the eggs into the water and poach for about 3 minutes or until the desired doneness. Normally, the yolk should still be runny. Place the poached eggs on paper towels. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the oil, lemon juice, and garlic. Add the lamb's lettuce, radishes and toss to coat. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the bread slices on four plates. Spread with the mustard. Top with the prosciutto slices, lamb's lettuce, and eggs. Serve immediately.
Breaded Shrimp: In a shallow dish, place the flour. In a second shallow dish, lightly beat the egg. In a third shallow dish, place the crumbled cereal.

Season the shrimp with salt and pepper. Working one at a time, dredge the shrimp in the flour, shaking off any excess. Dip into the beaten egg, letting some of the excess drip off. Press into the cereal to coat well.
Place the shrimp evenly spaced out in the basket of an air fryer. Cook for 6 minutes at 350°F (180°C), flipping them over halfway through cooking.
Sauce: Meanwhile, in a bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Set aside.
Sandwiches: Spread the insides of the buns with the sauce. Top with the lettuce, tomato, pickles and shrimp. Serve immediately.
In a bowl, combine the cream cheese, mayonnaise, and lemon juice until smooth. Add the chives and capers. Season with pepper. Set aside.

With a rolling pin, lightly press the bread slices and spread with the cheese mixture. Top with the salmon slices in a single layer and roll tightly. Cover each cylinder with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes or until ready to serve. Cut each roll into eight slices.
In a large bowl, mash the eggs with a fork. Add the mayonnaise and stir, while mashing, until the mixture is creamy. Add the pickles and green onions. Season with salt and pepper and mix thoroughly.

With a rolling pin, slightly flatten the bread slices. Spread the egg salad on the bread slices. Trim the crust. Place an asparagus spear at the bottom of the short side of each bread slice. Roll firmly to secure the asparagus in the middle of each roll. Cover the sandwiches in plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 15 minutes or overnight.
When ready to serve, remove the plastic wrap and cut each roll into ½-inch (1 cm) slices to obtain 5 to 6 small sandwiches per roll.
Using a vegetable peeler, cut the carrot into long ribbons. In a bowl, combine the carrot ribbons with the vinegar and sugar. Let sit for 5 minutes. Drain.

Cover one side of each bread slice with the mayonnaise. Drizzle with hoisin. Divide the chicken among 4 pieces of bread. Top with the cucumbers, carrot ribbons, jalapeño and cilantro. Close the sandwiches.
Tempeh: In a shallow bowl, combine the soy sauce, maple syrup, paprika and vinegar. Coat the tempeh slices in the marinade. Drain and set the marinade aside.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook the tempeh in the oil until nicely browned, about 5 minutes. Season with pepper. Flip the tempeh over and cook for 1 more minute. Add the reserved marinade and let reduce until almost dry.

Sandwiches: Cover the slices of bread with mayonnaise. Divide the lettuce, basil, avocados, tomatoes and tempeh among 4 slices of bread. Close the sandwiches with the remaining bread. Cut the sandwiches in half and serve immediately.
Pickled Vegetables: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Let marinate for 15 minutes. Drain.
Sandwiches: Meanwhile, on a work surface, cut off the ends of the baguettes. Save for another use. Slice each baguette in half crosswise, then cut each piece in half horizontally.

Butter the insides of the bread. Cover one side of each sandwich with the liver pâté and the other side with the mayonnaise. Top with slices of pork roast, pickled vegetables, cilantro and chili peppers. Close the sandwiches.
Sauce: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Set aside.
Ssndwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
Shape the sausage meat into 4 patties slightly wider than the hamburger buns. Lightly oil the patties.
In a large non-stick skillet over high heat, cook the sausage patties on each side until browned, about 6 minutes. Set aside on the baking sheet.
In the same skillet, cook the spinach in the sausage fat until wilted. Season with salt and pepper. Place the spinach over the sausage patties. Top with a slice of cheese. Clean out the skillet.
Place the buns beside the patties on the baking sheet, cut sides up. Bake everything for 2 to 3 minutes or until the buns are warm and the cheese is melted.

Meanwhile, in the clean skillet over medium heat, melt the butter. Crack the eggs into the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Season with salt and pepper.

Assembly: Spread the mayonnaise sauce over the inside of the buns. Top the bun bottoms with the lettuce, sausage patties and eggs. Sprinkle with the pickles, dill and shallot. Close with the bun tops.
Omelette: Place the rack in the middle position. Preheat the oven to 150 ˚C (300 ˚F). Butter a 28 x 20 cm (11 x 8 inch) glass baking dish.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the salt. Add the water and mix well. Pour the egg mixture into the dish.
Prepare a Water Bath: Place the dish in a large glass baking dish. Pour cold water into the large baking dish to come 1 cm (1/2 inch) up the side of the smaller dish (see note).
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until the eggs are just set. Remove from the oven. Remove the pan from the water bath. Let cool on a wire rack.
Cut the omelette into 6 squares. Refrigerate the omelette squares at this point, if desired (see note).

Sandwiches: For each sandwich, on a work surface, spread the inside of an English muffin with mayonnaise. Top with an omelette square and a slice of cheese. Add toppings of your choice. Serve immediately.
Sandwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

On a non-stick or parchment paper-lined baking sheet, toss the vegetables with the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Arrange the vegetables on one side of the baking sheet. Arrange the bacon on the other side of the baking sheet. Bake for 15 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and the bacon is crispy. Pat the vegetables and bacon dry with paper towels, as needed. Set aside.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, whisk the eggs with 1 tsp of the curry powder. Season with salt and pepper.

In a 10 ½-inch (27 cm) crepe pan over medium heat, melt one-quarter of the butter. Pour in one-quarter (½ cup/125 ml) of the egg mixture. Cook until the surface of the omelette is still slightly runny. Place 1 slice of cheese at the centre of the omelette. Fold two opposite sides of the omelette over the cheese, then fold over the other two sides to form a square. Set aside on a plate. Repeat with the remaining butter, egg mixture and cheese.
In the same pan, toast the inside of the hamburger buns.
Assembly: In a bowl, combine the mayonnaise and remaining curry powder.
Spread the curry mayonnaise over the insides of the hamburger buns. Top the bun bottoms with the ham, omelettes, vegetables, bacon and arugula. Close with the bun tops.
Barbecue Mushrooms: In a microwave-safe bowl, combine the ketchup, molasses and chili powder. Cook in the microwave oven for 30 seconds or until the sauce is hot and glossy (see note).

In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the mushrooms in the butter. Add 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the barbecue sauce and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the mushrooms are caramelized. Set aside on a plate. Clean out the skillet.
Sandwiches: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In the clean skillet over medium-high heat, toast the inside of the hamburger buns. Set aside. Wipe out the skillet.

In the clean skillet over medium-high heat, melt the butter. Add the eggs. Season with salt and pepper. Stir slowly with a spatula or wooden spoon, scraping the bottom and sides of the skillet, just until the eggs have coagulated but are still slightly wet, about 3 minutes.

In the skillet, divide the eggs into 4 patties the same diameter as the hamburger buns. Place 1 slice of cheese over each portion of egg. Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 2 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the eggs have firmed up.

Assembly: Spread the mayonnaise and remaining barbecue sauce over the inside of the hamburger buns. Top the bun bottoms with the remaining cheese. Top with the mushrooms and eggs. Garnish with the lettuce and tomato. Sprinkle with the green onion and cilantro. Drizzle with lime juice. Close with the bun tops.
In a large pitcher, combine all the ingredients except for the soda and ice cubes. Cover and refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours for the flavours to blend.
Just before serving, add the soda and ice cubes. Serve very cold.

In a 10-cup (2.5 litre) pitcher, combine the wine, elderflower liqueur, lemon juice and lemon rounds. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour. When ready to serve, add the club soda and ice cubes. Mix well and serve.

In a saucepan, combine the sugar, zest and juice. Bring to a boil. Remove from the heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Pour into a pitcher and refrigerate for about 2 hours. Strain if desired.
Just before serving, add the mineral water to the citrus syrup.
Put 3 ice cubes in each of 6 highball glasses. Partially fill the glasses with the syrup mixture, then top off with red wine, pouring gently to create two distinct layers. Stir before drinking.
In a pot, bring the orange juice, orange slices, lemon juice, sugar and cognac to a boil. Simmer for 1 minute. Remove from the heat and let cool.
In a large pitcher, combine the wine, peach, apple and cinnamon sticks with the cooled orange syrup. Cover and let marinate overnight in the refrigerator.
Strain the sangria through a sieve placed over a large measuring cup or pitcher, if desired. When ready to serve, add more fresh fruit and ice cubes.
In a pitcher, combine all the ingredients except the tonic water and ice cubes. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Add the tonic and ice just before serving. Garnish each glass with mint leaves.
In a large pitcher, combine the liquors and honey. Stir until the honey has dissolved.
Add the ice cubes, ginger ale and fruit.
In a large pitcher, combine all of the ingredients except for the ice cubes. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
When ready to serve, add the ice cubes and mix well. Serve very cold.
In a large 12-cup (3 litre) bowl, lightly crush the peaches with a potato masher. Add the remaining ingredients, except for the ice. Mix and cover. Refrigerate for 4 hours.
Place a sieve over a pitcher and strain in the sangria. Add a few fresh peach wedges. Serve in glasses filled with ice cubes.
In a pitcher, combine all of the ingredients. Serve in glasses. Garnish each glass with a cocktail pick threaded with a slice of orange and a cherry.
In a large jar or glass pitcher, combine clementines, lemon, cranberry, anise, cloves, cinnamon, clementine juice, cranberry juice and vodka. Cover and refrigerate for 24 hours.
When ready to serve, add wine, soda and ice cubes.
In a pitcher, combine all the ingredients except the soft drink and ice cubes. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Add the soft drink and ice just before serving.

Rhubarb and Strawberry Syrup: In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil and simmer for about 3 minutes, stirring frequently. Strain and keep only the syrup. Let cool and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 1 hour.
Sangria: In a pitcher, combine the rhubarb and strawberry syrup, rosé wine, soft drink, fruit, and ice cubes. Serve very cold.
In a pitcher, combine all the ingredients except the ginger ale and ice cubes. Refrigerate for 1 hour. Add the ginger ale and ice just before serving.

In a bowl and using a muddler, coarsely crush half the rambutans, star fruit and pineapple with the sugar and lime zest. Add the lime juice, mango juice and rum. Cover and let macerate for at least 4 hours or overnight in the refrigerator. Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher. Add the white wine and remaining fruits.
Just before serving, add sparkling water and ice cubes if desired.

Work with the fish while still frozen (they will be easier to manipulate). To remove the scales, gently run the back of a knife along the skin under cold running water, making sure to keep it intact. Pat dry with paper towels.

Using scissors, remove the fins, then place the sardines flat on a work surface. Cut off the heads with a breadknife. Remove the fillets by cutting along the body, following the backbone. Gut each fillet and rinse, if needed. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, lightly brown the sardines, daisy capers, garlic and pepper flakes in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the sardines and set aside on a plate.

Add the tomatoes to the skillet and crush using a wooden spoon. Bring to a boil, cover with a splatter screen and simmer for 30 minutes or until the sauce has thickened. Return the sardines to the skillet. Adjust the seasoning.
Sprinkle with the fresh herbs and serve with Fresh Semolina Pasta, boiled potatoes or fresh bread.
In a saucepan, bring the cream, butter and corn syrup to a boil. Remove the saucepan from the heat. Whisk in the chocolate. Refrigerate. Serve warm.

In a tall, narrow container (such as a measuring cup), combine the garlic, egg whites, lemon juice and salt. Using a hand blender , purée the ingredients until smooth. With the machine running, slowly drizzle in 1 cup (250 ml) of the oil. The emulsion will begin to form a mayonnaise in less than 1 minute. With the machine still running, add the water alternating with the remaining oil. The sauce will keep for 1 week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

In a saucepan off the heat, combine the maple syrup, cream and cornstarch with a whisk. Bring to a boil while stirring and simmer for 30 seconds. Cool slightly and spoon over the sliced Maple Cake Baked in the Can.
In a small food processor, combine all the ingredients and purée until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a bowl and refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a food processor, purée the cilantro, green onions, garlic, chili pepper, ginger and cumin.
Transfer to a bowl. Add the oil, water, lime juice and tomato. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve with lentil and squash curry or butter chicken.
In a blender, purée all of the ingredients into a fairly smooth paste.
Transfer to an airtight container. The zhoug will keep for 3 days in the refrigerator. Delicious served with white fish or with our corncob papillote with spice butter.

In a small pot, combine all of the ingredients and bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Add pepper to taste. Let simmer for 5 minutes. The mustard-based sauce will keep for 10 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
In a saucepan, bring all ingredients to a boil. Simmer for about 8 minutes or until sauce is very syrupy.
Remove garlic and ginger. You should be left with about 125 ml (½ cup) of sauce. Let cool. Keep in the refrigerator, if needed.
Place the tomatoes into a bowl and crush them with your hands.
In a pot over medium-high heat, soften the garlic in the oil. Add the tomatoes, basil and oregano. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, covering with a splatter screen, as needed.

In a large pot over medium-high heat, soften the onion in the oil. Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until nicely browned. Season with salt and pepper. Add the garlic and sausage. Cook for 2 minutes while stirring. Add the tomatoes, oregano and bay leaf. Mix well. Bring to a boil. Simmer over low heat for 1 hour or until the sauce thickens. Adjust the seasoning.
In a large bowl, with your hands, thoroughly combine the pork, wine, spices, salt and half the garlic. Season with pepper.
In a large non-stick skillet, cook one-quarter of the pork at a time in 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the oil, crumbling the meat with the back of a spoon, until golden brown and well-cooked. Set aside.
In a food processor, finely chop, one vegetable at a time, the celery, onions, carrots, bell peppers, zucchini and mushrooms.
In a very large pot over medium heat, soften the vegetables in ¼ cup (60 ml) of the oil for about 30 minutes or until the liquid has evaporated.

Meanwhile, in a skillet, cook the remaining garlic in the remaining oil (1 tbsp/15 ml) for 1 minute. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Transfer to the pot with the vegetables. Add the tomatoes, tomato juice, oregano, bay leaves and cooked meat. Bring to a boil and let simmer for 2 hours and 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the bread crumbs and continue cooking for 30 minutes. Adjust the seasoning (see note).
Processing in a Pressure Canner: Meanwhile, prepare the jars and lids in the pressure canner.
Spoon the sauce into the hot jars, leaving 1 inch (2.5 cm) of space at the top. Remove air bubbles with a non-metallic utensil and wipe the rim of the jar with a clean cloth.
Centre the lids (discs) on the jars and screw the rings down until the point of resistance, then tighten another eighth-turn, without forcing.

Place the jars upright on the support rack in the pressure canner. When all the jars are in the canner, add water up to the level recommended by the manufacturer. Lock the cover and let ventilate (let steam escape from the vent hose) over medium-high heat for 10 minutes. Then close the vent according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Bring the pressure to 10 lb (69 kPa), then adjust the heat to maintain pressure. Process for 1 hour and 10 minutes over medium heat from the moment the pressure is reached. When the processing time is up, remove the pot from the heat and let the pressure drop by itself before unlocking and removing the cover.
Remove the jars from the water.
In a large saucepan, brown the meat in 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of the oil, half at a time, with the red pepper flakes. Add oil, if needed. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside in a bowl.
In the same saucepan, soften the onions, carrots, celery, and garlic in the remaining oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute over high heat.

Add the meat, tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, oregano, and cloves. Bring to a boil and simmer gently, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan regularly, for about 3 hours or until it thickens. Serve over the pasta of your choice.
Preheat the pressure cooker on the Sauté function for 2 minutes. Brown the beef in 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the oil, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside in a bowl.
Brown the sausage meat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Add the onions, carrots, celery, garlic and the remaining 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the oil and cook for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, oregano, celery salt, clove and ground beef. Mix well, then add the tomato paste without stirring. Cover and select the Meat function. Set the machine to cook for 25 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally (about 15 minutes), and remove the lid. Mix well to combine. Adjust the seasoning. Remove and compost the clove. Serve with your favourite pasta.
With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C).

In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook the meat in 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the oil, breaking it up with a wooden spoon until browned. Season with salt, pepper and the dried herbs. Stir well. Set aside.

Meanwhile, in an ovenproof saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion and carrot in the remaining oil (1 tbsp / 15 ml). Sprinkle with the flour and cook for 2 minutes while stirring. Add the broth and tomato paste. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Add the cooked ground meat to the sauce and stir in the garlic.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes. Remove from the oven. Adjust the seasoning. Let cool.
Serve with pasta or transfer into a 4-cup (1 litre) jar and refrigerate. The sauce will keep for up to 3 days in the refrigerator.
In a large saucepan, brown the sausage meat in the oil, crumbling it with a wooden spoon. Set aside in a bowl.
In the same saucepan, soften the onions, carrots, celery, and garlic. Add oil, if needed. Season with salt and pepper. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute over high heat.

Place the sausage back in the saucepan and add the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer gently, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan regularly, for about 3 hours and 30 minutes or until the rib meat falls easily from the bone.
Remove the ribs from the sauce and let cool on a plate. Remove the bones from the ribs and put the meat back in the sauce. Adjust the seasoning. Let cool and freeze.
In a large non-stick skillet over high heat, brown the mushrooms, onion and garlic in the oil. Transfer to the slow cooker.
Add the vegetables, lentils, tomato sauce and broth. Season with salt and pepper and mix thoroughly. Cover and cook on Low for 6 hours. It can be maintained on Warm for up to 8 hours.
Delicious over pasta, but also with stuffed eggplant or baked potatoes.

In a large pot over medium heat, cook the garlic in the oil until golden, about 5 minutes. Add the onions, celery and carrot. Cook for 5 minutes to soften the vegetables. Add the wine and bring to a boil. Let reduce by half.

Add the mushrooms and vegetable protein. Cook for 2 minutes while stirring. Add the remaining ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium low heat for 2 hours, stirring regularly. Remove the bay leaf. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve the sauce with cooked spaghetti or another pasta of your choice. Sprinkle with our vegan Parmesan and drizzle with olive oil, if desired.
Place the dried mushrooms in a bowl. Cover with the hot water and let soak for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Strain the mushrooms through a fine sieve placed over a bowl, pressing down with the back of a ladle to extract as much water as possible. Set the soaking water aside for the sauce.
Meanwhile, in a food processor, chop the carrots, celery and onion.
In a large pot over medium heat, soften the chopped vegetable mixture in the oil, about 6 minutes.
In a food processor, chop half of the white mushrooms at a time. Set aside in a bowl. Chop the rehydrated mushrooms.
Add all of the mushrooms to the pot of vegetables. Cook for 10 minutes or until any liquid from the mushrooms has completely evaporated. Add more oil as needed. Season with salt and pepper.

Add the tomato paste, miso, soy sauce, red pepper flakes and garlic to the pot. Continue to cook for 2 minutes while stirring. Add the mushroom soaking water, tomatoes and bay leaves. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 30 minutes or until the sauce thickens, stirring occasionally. Adjust the seasoning. Remove and compost the bay leaves.
In bowl, combine the orange juice, vinegar, ketchup and cornstarch.

In a pot, bring the sugar and water to a boil. Cook without stirring until golden. Remove from the heat and add the orange juice mixture. Return to the heat and bring to a boil. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the mixture is smooth. Let cool. Cover and refrigerate.
Serve with chicken nuggets, if desired.
In a small saucepan off the heat, blend the vinegar and cornstarch. Add the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper. Allow to cool.
In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool.

In a personal blender fitted with the grinding blade, purée the mixture until smooth. Transfer to a small bowl and let cool completely. The sauce will keep for 1 week in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth.
Transfer to a small pot and, over medium-high heat, bring the mixture to a boil. Simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently. Transfer the sauce to a bowl. Let cool.

In a small pot over medium heat, bring the vinegar, brown sugar, pickling spice and garlic to a boil. Remove from heat and let the flavours infuse for 5 minutes. Add the mango purée. Place the pot back over medium heat and simmer for 2 minutes or until the sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Strain through a sieve. The amba sauce will keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
In a bowl, combine all the ingredients.
In a saucepan, soften the shallot in the butter. Season with salt and pepper. Deglaze with the wine. Add the cream and the broth and bring to a boil.
Remove from the heat, add the cheese and whisk until melted. Return to the burner if necessary, but do not boil. Add the tarragon and adjust the seasoning.

In a saucepan, bring the sugar and half the water to a boil. Cook for several minutes until the sugar become golden brown. Remove from the heat. Add the remaining water and corn syrup. Bring to a boil. Add the cream and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring continuously. Set aside at room temperature in an airtight container.

In a heavy saucepan, bring the sugar, brown sugar, corn syrup, and the Scotch to a boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Attach a candy thermometer in the centre of the pan and simmer over medium heat without stirring until the thermometer reads 121 °C (250 °F).
Remove the saucepan from the heat and gradually stir in the cream. Stir in the butter and vanilla, whisking until the sauce is smooth. Let cool. Store in an airtight container at room temperature.

In a saucepan over medium heat, bring the milk, cream and corn syrup to a boil. Remove from the heat and add the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. With a whisk, stir until the chocolate is melted. Add the butter in the same way. Serve at room temperature, or refrigerate and reheat just before serving. Outstanding with cake or Dessert Maki.
In a saucepan off the heat, combine cocoa powder and sugar. Add water and corn syrup and bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Simmer for 10 seconds.
Remove from the heat and add chocolate. Stir until smooth. Pour into a container and let cool.
This sauce can be served warm or cold over ice cream, waffles, pancakes and Chocolate Pavlova.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature.
In a small glass bowl, combine the chocolate and water.
Microwave for 30 seconds or until the chocolate has almost completely melted (a few pieces may remain). Stir until the sauce is smooth.
Serve right away, as the sauce sets quickly.
Place the chocolate in a bowl.
In a small saucepan, bring the creams to a boil. Pour the hot liquid over the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. Whisk the chocolate until the sauce is smooth. Add the cinnamon and stir. Let cool.
Serve the Baileys chocolate sauce with gluten-free cinnamon doughnuts, pancakes, waffles or simply ice cream.
Place the chocolate in a bowl.

In a small saucepan, bring the cream to a boil. Pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Let melt for 2 minutes. Whisk the chocolate until the sauce is smooth. Add the spices and stir. Let cool slightly.
If desired, serve the spicy chocolate sauce with the churros or simply with ice cream.

In a large saucepan over high heat, sauté the crab shells, onion and garlic in 2 tbsp of the butter for 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute while stirring. Deglaze with the Worcestershire sauce, wine, veal broth and 1 cup (250 ml) of the chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Strain the sauce through a sieve and into a small saucepan. Compost the crab shells and the aromatics.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, dissolve the corn starch in the remaining ¼ cup (60 ml) of chicken broth.
Whisk the corn starch mixture into the sauce. Bring to a boil and reduce the sauce for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat. Whisk in the remaining ¼ cup (55 g) of butter.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, brown the meat and onion in the butter. Add the spices and cook for 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Deglaze with the beer. Transfer to the slow cooker.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix thoroughly. Cover and cook on Low for 2 hours. It can be maintained on Warm for up to 2 hours.
Stir well before serving directly from the slow cooker. Serve with corn chips.
In a small bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in the milk.

In a small pot over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the flour and chili powder and cook for 1 minute, stirring with a whisk. Add the milk mixture while whisking. Bring to a boil over medium heat, whisking constantly. Add the cheese and mix until melted. Adjust the seasoning.
This recipe doubles easily. You can make it in advance and store it for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Warm over low heat before serving.

In a small pot, combine all of the ingredients and bring to a boil, stirring with a whisk. Add pepper to taste. Let simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. The honey bourbon sauce will keep for 10 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

Dissolve the cornstarch in the beef broth. In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil, stirring constantly with a whisk. Simmer for about 5 minutes or until the sauce is syrupy. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve with a steak.

Add 500 ml (2 cups) of cooked and diced chicken meat and 250 ml (1 cup) of frozen peas to your béchamel. Continue cooking for 3 to 4 minutes or until the peas are tender. Adjust the seasoning. Pour the sauce into the toasted bread cups, letting it overflow on each side.
In bowl, blend all the ingredients with a whisk.
In a large microwave-safe bowl or large measuring cup, combine brown sugar and cream with a fork.
Cook sauce for 3 minutes. Stir and continue cooking for 4 minutes. Let cool for about 15 minutes.
Serve over fruit (sliced apples or bananas, strawberries, pineapple, etc.), white cake or ice cream.
In a small pot, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Turn the heat to low and let simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pass the mixture through a sieve, using the back of a ladle to extract as much liquid as possible. The resulting sauce will be thick and smooth. Add water if needed.

In a skillet over medium heat, soften the shallot and garlic in the butter and honey. Deglaze with the wine and let reduce for 1 minute. Add the demi-glace, ground pepper and star anise. Simmer for 1 minute. Adjust the seasoning. Remove and compost the star anise. Serve with grilled steak, if desired.

In a pot over medium-high heat, brown the leek and onion in the butter. Add the wine and let reduce by half. Add the broth. Bring to a boil and simmer until reduced by three-quarters. Strain through a sieve, pressing firmly with the back of a ladle to extract all the flavours. Return the sauce to the pot and set aside.

In a small bowl, combine the cornstarch and water. Gradually pour the cornstarch mixture into the sauce, whisking constantly. Bring to a boil and simmer for 1 minute or until the sauce has thickened slightly. Season with salt and pepper.

In a saucepan over medium heat, soften the onion and carrot in the butter. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Add the wine and bring to a boil. Add the broth and molasses. Simmer for 10 minutes or until the sauce thickens slightly. Strain into a bowl and keep warm.
Meanwhile, in a skillet over high heat, brown the bacon until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Add the bacon and parsley to the sauce.
In a small bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in the water. Set aside.

In a skillet over medium-high heat, brown the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the broth, sherry and reserved drippings from the Turkey Roast, if desired. Bring to a boil and simmer over high heat for about 15 minutes or until the gravy reduces by half.

Drizzle in the cornstarch mixture, whisking continuously. Simmer for 1 minute or until the gravy thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with the Gluten-Free, Dairy-Free and Nut-Free Stuffed Turkey Roast with Sausage and Cranberry and mashed potatoes.
In a bowl, combine all the ingredients. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a bowl, blend all the ingredients with a whisk. Season with salt and pepper.
In a bowl, combine the cornstarch and water. Set aside.

Melt the butter in a saucepan and sauté the onion until golden. Add the vinegar and sugar and cook until the vinegar has evaporated. Add the broth. Bring to a boil and reduce by half. Add the cream and the cornstarch mixture. Return to a boil while whisking. Add the almonds and adjust the seasoning.
In a small saucepan, combine all the ingredients.
Bring to a boil while stirring with a whisk. Let simmer for about 2 minutes or until the sauce thickens slightly. Set aside.
The peanut sauce will keep for about 1 week in the refrigerator. Delicious with Crunchy Tofu Rolls, dumplings or pork.
In a saucepan, combine all the ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring frequently. Let cool. Store in the refrigerator.

In a saucepan, off the heat, combine the water, sugar, and cornstarch with a whisk. Add the blueberries. Place the pan on the stove over medium heat and stir with a wooden spoon until the sauce simmers. Let cook for about 1 minute.
Remove from the heat and let the sauce cool for about 30 minutes. You can keep the sauce in the refrigerator and reheat in the microwave oven, if needed.

In a saucepan, cook the zucchini, artichokes and olives in the oil for 2 minutes. Deglaze with the wine and reduce by half. Add the meatball sauce and basil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Serve over long pasta. Notes

MEATBALLS: In a bowl, blend the meat sausage, ground veal, breadcrumbs, egg and salt and pepper. Shape about 38 2.5-cm (1-inch) in diameter balls and dredge in flour. In a large saucepan, brown half of the meatballs in 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of oil. Remove from the pan as they brown and set aside. Cook the remaining meatballs.

SAUCE: In the same pan, brown the onion and garlic in the oil. Add the tomatoes and water. Bring to a boil. Add the meatballs and simmer for about 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Serve over long pasta.
SAUCE: In a large saucepan, cook the garlic in the oil for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and break with a wooden spoon, a potato masher or with your hands.
Add the tomato paste, water and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil and simmer for 45 minutes.
Cook the sausages in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain. Cut into 1-cm (1/2-inch) slices. Set aside.
MEATBALLS: In a bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in hot water for 2 minutes.
Drain by pressing in a colander.
Combine the drained bread with the remaining ingredients except for the oil. Form 45 ml (3 tablespoons) meatballs with the mixture. Place the meatballs on a baking sheet.
In a skillet, brown the meatballs, a dozen at a time, using 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of oil each time.
Add the cooked meatballs and sliced sausages to the sauce. Continue cooking for 1 h 15 minutes. Add the basil and cook an additional 15 minutes. Adjust the seasoning and serve over long pasta.

In a saucepan, bring the water, sugar and honey to a boil. Add the cranberries and return to a boil. Simmer over medium heat, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, cover and set aside for 15 minutes.
Serve warm or cold with turkey or pork.
Store in the refrigerator.
In a saucepan, bring all the ingredients to a boil and simmer until it as the consistency of jam, about 12 minutes. Refrigerate.
In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with pepper. Serve at room temperature.
Delicious with grilled meats, fish or pasta, such as our creamy ravioli raclette.
In a small food processor, purée all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve with the oysters.
Place all of the ingredients in a pot. Bring to a boil. Simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. Remove from the heat and let cool.

In a blender, purée the mixture until smooth. Strain the sauce through a sieve placed over a bowl. Compost the residue. The hot sauce will keep for 3 weeks in a bottle or airtight container in the refrigerator or for 3 months in the freezer.
In the bowl of a food processor, purée the beans until smooth. Strain. Set aside.
In a skillet, brown the bacon. Add the shallot, garlic, and pepper and cook until the shallot is golden brown. Add the bean purée. Bring to a boil and cook until the sauce thickens.
Serve with rice and cilantro. Delicious with Jeff Boudreault’s Mango Chicken.

In a skillet, soften the onion and garlic in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Add the peppers and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the wine and broth. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 3 minutes.
In a blender, purée until smooth. Add the basil. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve over pasta, white fish or boneless chicken breasts.

In a skillet, sauté the plums in the butter. Deglaze with port wine and vinegar. Add the broth, honey, and star anise. Simmer until the sauce is syrupy. Remove the star anise and adjust the seasoning. Serve with meat.
Prick the sausages with a fork and place in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes. Drain and let cool. Cut the sausages into 1-cm (1/2-inch) thick slices.
In a saucepan, brown the sausages in 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of oil. Set aside in a plate.
In the same pan, brown the onion, carrots and celery in the remaining oil. Add the tomatoes and sausages. Continue cooking for 10 minutes. Add the herbs and adjust the seasoning.
Serve over short pasta such as penne.
Make a small crisscross incision at the base of the tomatoes. In a pot of boiling water, blanch the tomatoes for 30 seconds. Drain and cool in an ice bath. Peel and seed the tomatoes.
In food processor, purée the tomatoes with the garlic, then add the oil, pulsing so as to retain some texture.
In a pot, bring the tomato purée to a boil and simmer gently for 30 to 45 minutes or until the desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
In a saucepan, soften the celery and garlic in the oil.
Add the tomato sauce and olives. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Add the tuna and onion. Cook for 5 minutes. Adjust the seasoning.
Serve over long or short pasta.
Preheat the grill, setting the burners on high.
In a large bowl, combine the tomatoes with 150 ml (2/3 cup) of the oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Place enough tomato pieces to completely cover the grate and grill for about 5 minutes per side. Remove from the grill and place on a baking sheet. Let cool.
Grill this way the remaining tomatoes, then remove the peel with your fingers and press them gently to remove the seeds. Set aside in a bowl.
Coarsely crush the tomatoes with your hands or using a potato masher.
In a large saucepan, soften the onion and garlic in the remaining oil. Add the peeled and seeded tomatoes and the bay leaves.
Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat for about 2 hours, stirring frequently. Season with salt and pepper. Add the basil.
Adjust the seasoning. Serve as is over pasta or with veal cutlets.
In a saucepan, soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil. Add the remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes. Purée in a blender until smooth.
In a saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Stir in the flour, chili powder and onion powder.
Add the remaining ingredients and bring to a boil, whisking continuously. Simmer for 1 minute. Remove from heat and let cool.
In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the flour and garlic and cook for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly with a whisk until the mixture is golden brown.
