With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, toss the chickpeas with the oil. Spread out on the baking sheet. Bake for 30 minutes or until the chickpeas are golden, stirring halfway through cooking. Return to the bowl.

Meanwhile, in a small pot off the heat, combine the butter, hot sauce, maple syrup, vinegar and cornstarch. Bring to a boil. Simmer over low heat for 3 minutes or until the sauce thickens. Pour over the chickpeas in the bowl and stir to coat well. Adjust the seasoning.
In another bowl, combine the lettuce, cheese shavings and dressing. Season with salt and pepper.

Lay the tortillas out on a work surface. Top with the chickpeas and salad. Fold the sides of each tortilla in towards the centre and tightly roll up to seal in the filling. Cut in half, if desired. Serve with vegetable crudités, if desired.

In a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, cook the chickpeas and onion in the oil until nicely browned, about 12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Add more oil as needed. Remove from the heat and let cool.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the sour cream, feta, mint, lemon zest, garlic and tomato. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Add the chickpea mixture and mix well. Adjust the seasoning.

On a work surface, lay out the tortillas. Divide the lettuce and the chickpea mixture among the tortillas. Fold the sides of the tortilla in towards the centre and tightly roll up from bottom to top to seal in the fillings. Serve with fresh vegetable crudités or a green salad, if desired.
Caesar Mayonnaise: In a bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients.

Wraps: On a work surface, lay out the tortillas. Spread with the Caesar mayonnaise. Cover with the lettuce, bacon, chicken and tomato. Season with salt and pepper. Roll tightly and wrap individually in parchment paper, sealing the ends. Cut in half.

Pork: In a large non-stick skillet over high heat, cook half of the pork at a time in the oil, breaking the meat up with a wooden spoon, until starting to brown, about 8 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, remove the pork from the skillet and place in a bowl. Set aside.
In the same skillet, cook the mushrooms in the pork cooking fat until nicely browned and slightly crispy. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute while stirring.
Return the meat to the skillet. Add the remaining ingredients and mix well. Continue to cook just until the sauce is thick and syrupy. Adjust the seasoning.
To Serve: Place the meat mixture, lettuce, green onions, carrot, cilantro, peanuts and sambal at the centre of the table. Let everyone garnish their own lettuce leaves with the toppings.
Crispy Tofu: Place the tofu in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with the cornstarch and toss to coat well. Add both types of oil. Mix well.
Spread the tofu mixture out in the basket of an air fryer. Cook for 15 minutes at 400°F (200°C). Stir and continue to cook for 5 minutes or until the tofu is golden and crispy.

Sauce: In a large non-stick skillet, bring all of the ingredients to a boil. Add the tofu and continue to cook until the sauce is thick and syrupy, stirring to coat the tofu well with the sauce. Transfer to a serving bowl.

To Serve: Place the tofu, lettuce, vermicelli, peanuts, green onions, cucumbers and carrot at the centre of the table. Let everyone around the table garnish their own lettuce leaves. Serve with lime wedges and the dipping sauce of your choice.
Sauce: In a bowl, whisk together all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.
Wraps: Place the veggie pâté, radishes, cucumbers and carrots in the lettuce leaves. Drizzle with the sauce.
Sour Cream: In a bowl, combine the sour cream and curry powder. Season with salt. Set aside.
Dressing: In a large bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt.
Wraps: Add the nectarines, cabbage, snow peas, carrots, radishes and green onion to the bowl of dressing. Mix well. Adjust the seasoning.
Place the sour cream mixture, nectarine salad, shrimp and lettuce leaves at the centre of the table. Let everyone around the table build their own wraps.
Chicken Filling: In a bowl, combine all of the ingredients. Season with salt and pepper.

Wraps: On a work surface, lay out the tortillas. Cover with mayonnaise. Divide the spinach, chicken filling and apple among the tortillas. Fold the two opposite sides of each tortilla in towards the centre, then roll up from the bottom towards the top around the filling. Cut in half, if desired.
Tofu: In a bowl, whisk together the cornstarch, tamari, honey, lime juice, curry powder and onion powder. Season with salt and pepper. Add the tofu and mix to coat in the sauce.
In a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, heat the oil. Spread the tofu and sauce out in the skillet. Brown the tofu on all sides, about 5 minutes. Spread out on a plate and let cool (see note).

Salad: Meanwhile, in another bowl, combine the cabbage and lime juice. Season with salt. Let sit for 15 minutes. Drain and discard any excess liquid. Add the mayonnaise and Sriracha to the cabbage. Add the apple. Season with pepper and mix well.

Assembly: On a work surface, lay out the tortillas. Using a fork, mash an avocado half at the centre of each tortilla. Drizzle lightly with lime juice. Season with salt and pepper. Divide the coleslaw and tofu among the tortillas. Fold the two opposite sides of each tortilla in towards the centre, then roll up from the bottom towards the top around the filling. Cover with parchment paper or plastic wrap.
With the rack in the highest position, preheat the oven’s broiler. Line two baking sheet with aluminum foil. Place a wire rack on a baking sheet.
Insert two cubes of pork tenderloin alternating two green onion pieces at one end of 16 skewers. Spread on the rack of the first baking sheet. Brush with oil.

To thread pork belly slices on remaining skewers, place them flat on a work surface and insert the skewer along its entire length, holding it in place with one hand. Spread over the second baking sheet. Brush with oil.

Broil tenderloin skewers for 5 minutes. With a brush, baste skewers with glazing sauce. Continue broiling for 2 minutes. Baste and broil skewers again for about 1 minute or until meat is cooked and glazed. At serving time, baste again.
Cook pork belly skewers in the same way, but for a little less time because they brown faster. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and drizzle with a little lime juice before serving.
If desired, serve skewers with shichimi and Japanese pepper.
Place a small rack on a plate

With a skewer, gently enlarge the cherry cavities. Insert a blueberry, stalk side out, so it is flush with the opening of the cherry. Insert the cherry in the cavity of the lychee, letting it bulge slightly out of the fruit, Place on the rack and store in the freezer for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over the fruit syrup and let stand for 2 minutes. Heat the syrup in the microwave oven for about 1 minute or until the gelatin is well dissolved. Set aside in a bowl in the refrigerator for about 25 minutes. Remove the syrup from the refrigerator before it sets. Melt in the microwave oven for a few seconds, if necessary, and stir.
Brush the eyes with the cooled syrup and return to the freezer for 15 minutes. Brush again and refrigerate until serving.
Place all the ingredients in a blender and purée until smooth. If you are using raspberries or strawberries, you can strain the mixture through a sieve to remove all the seeds.
Pour the mixture into two tall glasses.
Combine all the ingredients.

Rhubarb and Strawberry Compote: In a pot, combine all of the ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes or until the fruits have broken down. Pour into a bowl and refrigerate until completely chilled, about 2 hours.
Assembly: Serve the yogurt in bowls. Top each serving with 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the rhubarb and strawberry compote (or more to taste) and the crumble.
In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, bring the orange juice, sugar, carrot and cardamom to a boil, stirring. Simmer for 5 minutes or until the jam is syrupy. Let cool completely.
Divide the jam among 6 airtight containers. Add the yogurt. Serve or refrigerate. The yogurt jars keep for 1 week in the refrigerator.
In a small glass bowl, gently heat the honey in the microwave oven for 15 seconds until runny. Add the rose water and cardamom. Mix well and let cool.
In a small food processor, purée three-quarters of the mango until smooth.

In a bowl, combine the honey mixture with the yogurt. Pour in the mango purée. Gently fold the purée in with a spatula to create a marbled effect. Carefully divide the yogurt mixture among two bowls. Top with the remaining diced mango and the raspberries. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
When ready to serve, garnish with the pistachios.
Place the chocolate in a bowl.
In a small pot, bring the milk and sugar to a boil, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved. Pour over the chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute without stirring.

Whisk the mixture until smooth. Gradually stir in the yogurt until well combined. Transfer to an airtight container. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight. The chocolate yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator. Stir the yogurt before serving.
In a bowl, whisk together all the ingredients until the sugar has dissolved.
Pour the mixture into the siphon. Close to seal. Screw the cartridge to release the gas into the siphon.

Shake the siphon several times upside down to allow the gas to properly distribute into the preparation. Keep the siphon vertically upside-down and gently press the lever to garnish a fruit salad (see recipe Citrus Salad with Gingerbread Syrup), pancakes or any other dessert.
Refrigerate until ready to serve. However, you must shake it again upside down before use.
In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth.
Pour the mixture into the ice cream maker and churn for 20 minutes or until the frozen yogurt has set.
Transfer to an airtight container and freeze for 5 hours or until firm. Let the frozen yogurt sit at room temperature for several minutes before serving, if needed.

In a small pot, bring the sugar, water, corn syrup and lemon zest to a boil. Simmer for 1 minute or until the sugar has completely dissolved. Let cool, then refrigerate for 1 hour or until completely chilled.
In a sieve set over a large bowl, strain the syrup. Compost the zest. Add the yogurt and mix well.
Pour the mixture into an ice cream maker. Churn for 20 minutes (or according to the manufacturer’s instructions), until the yogurt has set.
Transfer to an airtight container and freeze for 3 hours or until the yogurt is very firm. Let sit out at room temperature for a few minutes before serving, as needed.
Banana Yogurt: In a blender, purée all the ingredients until smooth. Set aside.
Raspberry Yogurt / Blueberry Yogurt: Repeat with the raspberry and blueberry yogurt mixtures. Strain the purée through a sieve.
Pour the mixtures alternately into Popsicle moulds. Insert the sticks. Freeze for 5 to 6 hours.
Place the strainer in the container of a yogurt maker.

In a bowl, combine the yogurt and maple syrup. Pour the mixture into the strainer. Cover and let strain in the refrigerator for 4 hours or until the mixture has reached the desired consistency. Discard the liquid. Transfer the yogurt to an airtight container. The maple Greek yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
Place the strainer in the container of a yogurt maker

Pour the yogurt into the strainer. Cover and let strain in the refrigerator for 4 hours or until the desired consistency is reached. Discard the liquid. Transfer the yogurt to an airtight container. The Greek yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
Spoon the yogurt into four cups or glasses and drizzle with the honey. Sprinkle with the pistachios and mango.
In a pot over medium heat, heat the milk and powdered milk, stirring constantly, until a thermometer reads 185°F (85°C). Remove from the heat.
Submerge the bottom of the pot in an ice bath and let the milk mixture cool to 110°F (45°C). Remove the pot from the water.

In a small bowl, combine ½ cup (125 ml) of the mixture with the yogurt starter. Pour into the remaining milk mixture still in the pot and strain into a yogurt maker (see note). Close the machine and let ferment at room temperature for 5 hours.

Place a fine sieve lined with a few layers of paper towel over a large bowl. Pour the yogurt into the sieve. Cover with plastic wrap and let strain for 4 hours in the refrigerator or until completely chilled. Discard any liquid. Transfer the yogurt to an airtight container.
The homemade Greek yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
Granola: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a large bowl, combine the oats and pecans.
In a small pot, melt the butter with the brown sugar, maple syrup and spices. Pour into the bowl with the oats and mix well. Spread out on the baking sheet.
Bake for 25 minutes, stirring three times during cooking. Let cool completely, about 1 hour. The granola will keep for 1 month in an airtight container at room temperature.

Confit Apples: Meanwhile, in a pot, bring the water, sugar and lemon juice to a boil just until the sugar has dissolved. Add the apples and simmer over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes or until tender and slightly translucent. Remove from the heat. Let sit for 15 minutes without stirring. Transfer into an airtight container and let cool. Cover and refrigerate. The apples will keep for 1 week.

Assembly: For each serving, when ready to serve, pour about 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the apple cooking syrup into the bottom of a glass or jar. Add 1/3 cup (75 ml) of the yogurt. Top with apples, apple cooking syrup and granola, to taste.
Granola: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together the oil, molasses, brown sugar and egg white. Add the oats and peanuts. Mix to coat the oats well. Spread out on the baking sheet.

Bake for 15 minutes. Gently flip the granola over. Bake for another 5 to 10 minutes or until the granola is caramelized. Let cool completely, about 1 hour. The granola should clump together in pieces of varying sizes. Break the larger pieces, as needed. The granola will keep for 1 month in an airtight container at room temperature.

Assembly: For each serving, when ready to serve, in a bowl, combine 1/3 cup (45 g) of the berries with 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the jam. Place some of this berry mixture at the bottom of a glass or jar. Add 1/3 cup (75 ml) of the yogurt. Top with the remaining berry mixture and granola, to taste.
Crunchy Granola: With the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper.

In a bowl, combine the yogurt, maple syrup, oil and cinnamon. Add the oats and mix well. Let sit for 5 minutes in order for the liquid to be soaked up by the oats. Spread the mixture out on the baking sheet.

Bake for 25 minutes. Gently flip the granola over. Bake for another 5 minutes or until the granola is nicely browned. Let cool completely, about 1 hour. The granola will keep for 1 month in an airtight container at room temperature.

Caramelized Pineapple: Meanwhile, in a small pot, bring the syrup to a boil. Simmer until light amber, about 4 minutes. Add the pineapple and cook until slightly tender and the syrup is slightly thickened, about 8 to 9 minutes. Transfer into a bowl and let cool. Cover and refrigerate. The caramelized pineapple will keep for 1 week.

Assembly: For each serving, when ready to serve, pour about 1 tbsp (15 ml) of the pineapple cooking syrup into the bottom of a glass or jar. Add 1/3 cup (75 ml) of the yogurt. Top with about 2 tbsp of the caramelized pineapple and granola, to taste.
In a pot, combine the milk and milk powder. Warm over medium heat, stirring, until a thermometer reads 185°F (85°C). Remove from the heat.
Let the mixture cool to 110°F (45°C). Stir in the yogurt. Pour the mixture into clean, warm glass jars. Cover the jars.

Place the jars in a baking dish. Fill the baking dish with hot (not boiling) water. Transfer to the oven. Turn on the oven light (the light will keep the oven at a temperature that promotes fermentation). Leave the jars in the oven until the yogurt is set, about 4 to 6 hours. Remove from the oven.
Remove the jars from the water and dry off with a clean dishcloth. Refrigerate the yogurt for 4 hours. The yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
In a pot over medium heat, warm the milk until just simmering, stirring a few times. Let sit at room temperature until the milk cools to 104°F (40°C), about 1 hour (see note).
Stir the yogurt starter into the milk. Pour the mixture into the container of a yogurt maker. Cover. Set the temperature to 108°F (42°C) and the fermentation time to 8 hours.
Refrigerate the yogurt for 4 hours or until completely chilled. The yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
In a pot over medium-high heat, bring the milk and milk powder to a boil, stirring constantly. Transfer to a bowl and let cool for 1 hour.

Add the yogurt starter and mix well. In a sieve set over a bowl, strain the mixture. Pour about 3/4 cup (180 ml) of the mixture into 1-cup (250 ml) sterilized glass jars (see note). Seal the jars and place in the pressure cooker. Add enough water to cover the jars halfway.
Cover and select the Yogurt function. Set the timer for 4 hours. Remove the jars from the water and dry with a clean cloth.
Refrigerate the yogurt for 4 hours. When ready to serve, garnish with fresh fruit, jam or granola, to taste. The yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
Pour the milk into the pressure cooker. Cover and select the Yogurt function. Set the machine to cook for 8 hours.
After 1 hour (the pressure cooker will beep after 1 hour of cooking), remove the lid. Using a spatula, stir in the yogurt starter. Cover and continue cooking for 7 hours.
Remove the lid. Transfer the yogurt into an airtight container. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours or until completely chilled. The yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

For Greek yogurt, line a large sieve with coffee filters and set it over a bowl. Pour the hot yogurt into the lined sieve. Cover with plastic wrap and let drain in the refrigerator for 4 hours or until completely chilled. Discard the liquid. Transfer the chilled yogurt to an airtight container. The Greek yogurt will keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.
In a bowl, combine the yogurt, grated cucumber and lime juice.
Top with the almonds, cucumber slices and a drizzle of oil. Sprinkle with fleur de sel and sumac, if desired. Serve immediately.
Preheat a pressure cooker on the Sauté function for 2 minutes. Brown half of the meat at a time in 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside on a plate.

In the pressure cooker, cook the onion and garlic in the beef cooking fat until translucent. Deglaze with the wine. Add the strained tomatoes, broth, sugar, tomato paste and spices. Return the meat to the pressure cooker. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. Cover and select the Meat function. Set the machine to cook for 35 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large pot of salted boiling water, cook the orzo until very al dente, about 3 minutes. Set aside 1 cup (250 ml) of the cooking water. Drain the pasta. Place in a bowl. Add the remaining oil and toss to coat the orzo well.

Let the pressure release manually. Once the pressure is released, remove the lid. Mix well. Remove and compost the bay leaf and cinnamon stick. Add the orzo and mix well. Let sit for 10 minutes to allow the orzo to cook through. Add the reserved pasta cooking water to thin out the sauce as needed. Adjust the seasoning.
